https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08503.title: Effects of climate change on hydrogeological hazard: the case of the Niscemi landslides (Southern Sicily, Italy)
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08503.abstract: Abstract This study analyzes precipitation variability and the hydrometeorological conditions associated with extreme hydrogeological events in the Niscemi area (southern Sicily), combining historical series (1885–2020), ERA5 data, and future projections of rainfall intensity. The comparison between the hydrogeological events of October 12, 1997, and January 26, 2026 highlights how such events can develop through different hydrometeorological configurations, yet are both preceded by high soil moisture conditions, confirming the key role of antecedent precipitation and its temporal distribution. The climatic analysis shows that cumulative precipitation does not exhibit a significant linear trend but is strongly modulated by Euro-Mediterranean atmospheric circulation, with significant negative correlations with EA (ρ = -0.74) and MOI (ρ = -0.66), and more moderate correlations with NAO and WeMO. In contrast, mean rainfall intensity shows an increasing trend over time and is only weakly correlated with the indices, with a significant relationship observed only with WeMO (ρ = -0.34). The intensification is also associated with synoptic configurations characterized by positive NAO. Projections obtained using a SARIMAX model, forced with SSP scenarios, indicate a progressive increase in rainfall intensity throughout the 21st century, reaching up to approximately 40% under high-emission scenarios. Overall, the results highlight that extreme hydrogeological events arise from the interaction between atmospheric circulation variability, thermodynamic conditions, and antecedent rainfall conditions, emphasizing the need for integrated approaches to risk assessment in a climate change context.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02481.title: Multi-scale modeling of continent-wide tracking data confirms the importance of landscape mosaics for the European wildcat
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02481.authors: María Alejandra Cuentas Romero, Julian Oeser, Matteo Luca Bastianelli et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02481.abstract: Abstract Context Land use change is a major threat to the persistence of wildlife in human-dominated landscapes, making the knowledge of the amount and spatial configuration of suitable habitat essential for conservation. The European wildcat ( Felis silvestris ) currently persists in fragmented populations and faces ever increasing human pressure. Objectives We modeled and mapped suitable wildcat habitats at the continental scale, to identify opportunities and constraints for its conservation. Methods We compiled a large telemetry dataset comprising 200 wildcats across Europe and developed multi-scale habitat suitability models using Maxent. Habitat selection was analyzed at two hierarchical levels: home-range placement within the wider landscape and selection within the established home ranges. Results At both levels, wildcats selected broadleaved forests, mixed forests, and grasslands, while avoiding landscapes dominated by large continuous forests. For home-range placement, they preferred lower terrain ruggedness and less intensive agriculture. Within the home ranges, wildcats selected forest edges and small woody features. Conclusions Our results highlight the importance of heterogeneous forest–grassland mosaics habitats. More than half of the predicted suitable habitat occurred outside protected areas, highlighting the need for effective conservation strategies beyond their borders. Predictions of suitable areas should, however, be interpreted cautiously in regions where environmental conditions extend beyond those represented in the calibration data. By providing the first continental-scale habitat suitability map based on a large European telemetry dataset, our study offers a spatial foundation for identifying conservation priorities and supporting the long-term connectivity and recovery of wildcat populations.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: A decision support framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration through process-based ecosystem modeling and optimization
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Vsevolod A. Bohaienko, Fasma Diele, Carmela Marangi et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Wetland restoration is increasingly recognized as a nature-based climate solution, but effective planning requires balancing nonlinear ecological responses with economic and implementation constraints. We propose a conceptual and computational framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration that embeds process-based ecosystem modeling within restoration optimization. Restoration strategies are represented as portfolios combining discrete intervention choices with continuous decisions on implementation intensity and spatial allocation. A vertically resolved ecohydrological model simulates soil organic carbon dynamics and decomposition-driven CO$_2$ and CH$_4$ emissions, allowing environmental outcomes to arise from the interaction between restoration decisions and ecosystem processes.The framework is illustrated through a benchmark analysis and an application to the Ebro Delta. The benchmark shows that alternative objective specifications select distinct interior and corner solutions from the same ecological trade-off. In the Ebro Delta application, imposing a budget constraint reallocates restored area from the deep-rooted vegetation type toward the less expensive shallow-rooted type, while maintaining high vegetation densities and compliance with the methane target, although the CO$_2$ target is exceeded. Global sensitivity analysis identifies the density and spatial allocation of the deep-rooted vegetation type as the main drivers of restoration performance.The results show that restoration outcomes depend not only on total vegetation cover but also on portfolio composition and implementation intensity. The proposed framework provides a flexible methodology for integrating process-based ecological models into restoration planning under alternative environmental objectives and resource constraints.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Maintenance matters: Insights from guidelines and practice on nature-based stormwater solutions
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Emma Girot, Ning Ding, Ivar Annus et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Nature-based stormwater solutions (NBSS) support urban stormwater management while providing additional ecosystem services. Their hybrid grey–green design sets them apart from conventional drainage systems requiring specific maintenance to ensure long-term performance. This study combines a global practitioner survey and a review of maintenance guidelines aiming to characterize shortcomings in NBSS management, focusing on failure mechanisms and maintenance practices. Based on 22 responses, survey results show that, in the absence of maintenance, systems are mainly affected by sediment buildup, litter, and green waste accumulation, as well as excessive vegetation growth, and invasive species. Maintenance (e.g., visual inspections, litter removal) is performed regularly, from monthly to annually, consistent with guidelines. Vegetation management typically follows a seasonal frequency (∼three months). Our review of 35 guidelines indicates that maintenance practices are very diverse and context-dependent, depending on the type of NBSS and socio-ecological-technological context, reflecting a potential barrier to mainstreaming of best practices. No universal maintenance frequency can be established as it strongly depends on NBBS and local context (e.g., climate, available resources). Systematic data collection on failures, their occurrence, and impacts is however essential to support predictive local maintenance strategy.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Bismuth-based photocatalysts for sustainable water remediation and solar hydrogen generation: State-of-the-art and future directions
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Lovedonia K. Kganyakgo, Daniel Masekela, Kwena Desmond Modibane
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: The rapid increase in environmental pollution and global energy demand has intensified the search for sustainable technologies capable of simultaneously addressing wastewater contamination and clean fuel generation. Photocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy because it utilizes solar energy to drive redox reactions under mild operating conditions. Among various photocatalytic materials, bismuth-based photocatalysts have attracted significant attention due to their narrow band gaps, excellent visible-light absorption, layered crystal structures, chemical stability, and tuneable electronic properties. The review discusses the structural and functional characteristics of major bismuth-based systems. Emphasis is placed on advanced modification strategies such as heterojunction construction, metal/non-metal doping, and oxygen-vacancy defect regulation, all of which significantly improve charge separation efficiency, light harvesting and surface reaction kinetics. Recent ternary and Z-scheme systems have demonstrated excellent capability for degrading organic pollutants while concurrently enhancing hydrogen production rates under visible-light irradiation. The review further analyzes the photocatalytic mechanisms governing reactive oxygen species generation, interfacial charge migration and proton reduction pathways. Despite major progress, several limitations remain, including photo-corrosion, charge recombination, low quantum efficiency and challenges in scaling laboratory results to practical reactors. Future perspectives highlight defect-controlled nanostructures, noble-metal-free cocatalysts, real wastewater applications and pilot-scale solar reactor development. Overall, bismuth-based photocatalysts offer strong potential as multifunctional materials for integrating environmental remediation with renewable hydrogen production, supporting the transition toward sustainable energy and water treatment technologies.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.title: Estimation of pre-existing deformations in historical masonry vaults from contemporary point clouds
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.authors: Giulio Lucio Sergio Sacco, Chiara Calderini, Sinan Acikgoz
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.abstract: Vaults in historical masonry structures often feature geometric distortions whose deformation history remains unknown. Understanding these deformations can support damage assessment and residual load-carrying capacity evaluation. This study presents a methodology to estimate pre-existing deformations through non-rigid registration of a reference template to surveyed point clouds. A physics-informed iterative closest point algorithm (π-ICP) which minimises normal distances while constraining elastic strain energy is developed. The template is a triangular three-noded finite element mesh; the optimal nodal displacement field is sought as a linear optimization problem solved using least-squares approach. This enables a flexible representation of undeformed geometries, allowing imposed displacements and discontinuities such as cracks. The method is evaluated on synthetic data generated through FEM simulations of a barrel vault under differential support movement and on real data of a viaduct damaged during piling works. Both applications show accurate displacements recovery and the ability to detect pre-existing and ongoing distortions.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.authors: Davide Schaumann
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.abstract: Multi-agent simulation supports occupant behavior analyses in static buildings, but rarely extends to dynamically reconfigurable environments, preventing pre-deployment evaluation of human-building interactions. This paper introduces a narrative-based framework modeling occupants and adaptive architectural systems as agents, positioning buildings as active participants rather than passive containers. A narrative formalism coordinates human and spatial agents, a visual scripting interface enables non-experts to author interaction scenarios, and modular components aim to foster usability and transfer across spatial contexts and interaction types. An exploratory, early-stage evaluation with novice architects in an academic setting modeled eight scenarios spanning multiple spatial scales and four adaptive component types using a shared component library, indicating the framework supports simulations across spatial contexts and adaptation types. Survey responses ( n = 25) suggest participants perceived it as valuable, transferable, and supportive of complex interaction scenarios. An exploratory between-cohort comparison links reduced visual scripting node counts to improved perceived template support.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.abstract: Although digital technologies are increasingly adopted in projects, limited research has explored how they may support trust, communication, commitment, collaborative problem-solving, and alignment around shared objectives in Collaborative Project Delivery Models (CPDMs)-based AEC projects. This paper addresses a gap in understanding how digital technologies enhance collaboration in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry. https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150138.title: Limits on growth: Governing urban futures in Beijing
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150138.abstract: This paper conceptualises limits on growth in Beijing, whose 2016–2035 master plan constructs a highly selective national capital for the central state by removing functions and populations deemed non-essential. Drawing on archival analysis of planning documents since 1949, extensive expert and ethnographic interviews, and multi-sited fieldwork conducted between 2017 and 2023, it develops a Lefebvrian spatio-temporal framework with three relational dimensions for analysing urban future-making. Temporal entanglements show how a historically sedimented anti-metropolis disposition is reactivated amid contemporary state recentralisation. Performative governance examines how the diagnosis of ‘big city disease’ reframes demographic and functional pressures as urban pathology, legitimising relocation and greening as therapeutic intervention. Lived futurity reveals how officials, villagers and migrants negotiate these measures through procrastination, speculation and retreat. The article theorises limits on growth as an emergent mode of Chinese statecraft in which extra-economic priorities selectively guide the production of the urban future. Situating Beijing within a wider, politically heterogeneous turn that increasingly treats demographic and territorial growth as a crisis, it reconceives urban future-making as a politics of foreclosure: not only who profits from growth, but who is permitted to remain when growth is limited by design.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150340.title: The gendered right to the city: Mediated access, urban agriculture and women’s empowerment in Kumasi
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150340.authors: Mary Duah, John Boulard Forkuor, David Forkuor et al.
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150340.abstract: Urban space is a vital resource for city dwellers. While literature examines the use of formal public spaces by urban residents for commerce and social activities, scholarly attention to informal agricultural spaces remains limited. This study uses a synthesis of Kabeer’s empowerment framework and Lefebvre’s right to the city to analyse women’s access to and use of urban space for agriculture in Ghana as a transformative space where gender, body and empowerment intersect. Our findings reveal that male networks serve as gatekeepers through whom women access urban space for urban agriculture. While women’s access to this social capital is empowering, it indicates that women’s right to the city and to spatial justice is mediated, achieved through relational networks and experienced as a relational right. Our findings further reveal that women appropriate these urban spaces in ways that enhance their general well-being, bodily sovereignty and promote intergenerational rights to the city for their children. By demonstrating how women’s spatial access enables agency, bodily sovereignty and the pursuit of intergenerational rights, we argue for a more nuanced understanding of empowerment and rights within informal urban contexts in the Global South.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70414.title: Geo‐Setting Risk Assessment in Eurasia: A Multidimensional Framework and Strategies
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70414.authors: Zhang, J., Dong, S., Li, J., Zhao, Z.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70414.abstract: ABSTRACT Amid intensifying geopolitical tensions and climate‐related pressures, geo‐setting risk has become increasingly multidimensional. This analysis of geo‐setting risk in 16 Eurasian countries from 2010 to 2023, using a composite framework integrating regional geopolitical, political, economic, social, and ecological indicators, revealed marked spatial and temporal heterogeneity. Ukraine, Armenia, the Russian Federation, Georgia, and Azerbaijan were identified as high‐comprehensive‐risk countries, whereas other countries displayed distinct vulnerabilities across specific dimensions in 2023. The findings suggest that Eurasian geo‐setting risk cannot be reduced to the Russia–Ukraine conflict alone but reflects the combined influence of conflict exposure, governance conditions, economic structure, social pressure, and ecological constraints. A two‐dimensional typology linking comprehensive risk to the dominant mechanisms is proposed to support comparative risk profiling and differentiated governance discussions.

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02785.title: The carbon at risk measure for managing carbon removal risk and guiding portfolio construction
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02785.authors: Bali Lee, Tom Bearpark, Oleksandr Kit et al.
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02785.abstract: Abstract Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted removals and realized storage at a given confidence level and time horizon. We calibrate CaR in two proof-of-concept applications: forest carbon, where Monte Carlo simulations driven by satellite fire data yield a single-project 95% CaR of more than 70% over 200 years for California, and geological storage, where simulations using the Storage Security Calculator show that the 95% CaR ranges from 0.15% (well-regulated offshore) to 17% (poorly regulated onshore). Combining technologies in a portfolio can help manage tail risk cost-effectively. The minimum cost of meeting a permanence target depends on the magnitude and correlation structure of key risk factors. CaR provides a technology-agnostic basis for risk-calibrated buffer sizing, insurance pricing and reserve-fund design, over both policy- and climate-relevant horizons.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08494.title: Quantifying the long-term evolution of post-earthquake debris-flow activity in the epicentral area of the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake, China
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08494.authors: Qingyun Shi, Weihua Zhang, Chuan Tang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08494.abstract: Abstract The 2008 Wenchuan earthquake triggered widespread coseismic landslides and supplied large volumes of loose material on hillslopes and channels, resulting in persistent post-earthquake debris flow activity near the epicentral area. Quantifying the long-term evolution of this activity is important for geohazard assessment, but remains challenge because debris flows are jointly controlled by sediment supply, topography, and rainfall. In this study, a catchment-scale framework was developed to evaluate debris flow activity intensity in 44 catchments affected by the Wenchuan earthquake. Multi-temporal landslide inventories from 2008 to 2019 were used to calculate landslide sediment supply potential (LSSP), which integrates landslide areal density, spatial distribution indices, and channel gradient. LSSP was then combined with representative hourly rainfall intensities from documented debris flow triggering events to derive a debris flow activity intensity index (AI DF ). The results show that active landslide area decreased from 122.05 km² in 2008 to 30.55 km² in 2019, while recovery areas expanded progressively. LSSP increased sharply immediately after the earthquake and then declined over time, with a rapid decrease during 2008–2011 followed by a slower adjustment phase. Nevertheless, sediment supply in many catchments remained above the pre-earthquake level in 2019. AI DF showed an overall decline after its post-earthquake peak, although temporary increases occurred during major rainfall events. Comparison with documented debris flow events indicates that AI DF captures the main temporal pattern of observed activity. The fitted long-term trend suggests three stages of post-earthquake debris flow activity: an active period from 2008 to 2013, a recession period from 2013 to 2048, and a relatively stable period after 2048. These results indicate that debris flow activity in the Wenchuan earthquake-affected area may persist for several decades, mainly controlled by the gradual depletion and redistribution of landslide-derived sediment under rainfall forcing.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.title: Beyond exposure: Pathways between urban greening, nature connection and wellbeing in Australian policy frameworks
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.authors: Rose Macaulay, Rebecca Toohey, Stéphanie Lavau, Kathryn J. H. Williams
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.abstract: Urban greening initiatives are increasingly positioned as strategies to improve health and wellbeing in cities. While academic research has long acknowledged the role of psychological connections to nature in shaping wellbeing, it is unclear whether and how this relationship is recognised in urban greening policy. This study examines how Australian urban greening and biodiversity strategies conceptualise and evaluate wellbeing and nature connection. We conducted a structured review of 43 policy documents from state and local governments across Australia, analysing how strategies define and operationalise these concepts. We found that while strategies acknowledge multiple dimensions of wellbeing and recognise both physical and psychological connections to nature, evaluation practices focus almost exclusively on biophysical outputs of urban greening, such as canopy cover and park access. Psychological connections to nature were absent from evaluation targets, and most strategies lacked indicators assessing medium- to long-term wellbeing outcomes. This highlights a significant gap between how wellbeing and nature connection are conceptualised and how they are evaluated in practice. We provide recommendations for integrating psychological dimensions of nature connection into urban greening policy, including clearer articulation of causal pathways, consistent conceptualisation, and development of evaluation frameworks that capture both nature connection and wellbeing as measurable outcomes.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.title: Effects of residential garden features on biodiversity: A systematic review
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.authors: Muriel Deparis, Mathieu Lachaise, Quentin Dutertre, Emmanuelle Baudry
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.abstract: In the urban mosaic of habitats, residential gardens can sustain high levels of biodiversity. Although many gardeners are interested in biodiversity-friendly designs, they lack a clear overview of the available evidence to guide their choices, as the scientific knowledge about it remains dispersed. Here, we present a comprehensive synthesis of peer-reviewed articles investigating the relationship between residential garden features and biodiversity. Through a systematic search of Web of Science and Scopus, we identified 3,872 articles and retained 31 after a three-stage screening process and critical appraisal. These articles report the effects of 16 garden features on the richness and abundance of 62 taxonomic groups. Evidence was generally sparse and uneven across garden features and taxa, with many results supported by a few studies. Arthropods were highly documented, contrary to bats, amphibians, or reptiles. Index of garden heterogeneity was the most documented feature and often showed positive effects on birds, bumblebees, and butterflies. However, many studies reported non-significant or contradictory results, limiting broad generalizations. Floral resources showed the most consistent positive effects on pollinators, regardless of their nativness. Lawn area did not show clear effects. Shrub area and tree number and cover were generally beneficial for beetles, birds, earthworms, and wasps, although many other taxa appeared unaffected. Future studies should propose new protocols to study a wider range of garden features, beyond their presence and area, and provide independent replication for poorly documented taxa. Explore the tensions between garden use and biodiversity-oriented design options is also a promising line for future research.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Recent environmental change shapes biotic homogenisation of Orthoptera and Mantodea communities in semi-dry grasslands
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Dominik Poniatowski, Felix Maximilian Freienstein, Marco Drung et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. However, many grassland remnants are undergoing gradual habitat degradation due to climate change, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and the relaxation or abandonment of traditional management. While declines of specialised insects have repeatedly been reported, the extent to which these drivers promote long-term community reorganisation and biotic homogenisation remains poorly understood. Using a nationwide resurvey of 221 semi-dry grassland patches across Germany, spanning two to three decades, we investigated long-term changes in Orthoptera and Mantodea communities. We quantified changes in species richness, community composition, and beta diversity, and related these patterns to major global change drivers. Despite an increase in total species richness, these communities became increasingly homogenised, as indicated by declining beta diversity. Community reorganisation was characterised by pronounced winner-loser dynamics, with highly mobile generalists and thermophilous species expanding, whereas threatened species, low-mobility habitat specialists, and species associated with High Nature Value farmland declined. Winner species richness increased particularly in warm and dry regions, under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and outside protected areas. By contrast, low-mobility habitat specialists and threatened species persisted most successfully in structurally heterogeneous habitats. High shrub cover was negatively associated with both winners and losers, indicating an overall deterioration of habitat suitability. Our findings demonstrate that environmental change does not necessarily reduce species richness but can profoundly reorganise communities through selective filtering of species. Maintaining habitat heterogeneity with appropriate management strategies is therefore crucial for buffering biodiversity loss under ongoing global change.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebee4.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping sustainability science through advances in climate modeling, ecosystem monitoring, resource management, and evidence synthesis. Yet its use also raises concerns about reliability, equity, and environmental impacts. In this Prospective, we identify four priorities for responsible AI integration: ensuring AI-supported claims are causal, transparent, and auditable; treating model selection as an environmental decision; building sustainability-focused AI infrastructure; and engaging sustainability scientists and affected communities in AI design and governance. With these safeguards, AI can enhance sustainability science while promoting equitable and environmentally responsible decision-making.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdd.title: Wave and slope thresholds for mangrove restoration and nature-based solution design
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdd.authors: Jin Liu, Andrew Pomeroy, Brendan  Scott Lanham et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdd.abstract: Abstract Globally, shorelines are experiencing widespread recession, promoting greater interest in nature-based solutions (NbSs) for coastal protection. Along tropical and sub-tropical coastlines, mangroves are among the habitat-forming species increasingly targeted for nature-based coastal protection. However, practical implementation requires tools that identify shorelines where hydrodynamic and geomorphic conditions are likely to support successful mangrove establishment and long-term persistence. This study quantifies first-order suitability envelopes (hereafter thresholds) for mangrove presence by linking wave height and bathymetric slope to observed mangrove distributions in subtropical wave-dominated barrier estuarine systems. Mangroves were most likely to be present where the 80 th percentile significant wave height ( H s ) was below 0.14 m and bathymetric slope was gentler than 0.01. Above these thresholds, the probability of mangrove occurrence decreased from approximately 23%–25% to 13%–15%, indicating strong but non-exclusive physical controls. Importantly, the probability did not decline to zero beyond these limits, suggesting that mangrove distribution is better described as a suitability threshold rather than a fixed ecological threshold. Spatial analysis indicated that approximately 26% of currently unvegetated shoreline areas in the study fell within the identified wave-slope thresholds, representing potentially suitable but unrealized mangrove habitat. These findings demonstrate that mangrove distribution is partly governed by hydrodynamic and geomorphic processes. While these potential restoration areas are identified based strictly on hydrodynamic and bathymetric thresholds, other critical drivers, such as tidal elevation, sediment supply, and salinity gradients, may further restrict suitable locations. The proposed methods of deriving thresholds in this study provide transferable, process-based criteria for identifying restoration opportunity areas and informing the design of NbSs for coastal resilience in estuarine environments.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebee5.title: Evolving energy-water infrastructure strengthens drought resilience in the U.S. Northeast and Midwest
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebee5.authors: Hussain H. Bokhari, Charles J Vörösmarty, Stephanie Herbert, Carry Pak
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebee5.abstract: Abstract Strategies to strengthen regional water security will be essential for navigating a critical 21st-century environmental challenge: securing freshwater supplies against growing demands and increasingly severe climate extremes. This paper assesses the evolution of water security in the historically water-rich U.S. Northeast (NE) and Midwest (MW) to quantify their resilience to severe drought now and in the future. We develop a counterfactual framework that projects sectoral water demands based on socio-economic drivers and deconstructs the benefits of supply- and demand-side adaptations at the regional scale. During the half-century between the historic NE/MW 1960s drought and the 2012-2013 North American drought, rapid socio-economic growth held the potential to push water systems to a breaking point, rendering them unequipped to manage the impact of such severe droughts. However, this study reveals that both regions built resilience through long-term adaptations that averted potential water crises, mitigating otherwise severe summertime water stress (withdrawal-to-available supply) by factors of 2.8 (MW) and 5.6 (NE). While supply-side strategies through reservoir construction and coastal power development played a role, the driving factor has been water demand management, accounting for 83% to 92% of summertime water stress mitigations across the two regions and drought scenarios. These gains were rooted in economic and political incentives to adopt advanced thermoelectric cooling technologies and efficient industrial technologies, together with the regions’ shift from a manufacturing to service economy. Thus, our projections of increased water demand by the mid-21st century highlight a critical reality: future drought resilience will require continued investments in demand-side efficiency gains, such as water-efficient electricity production systems, to keep pace with expected socio-economic trends.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb1de.title: Manage derailment risks to avoid Hothouse Earth
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb1de.authors: Dyke, J., Laybourn, L., Abrams, J.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb1de.abstract: Abstract The risk of a ‘Hothouse Earth’ trajectory has become increasingly prominent in debates about Earth system stability and climate overshoot. Existing analyses primarily focus on biophysical feedbacks that may amplify warming beyond direct anthropogenic forcing. We argue the concept has not previously incorporated how social destabilisation lowers the effective threshold at which biophysical tipping dynamics become self-sustaining, independently of further anthropogenic forcing and so undermines the capacity for planetary stewardship. We define ‘derailment risk’ as the possibility that escalating Earth system disruption weakens the social, political, and economic conditions required to sustain mitigation, adaptation, and ecological restoration. Such risks emerge when climate impacts contribute to a wide range of challenges, including debt crises, institutional erosion, political fragmentation, supply-chain instability, and declining public support for environmental action. These reinforcing feedbacks may reduce humanity’s capacity to respond even before biophysical tipping thresholds are crossed. We therefore extend the Hothouse Earth framework by incorporating social dynamics into the Earth system stability landscape. We propose a three-stage framework for assessing and managing derailment risks: conceptual mapping of socio-biophysical feedbacks; anticipatory resilience-building interventions; responsive governance strategies for periods of escalating instability. We conclude that planetary stewardship should prioritise maintaining and expanding collective agency under worsening Earth system stress.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb55d.title: Carbon prices and cooking fires: how decarbonization pathway design shapes household energy burdens
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb55d.authors: George, M., Clarke, L., Min, J., Pachauri, S. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb55d.abstract: Abstract Pathways reaching the same climate target can distribute household energy costs very differently across income groups. We compare 16 core mitigation pathways spanning a cost-optimal benchmark and technology, timing, effort-sharing, and demand-side designs, plus one rebound sensitivity, within a common integrated assessment framework. All core pathways remain below 2 °C and converge to approximately 1.5 °C warming by 2100, consistent with the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C temperature goal. We translate energy- and food-price outcomes into household energy burdens across income deciles in India and the United States using survey-informed downscaling. In 2030, cost-optimal, technology, and pace pathways are regressive in both countries, with larger burden increases for poorer deciles. In India, lower-demand pathways reduce global carbon prices and lower burdens for poorer households, whereas accelerated electrification and rapid traditional-biomass phase-out raise burdens. Historical-responsibility transfers lower burdens in India and raise them in the United States under the stylized transfer design. A conventional gross-income sensitivity preserves pathway rankings and almost all decile-level burden-change signs but roughly halves poorest-decile magnitudes in India. Accounting for food expenditure therefore reveals affordability pressures on poorer households that gross-income measures mute. Scenario design is an equity-relevant dimension of pathway assessment alongside revenue recycling.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebb4c.title: Characterizing drinking-water facility exposure to historical wildfires in Northern Colorado
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebb4c.authors: Mosher, D., Sun, G., Caldwell, P., Zhang, Y. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebb4c.abstract: Abstract Wildfire increasingly threatens forested headwater watersheds that supply drinking water to downstream communities, yet current wildfire exposure assessments rarely account for inter-basin transfers (IBTs), which can expand source-water footprints beyond natural watershed boundaries and alter the hydrologic connections between fires and drinking-water intakes. Here, we developed a reproducible assessment approach to quantify historical wildfire exposure for drinking-water intakes and applied it in northern Colorado as a case study. The analysis integrated historical (1984–2024) wildfire perimeters, burn severity, subwatershed boundaries, natural hydrologic flow paths, IBT connectivity, and public water supply utility information. Across the 7,308 km 2 study area, 1895 km 2 burned (26% of the landscape), at least one fire occurred in 54 of the 90 watersheds examined, and approximately 31% of total burned area was classified as high severity. Across all 14 events studied, fires affected drinking-water systems serving an average of 344 854 people and four downstream intake facilities per event. Intake-level exposure depended not only on fire size, but also on burn severity and hydrologic connectivity. Incorporating IBTs altered the relative importance of individual subwatersheds in headwater areas in terms of their wildfire exposure on downstream intake systems. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for both natural and managed hydrologic connectivity in source-water wildfire exposure assessments and provide a basis for decision-support tools, such as Forests to Faucets, that directly link forest disturbance, water-supply infrastructure, and downstream communities.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb4ca.title: Democracy and income inequality moderate the impacts of protected areas
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb4ca.authors: Coleman, E., Kashwan, P., Haque, M.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb4ca.abstract: Abstract Many policymakers and conservation activists promote creating terrestrial protected areas (PAs) as a central tool to preserve biodiversity and offset global carbon emissions. However, the socioeconomic consequences of PA designation remain understudied. Using an event study design, this paper estimates the causal treatment effect of creating PAs on changes in cultivated agriculture land from within PA boundaries. We examine the global population of 64 997 terrestrial PAs established 1995–2020 and evaluate temporal changes in land classified as agriculture cultivation in 5 year intervals. We find that PAs (modestly) reduce the amount cultivation within their boundaries. Then, using data on country-level income inequality and democratic institutions we estimate the treatment effect of creating PAs in countries that are less democratic and have more income inequality. We find that PAs located in places with more income inequality and less democracy significantly reduce cultivation, at a much greater rate than in countries that score higher on democracy and have less income inequality. These findings highlight the critical role of socioeconomic and political context in shaping the outcomes of PA policies. Conservation policy in nondemocratic and high economic inequality countries must create appropriate safeguards for local people.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb70b.title: Consistent drivers of lightning-ignited wildfires across global boreal forests
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb70b.authors: Engle, B., Bratoev, I., Crowley, M., Zhu, Y. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb70b.abstract: Abstract Climate change is expected to change both fire susceptibility and lightning activity in global boreal forests. The mechanics governing lightning-ignited wildfire (LIW) ignition remain, however, unclear, making predictions at global boreal scale challenging. Here we examine short-term temporal impacts of weather on ignition probability using a novel dataset on LIWs in a quasi-experimental design of ignition and non-ignition lightning pairs. Specifically, our dataset is comprised of 5251 lightning pairs coupled with temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, lightning characteristics (multiplicity, polarity, peak current, and duration) and net primary productivity. We estimate the effect of these predictor variables on ignition probability across three separate models; the full boreal, open forests and closed forests. We find a clear relationship between ignition probability and temperature, relative humidity, total precipitation, and polarity. A one standard-deviation increase in temperature (∼3.3 °C) increased ignition probability by 44%–69%, while increased precipitation and relative humidity reduced ignition probability. Both temperature and precipitation were most predictive 3–8 d before lightning and the effect lasted up to 7–11 d after lightning. Positive polarity was also associated with increased ignition likelihood. Our results suggest that LIW occurrence within the global boreal is primarily driven by short-term fire weather rather than lightning characteristics alone. A projected increase in temperatures is expected to drive ignition probability in the boreal, though this may be partly offset by an increase in total precipitation.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cities.2026.10.authors: Damaris Chieregato Vicentin, Gustavo Hermínio Salati Marcondes de Moraes, Walter Leal Filho et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cities.2026.10.abstract: Everyday urban problems in Latin American cities, particularly those related to public safety and traffic congestion, have become increasingly relevant in debates on smart and sustainable urban development. This study investigates perception-based indicators of structural and technological aspects associated with more favorable perceptions regarding everyday urban problems in 12 Latin American cities, focusing on public safety and traffic congestion. The methodology employed Grey Incidence Analysis on indicators from the IMD Smart City Index 2025. The results reveal that more favorable perceptions regarding public safety are most strongly associated with lifelong learning opportunities offered by local institutions, followed by access to basic sanitation in poorer areas. In contrast, more favorable perceptions regarding traffic congestion are most strongly associated with satisfaction with public transport and the perceived contribution of ride-sharing apps to reducing congestion. Parking guidance apps and bike-sharing services show a comparatively weaker relational link to favorable perceptions regarding congestion. The study contributes to citizen-centric smart city research by showing that urban policies require problem-specific configurations: socially integrated structural interventions for public safety and coordinated transport infrastructure and digital mobility solutions for congestion.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70391.title: Estimation of Excess Inhalation Non‐Cancer and Cancer Risk From Volatile Organic Compound Mixtures in New York City Nail Salons
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70391.authors: Ierardi, A., Thompson, R., Fisher, S., Anderson, K. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70391.abstract: ABSTRACT Nail salon workers are acutely and chronically exposed to mixtures of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), yet health risks in New York City (NYC) salons have not been systematically assessed. We performed an occupational risk assessment using integrated real‐time total VOC (TVOC) monitoring and chemical‐specific sampling of 11 VOCs across five NYC salons. Median and peak exposures and their 95th percentile (upper‐bound) values were used in non‐cancer and cancer risk models using deterministic and probabilistic approaches. Deterministic non‐cancer risk modeling indicated hazard indices (HIs) were generally below the benchmark value of 1, with exceedances observed only using upper‐bound exposures in the salon with the highest VOC concentrations. The probabilistic non‐cancer assessment showed a similar pattern, with some salons having non‐negligible probabilities of HI exceedance despite median HIs below 1. Deterministic and probabilistic benzene cancer risk assessments indicated exceedances of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) de minimis benchmark under multiple exposure scenarios. Although VOC concentrations were below occupational exposure limits (OELs), incorporating exposure variability and uncertainty identified elevated non‐cancer and cancer risks under certain scenarios. Previous research has linked nail salon work to adverse health effects, including respiratory symptoms and developmental and reproductive effects, suggesting that current OELs may not adequately protect this workforce. Our results highlight the need for improved exposure limits, chemical mixture risk assessment methods, and health protections for nail salon workers.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Incentive-compatible risk preferences and sustainable land management adoption under climate risk: Evidence from semi-arid Kenya
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Amos Nyangira Tirra, Rose Adhiambo Nyikal, John Mburu et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Sustainable land management (SLM) practices are widely promoted as an effective pathway for mitigating climate-induced production risks and enhancing agricultural sustainability. However, their uptake has remained low across Sub-Saharan Africa despite the associated benefits. Existing studies have primarily evaluated socio-economic and institutional determinants, with limited evidence on incentivized risk preference and loss aversion, particularly for multiple practice adoption. This gap is especially consequential in arid and semi-arid regions, where production uncertainty is high and adoption decisions are inherently risky. In South Eastern Kenya (SEK), recurrent droughts and extreme climate events have contributed to widespread food insecurity, crop losses, and livestock deaths, making adoption important for agricultural sustainability and climate resilience. Using data from 867 farm households selected through multistage sampling in semi-arid SEK, this study examines how risk preference and loss aversion are associated with SLM adoption breadth. An incentivized field experiment was employed to elicit both measures while adoption behaviour was assessed using a generalized Poisson regression model. Risk-loving farmers show greater adoption breadth than risk-averse farmers, while higher loss aversion is associated with lower adoption breadth. Locus of control, aspiration, wealth, shock exposure and crop diversity are positively associated with adoption breadth. Perceived climate-resilience benefits show a modest positive association, whereas perceived productivity and environmental-quality benefits are negatively associated. These findings highlight the relevance of behavioural heterogeneity for strategies to broaden SLM adoption in climate-vulnerable semi-arid areas.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Quantification and characterisation of the illegal dumping of municipal waste
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Beatriz Afonso, Graça Martinho, Joaquim Pires Pina, Mário Ramos
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Even in developed countries, municipal waste (MW) left outside communal containers remains a significant challenge, affecting urban hygiene. This study analysed the improper disposal of MW across three monitoring circuits, each 14 km long, representing rural inland, urban inland, and urban coastal settings, with particular attention to the pre-holiday period and the preparation of dwellings for the tourist season. A total of 128 sites were systematically monitored over three periods, recording 407 occurrences. The total estimated volume and mass of abandoned MW varied across circuits, with the urban inland circuit accounting for the highest number of new occurrences, as well as the largest estimated volumes and masses of waste. By volume, paper and cardboard packaging and bulky waste predominated, particularly in the coastal urban area. By mass, construction and demolition waste (CDW) arising from minor construction and demolition activities within private households accounted for the largest fraction. In Portugal, the management of CDW generated by such activities is the responsibility of MW management systems. Furthermore, higher per capita amounts of abandoned MW were recorded in the urban coastal area. These patterns may reflect the preparation of dwellings for the summer tourist season. The recurrence of improper waste disposal highlighted operational challenges for waste collection planning. The findings also suggest a potential role of citizen behaviour in waste abandonment. In addition, the study developed context-adjusted indicators of MW abandonment, which may support further research and inform MW management practices, particularly by helping to identify spatial patterns of waste abandonment and optimise collection strategies.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: An integrated assessment framework for comparing and enhancing flood resilience in heterogeneous floodplains
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Thanh Phuoc Ho, Wenhan Feng, Trung Nguyen Ly et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Climate change is intensifying flood hazards in deltas, challenging agricultural communities dependent on hydrological conditions. Flood resilience has therefore emerged as an alternative to traditional risk management. Yet, comparative resilience studies often overlook how resilience measures vary across floodplain hydrological regimes (FHRs) within a delta. This study proposes an integrated flood-resilience assessment framework integrating FHRs, including freshwater (Fresh_Fl), transitional (Transitional_Fl), and tidal (Tidal_Fl), with flood resilience capacities (FRCs) (absorptive, adaptive, and transformative). Using the Vietnamese Mekong Delta as a case study, the framework operationalizes 31 flood-resilience measures as regime-specific indicators, drawing on 357 surveys and 30 semi-structured interviews. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used to visualize broad resilience orientations, while Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis H tests identified statistically supported measure-level differences. Results show that most measures were applied and received high perceived-effectiveness scores with non-significant differences, forming a shared baseline across FHRs, whereas each FHR showed different measure emphases. Fresh_Fl was characterized by strong absorptive protection through large-scale dikes, and farmer-led low dikes were perceived more positively than in Transitional_Fl. Yet, high-dike dominance reduced the role of some adaptive measures and shifted environmental and downstream trade-offs. Additionally, Transitional_Fl and Tidal_Fl showed higher ratings for mechanization and flood utilization under variable water conditions, while government support for flood-adaptive rice was rated more positively in Fresh_Fl and Transitional_Fl. These findings support resilience planning moving beyond one-size-fits-all strategies and differentiated policy pathways considering hydrological conditions, feasibility, governance responsibilities, and maladaptation risks. The framework offers conditional decision-support logic for other flood-prone deltas.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Layered double hydroxides functionalized electrospun recycled polyamide 6 from fishing nets: structure–property relationships for antimicrobial non-woven fabrics
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Annafelicia Civitavecchia, Simona Sabbatini, Emiliano Laudadio et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Plastic pollution, particularly marine plastic waste from discarded fishing nets, represents a significant environmental challenge and highlights the need for effective strategies to recover and valorize end-of-life polymers. Polyamide 6 (PA6) fishing nets are an underexploited source for the development of high-value functional materials. This work develops antimicrobial non-woven fabrics (NWFs) from recycled PA6 (rPA6) incorporating organo-modified Mg/Al layered double hydroxides (LDHs) intercalated with antimicrobial anions, namely ascorbate (ASA), ferulate (FER), salicylate (SAL), and citrate (CA), into rPA6, followed by electrospinning. The resulting nanofibrous NWFs were characterized by Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Fourier Transformed Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Wide Angle/Small Angle X-ray Scattering with micro-beam (μWAXS/μSAXS), thermal analysis and tested against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Homogeneous nanofibers were obtained and LDH incorporation preserved rPA6 chemical structure while reducing crystallinity. rPA6/LDH-FER, rPA6/LDH-ASA, and rPA6/LDH-CA, showed 96.7 to 99.9% bacterial mortality. After thermal aging at 115 °C, LDH-containing NWFs exhibited improved structural stability. These results demonstrate the feasibility of converting recycled PA6 fishing-nets into functional antimicrobial nanofibrous fabrics through LDH functionalization and electrospinning, supporting circular and sustainable applications of marine recycled polyamides.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4a.title: Spatially compounding climate extremes and environmental risk: cross-regional synchrony, spatial buffering loss, and systemic consequences
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4a.abstract: Abstract Spatially compounding climate extremes are increasingly recognized as a source of climate-related risk, and their risk significance depends on how synchrony affects connected systems. The critical transition occurs when cross-regional synchrony reduces support from places that would otherwise buffer one another through substitution, reserve capacity, mutual assistance or recovery support—a condition we term spatial buffering loss. This Topical Review synthesizes empirical and methodological evidence to examine how synchrony is generated, when it translates into functional loss, and what is required to assess that transition. Food production, water allocation and firefighting cooperation provide complementary settings for examining substitution, reserve and assistance functions, while the synthesis distinguishes joint exposure from support available to recipients. Atmospheric circulation, persistent weather patterns, land–atmosphere feedbacks and hydrological connectivity can organize synchrony; functional evidence determines whether that synchrony reduces compensating support and produces systemic consequences. Accordingly, credible assessment must connect event topology and joint-tail behaviour with functional exposure, an explicit compensating relation and a counterfactual estimate of support that would otherwise have remained available. By linking event organization to recipient support, the synthesis provides a functional basis for assessing spatial buffering loss across connected systems. This perspective connects the evidence to decisions about supplier diversification, reserve operation and mutual assistance.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4c.title: Is Indigenous Knowledge meaningfully represented in the IPCC AR6? A bibliometric meta-analysis
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4c.authors: Ritodhi Chakraborty, Pasang Yangjee Sherpa, Eric Nost et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4c.abstract: Abstract In recent global climatic and environmental reports, Indigenous Knowledges (IK) are recognised as essential to comprehending social-ecological systems and multi-scalar climate-society relationships. However, IK and Indigenous Peoples (IP) continue to be mostly excluded from important and powerful processes such as the UNFCCC and the IPCC reports. In the current (AR7) cycle of the IPCC, it is important to understand whether the last cycle (AR6) meaningfully engaged with IK and IP. Here, we present a multi-tiered bibliometric analysis of the literature cited in the AR6 report (n=46,145 citations), through which we identified citations with abstracts mentioning IK (n=482). Additionally, through exploring this cluster of IK citations, we address enduring questions around disciplinary bias, geographical bias, and academic journal bias. Finally, we categorise IK citations using two indexes of equitable knowledge production. This highlights the different types of relationships (from extractive to co-productive) that guided the cited papers’ research process. Our findings highlight that despite advocacy, promises, and assurances, IK is mostly excluded from the IPCC AR6 report (1.04% of scholarly literature cited). We also call attention to the fact that biophysical sciences, elite journals, and authors from the Global North are dominant in the IK that is included. Finally, we identify some key points of intervention for AR7, which include strategic choices for chapter authors, a focus on Working Group I (climate science), and the inclusion of chapter-scale knowledge justice audits.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4d.authors: 崖丽娟, Jieyi Ou, Yongfen Zhao et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4d.abstract: Abstract The South China Sea (SCS) is one of the most active marginal seas for tropical cyclones (TCs) worldwide and a key region for TC hazards along the coasts of southern China, Philippines and Vietnam. However, the drivers of long-term changes in intense TC development in this region remain unclear. Here, we show that the number of TCs reaching Category 3-5 intensity has increased significantly, with more occurring in the northern SCS. This change is primarily linked to an increasing contribution of western North Pacific TCs entering through the Luzon Strait, which experience weaker land-induced weakening than those crossing the Philippine archipelago and retain greater intensity for subsequent development. After entering the SCS, reduced ocean cooling and enhanced oceanic and atmospheric conditions have increased the environmental favorability for intense TC development in the northern SCS. These results highlight the role of regional ocean-land-atmosphere interactions in reshaping where TCs reach high intensities.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4b.title: Integrating local ecological knowledge from professional fishers with environmental observations can improve the understanding, forecasting, and management of climate-sensitive jellyfish hazards
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4b.authors: Seo Yeol Choi, Seok‐Hyun Youn, Kyoung Yeon Kim
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4b.abstract: Abstract Climate variability is increasing the frequency and impacts of marine hazards, yet early warning systems often lack mechanisms to translate environmental signals into timely governance responses. Here, we examine how local ecological knowledge can be operationalized within a national hazard monitoring framework using jellyfish blooms as a model marine hazard. We analyzed 15 years (2010–2024) of weekly, fisher-reported observations from Korean coastal waters, focusing on Aurelia coerulea and Nemopilema nomurai. From these weekly reports, we calculated occurrence rate, defined as the percentage of respondents reporting jellyfish presence, and aggregation frequency, defined as the percentage reporting jellyfish aggregations. These indices were interpreted as operational risk indicators rather than standardized abundance estimates. Their utility was evaluated by testing temporal alignment with official national jellyfish alerts and by quantifying species-specific lead–lag structures. Distinct bloom dynamics emerged: A. coerulea formed persistent aggregations peaking from late spring to summer, whereas N. nomurai exhibited low background occurrence punctuated by abrupt mass events in late summer to autumn. Monthly sea surface temperature (SST) showed positive associations with fisher-reported occurrence and aggregation frequencies for both species (p < 0.05). Generalized Additive Models indicated a long-term weakening of A. coerulea bloom intensity and an earlier seasonal shift in N. nomurai peaks, consistent with warming-related phenological change. Alert timing closely tracked A. coerulea peaks, while N. nomurai alerts preceded peaks by 4–6 weeks, reflecting differences in life history and cross-boundary transport. By linking weekly fisher-reported bloom signals with official national jellyfish alerts, this study shows how local ecological knowledge can provide decision-relevant information for bloom timing and operational response to jellyfish hazards under changing climate conditions.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4e.title: Greenhouse gas forcing dominates the recent strengthening of North Pacific Meridional mode influence on ENSO
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4e.authors: Yuqiong Zheng, Shangfeng Chen, Bin Yu et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebe4e.abstract: Abstract The North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM) is a key extratropical trigger of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, and its influence on ENSO has increased markedly in recent decades, offering a pathway to improve ENSO predictability. Yet, the relative contributions of external forcings versus internal variability to this intensified influence remain uncertain. Using multi-model simulation outputs from the Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project and a suite of numerical experiments, we demonstrate that greenhouse gas (GHG) forcing dominates over internal variability in driving the recent strengthening of the NPMM–ENSO connection, whereas aerosol and natural forcings have minimal impact. GHG forcing enhances the wind–evaporation–SST feedback over the subtropical North Pacific by elevating the background mean SST, which amplifies NPMM-induced westerly wind bursts over the western tropical Pacific and promotes ENSO development. Sensitivity experiments further demonstrate that GHG-induced SST increasing in the subtropical North Pacific enhances the atmospheric response associated with the NPMM. These findings reveal an important role of anthropogenic forcing in modulating the extratropical impact on ENSO and suggest potential opportunities for extending ENSO prediction lead times.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb146.title: Regional economic impacts and emission responses under solar radiation modification
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb146.authors: Bjordal, J., Dijk, E., Cornec, H., Smith, A. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb146.abstract: Abstract Solar radiation modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the climate system’s response to various SRM strategies, as well as their aggregate economic consequences, the spatial distribution of economic impacts has received less attention. In this study, we use NorESM2-Disaggregated Integrated Assessment Model—an Earth System Model coupled to a high-resolution integrated assessment model—to assess the economic impacts, measured in gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, in an idealised SRM scenario where incoming solar radiation is reduced by 1%. Our results suggest that, relative to a baseline without SRM, most countries experience economic gains under SRM, with only a few countries facing negative impacts. Low-income countries tend to see the largest benefits, reducing disparities in GDP per capita across countries relative to the baseline. However, reduced damages and smaller disparities in GDP per capita are accompanied by a ‘moral hazard’ effect, in that SRM leads to higher emissions, which may in turn cause additional adverse effects not captured here. These findings highlight potential trade-offs between economic benefits, the distribution of economic impacts, and increased emissions relevant for SRM governance.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149948.title: The simultaneous slow death and persistent vitality of social infrastructure in elite neighbourhoods
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149948.abstract: This article examines the vitality of social life at street level over time in the patrician elite area of Kensington, London. We consider how luxury amenities, prime homes and high-end stores intersect with the durable presence of an everyday, working city comprising diverse social infrastructures: budget hotels, rent-controlled housing and interstitial social spaces of cafes, parks and street benches. These layers of uses and users co-exist in complex time–space configurations despite the historical and contemporary designation of the neighbourhood as an elite space. Using a range of data sources, we show how the neighbourhood contains distinct features that enable the limited and partial social engagement and hypermobility of wealthy bodies with the social life of the area. However, we also find a diverse social history, culture and complex grounded experiences at street level involving a wide range of residents and other users. These observations demonstrate how, even in the most elite of urban neighbourhoods, spaces remain socially complex and diverse, despite ongoing tensions.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70407.title: Virtual Flood Experience Enhances Preparedness Through Emotional and Neural Engagement
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70407.authors: Fujimi, T., Kochiyama, T., Sato, W., Watanabe, M.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70407.abstract: ABSTRACT As climate change intensifies flood risks, strengthening individual preparedness is essential for sustainable societies. This study tested whether first‐person three‐dimensional computer graphics (3DCG) flood videos can complement official flood maps in motivating preparedness. We used these materials as operationalizations of experiential and descriptive information, respectively. In a preregistered web experiment with 1000 participants, those who viewed flood videos showed a small but statistically significant increase in preparedness intentions compared with those who viewed flood maps. Mediation analyses showed that, among the measured psychological variables, only fear had a significant indirect effect, suggesting that stimulus‐evoked fear helped explain this increase. We also conducted a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study with 45 participants using a within‐subjects design. Flood videos elicited greater right amygdala activation than flood maps, consistent with fear‐related processing. Together, these findings provide convergent behavioral and neural evidence that first‐person 3DCG flood videos evoke stronger fear‐related responses than flood maps and that subjective fear helps account for their effect on preparedness intentions. The results suggest that visually vivid flood videos may complement map‐based communication by increasing emotional salience and promoting flood‐preparedness intentions.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08492.title: Multi-hazard assessment of the eastern slope of the Sistema de Famatina, La Rioja province (Argentina)
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08492.authors: María Cecilia Corbat, Oscar Juárez, Enrique Fucks, José Augusto Casas
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08492.abstract: Abstract In the eastern sector of the Sistema de Famatina, both natural processes and anthropogenic activities pose considerable risks to the landscape and its inhabitants. This study investigates the geohazards and environmental agents that have historically affected the region, with a focus on their implications for local communities and territories. The analysis integrates case studies of documented natural events, identification of mitigation strategies, satellite imagery interpretation, landform recognition, and direct field observations. In addition, meteorological, hydrological, seismic, and demographic data were compiled to identify previously undocumented events with the potential to generate significant socio-environmental impacts. The study area is subject to a range of natural hazards, including those originated by meteorological events (e.g., intense precipitation and strong winds), fluvial processes (e.g., avulsion, gully erosion, and flooding), mass movement processes (e.g., landslides and rockfalls), and seismic activity. Our results reveal the recurrent nature of these hazards; in general, their consequences are compounded by anthropogenic pressures, including land-use changes, variations in land cover, and environmental pollution. Collectively, these factors intensify existing socio-environmental issues. This research contributes to sustainable environmental management by considering plausible future scenarios and hazard interactions. Our findings are intended to inform local and regional socio-economic development strategies and to serve as a scientific resource for policymakers and planners. Furthermore, by enhancing awareness of ongoing and recurring hazards, the study supports community resilience building and the reduction of adverse impacts at the local level.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08496.title: Likelihood-robust fusion of crowdsourced road-passability reports for flood relief dispatch and UAV inspection targeting
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08496.authors: Hailong Li, Ya Li, Xiangnan Song
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08496.abstract: Abstract Flood emergency agencies increasingly combine crowdsourced road reports with scarce unmanned-aerial-vehicle (UAV) inspections, yet panic, stale forwarding, and deliberate rumours can distort road-passability beliefs and redirect relief. This study develops a decision framework for fusing reports when source credibility is uncertain or adversarially exploited and for choosing whether the next trusted observation should inspect a road or recalibrate a reporting source. Credibility is represented by a data-driven ambiguity set and rumours by bounded contamination, yielding a distributionally robust credal posterior and min-max dispatch. We derive the dual value of verification-road-state clarification and calibration spillover-and prove a contamination threshold τ* at which the preferred action switches from road inspection to source recalibration. We further bound robust loss and characterize a strategic relocating attacker. On synthetic benchmarks, non-robust regret rises from 142 to 297 stranded passengers as contamination reaches 0.5, whereas robust regret remains within 105-168; the predicted switch occurs near τ* = 0.13-0.16. In a replay of the 20 July 2021 Zhengzhou flood, non-robust fusion reverses a blocked-road assessment and propagates error across about 62 cells, while robust fusion preserves the assessment and one verification recalibrates about 59 reports. In a Zhengzhou road-network decision test, eight baselines incur 233-300 stranded-passenger equivalents under the rumour, whereas the robust policy retains clean-evidence delivery. The framework provides flood-response agencies with a principled rule for allocating scarce verification when crowdsourced road information may be unreliable or manipulated.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08450.title: Early warning system for non-seismic gravity driven tsunamis
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08450.abstract: Gravity-driven mass flows represent a significant near-field hazard in volcanic environments and, increasingly, in coastal regions affected by climate-driven slope instability. Despite their destructive potential, quantitative assessments of real-time detection systems operating under natural conditions remain scarce. Here we present the performance and sensitivity of the tsunami early-warning system currently operating at Stromboli Volcano (Italy), based on offshore pressure gauges and a real-time detection algorithm. Sixteen years of sea-level records (2010–2026), including 63 tsunamis events ranging from 0.02 to 2 m height, show that the system issues alert within less than 22 s from the tsunami onset and tens of seconds before its maximum amplitude, with no false alarms. A sensitivity analysis, based on Peak-Over-Threshold statistics and extreme wave modeling, demonstrates that the detection capability remains effective even under extreme sea state conditions also for tsunami with height as low as 4 m. To support regional tsunami warning and reduce the alerts for tsunami with no inundation effects on a distant (> 10 km) coasts, we apply real-time Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD), which successfully extracts tsunami signals and preserves waveform characteristics. EEMD also isolates longer period sea level oscillations associated with atmospheric pressure waves within the meteotsunami frequency band, demonstrating the applicability of the method to multiple classes of non-seismic tsunamis. This work provides the first long-term quantitative evaluation of an operational near-field early-warning system for volcanogenic tsunamis and proposes a transferable multi-tier framework for landslide-tsunami and meteotsunami hazard mitigation for coastal environments worldwide.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.title: Smartphone mobility data reveals how home-location heat and park cooling shape park visitation in Los Angeles
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.authors: Yongli Tang, Xiang Li, Xiao Huang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.abstract: Parks can support climate adaptation by providing cooling, but their use is shaped by residents’ cooling needs, parks’ cooling potential and the ability to reach them. Little is known about how residential heat exposure and relative park cooling, measured by the home-park temperature difference, jointly relate to park visitation from an origin-destination perspective. Using mobile phone data and explainable Random Forest models, we examine these associations across park types and demographic groups in Los Angeles County. Results show that local-park visitation was generally negatively associated with home-location temperature, whereas visitation to regional parks and natural areas increased above approximately 35 °C. However, greater visitation did not necessarily correspond to trips to cooler parks relative to home locations. For local parks, greater relative cooling was associated with higher visitation, and this association strengthened as home-location temperature increased. Under extreme heat, the positive cooling-visitation association was strongest in predominantly Hispanic, Asian, and low-income communities. In contrast, visitation to regional parks and natural areas generally peaked when park and home temperatures were similar, with greater cooling not associated with higher visitation. Spatial accessibility may partly explain these differences. Home-park distance was the leading predictor across all park types. Greater cooling at regional parks and natural areas was often associated with longer travel distances and lower transit availability, potentially limiting access to these cooling opportunities. These findings highlight the need to improve cooling capacity in local parks serving socially vulnerable populations while reducing access barriers to larger green spaces during extreme heat.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Impact of global supply chain pressures on energy demand and stability: The role of global sustainability initiatives
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Riazullah Shinwari, Junyi Feng, Nazim Hussain, Shah Mir Mowahed
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Global supply chain pressures (GSCP) have become a major challenge for multinational enterprises (MNEs), influencing firm-level operational decisions, including evolving energy demand patterns. This paper investigates the impact of global supply chain pressures on energy consumption in Chinese MNEs from 2013 to 2022. Results from Double-Selection Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) linear regression indicate that GSCP increases the energy demand of Chinese MNEs. One possible explanation is that GSCP undermines production stability and operational efficiency, prompting firms to intensify production, extend operating hours, and adopt additional shifts to meet volatile demand conditions. Furthermore, global shocks (i.e., US-China Trade War and COVID-19) and global green initiatives (i.e., Montreal Protocol–Kigali Amendment, the EU Innovation Fund, and the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative) significantly moderate the relationship between GSCP and energy demand. The heterogeneity analysis exhibits that the GSCP impact is most pronounced among state-owned MNEs, firms with substantial overseas investment experience, and enterprises exhibiting lower degrees of internationalisation. This study contributes new empirical and theoretical insights into how global supply chain disruptions affect corporate energy demand and shape the strategic responses of Chinese MNEs.
