https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebda8.title: Towards high-resolution forecasting of tropical deforestation with deep learning
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebda8.authors: Jan Pišl, Gencer Sümbül, Gaston Lenczner et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebda8.abstract: Abstract Reducing tropical deforestation effectively requires spatially explicit data on deforestation dynamics. While past deforestation is now detected and mapped with high accuracy, producing reliable future forecasts remains a challenge. We present a deep learning approach for high-resolution deforestation forecasting in the Brazilian Amazon. We train a spatio-temporal ConvLSTM model on past deforestation maps and other covariates. Our model achieves an F1 score of 0.47 when forecasting one year ahead, substantially improving over comparable prior work. For multi-year predictions, we obtain promising results within a 3-year horizon, while sensitivity to shifts in deforestation dynamics suggests limitations for longer-term forecasts. We generate forecasts for years 2016–2018 across the Brazilian Amazon, and make them available through an interactive Google Earth Engine application. Our results demonstrate the potential for high-resolution, short- and medium-term forecasting that can support conservation efforts and help protect tropical forests.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebda9.title: Post-harvest stages account for more than half of seafood carbon footprint
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebda9.authors: Yuanchao Hu, Weiwei Lu, 张浩冉 et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebda9.abstract: Abstract Seafood is increasingly important for healthy dietary transitions in modern urban lifestyles. Yet, the patterns of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain poorly understood, which hinders the low-carbon pathways for city-specific seafood supply chains. Here, we constructed a disaggregated supply chain dataset to quantify the GHG footprint of consumption of five major seafood categories across 313 Chinese cities. In 2023, total GHG footprint of Chinese seafood consumption reached 182.6 Mt CO₂-eq (1.5% of the national total emissions), dominated by shellfish (65.7%) and fish (25.1%). Annual per-capita emissions varied from over 1000 kg CO₂-eq/capita in coastal and tourism cities to near zero in many inland cities. Spatially, 79.9% of emissions were concentrated in coastal cities, with the top five cities contributing 27.2%. Most transported seafood (58–88%) was within 200 km, indicating shorter food miles than other food categories. We find that off-farm supply chain stages, which account for 55% of total emissions, are key to retaining seafood's low-carbon advantage over terrestrial protein sources such as chicken and pork. We highlight the need for coordinated strategies to support both sustainable and healthy diets, including efficient mariculture practices in coastal cities and low-carbon cold-chain logistics and feed production in the supply chain.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb9fb.title: Adapting with justice: a governance framework for equitable urban resilience beyond the environmental justice triad
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb9fb.authors: Sarker, M., Ning, Z., Feng, W., Al Mamun, M.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb9fb.abstract: Abstract Urban adaptation can redistribute protection, public investment, land value, and displacement risk across neighborhoods and social groups. This scoping review, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, synthesized scholarship on justice, governance, and equitable urban resilience. Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language publications from January 2000 through February 2026, supplemented by backward reference checking. After duplicate removal, title/abstract screening, and full-text assessment, 79 studies were included. A combined deductive–inductive thematic synthesis, organized with MAXQDA Analytics Pro, identified three interlocking governance pillars: justice architectures, accountable co-production, and context-tuned strategies. Across the included studies, equitable adaptation was repeatedly discussed in relation to enforceable rights, distributional targeting, meaningful community authority, attention to compound and context-specific risks, anti-displacement safeguards, and durable operations and maintenance. By contrast, consultation without decision authority and adaptation investment without housing protection were described as risks for reproducing exclusion, unequal access, and climate gentrification. The review translates these patterns into five assessable governance checkpoints: rights and intergenerational accountability, distributional targeting, shared decision authority, scale and compound-risk fit, and anti-displacement protection and benefit durability. The resulting framework is an analytically derived and testable governance framework rather than a validated causal model. It provides a structured basis for evaluating whether urban adaptation is environmentally effective, socially just, institutionally accountable, and durable over time.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebaa0.title: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies rainfall in extreme compound rainfall-wave events in the NW Mediterranean
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebaa0.authors: Aguilera-Vidal, M., Wahl, T., Jiménez, J.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebaa0.abstract: Abstract The concurrent occurrence of extreme rainfall and energetic wave conditions can generate compound coastal hazards with impacts exceeding those produced by either driver alone. Although recent studies have identified changes in rainfall-wave extremes along the northwestern Mediterranean coast, whether these changes can be attributed to anthropogenic climate remains unclear. Here, we investigate the anthropogenic influence on compound rainfall-wave extremes using five initial-condition ensemble members of the CMIP6 MRI-ESM2.0 model from the Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project, comparing factual (ALL) and counterfactual (NAT) experiments over 1961–2020. Changes in dependence and joint return periods are assessed using Kendall’s τ-b and copula-based analyses. No robust anthropogenic signal is detected in the observed strengthening of rainfall-wave dependence, as neither its temporal evolution nor the change in dependence structure identified in ERA5 is consistently reproduced across the ensemble. In contrast, the ALL-NAT comparison suggests an anthropogenic contribution to rainfall intensification in the most extreme compound events, while wave changes remain small and variable across realizations. For example, fitted estimates associate a rainfall-wave combination of P24h ≈320 mm and Hs ≈4 m with joint return periods of approximately 50 years under NAT and 25 years under ALL. This comparison is indicative, with its magnitude subject to uncertainties in event sampling, marginal fitting, and copula estimation that have yet to be quantified. Agreement with ERA5 supports the model’s representation of baseline characteristics, although further evaluation would strengthen confidence in its response to external forcing. Overall, the findings suggest rainfall intensification within the model framework, while the associated frequency change should be interpreted with caution.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aead02.title: Satellite observations and energy balance constrain the thermal footprint of a hyperscale data-centre cluster
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aead02.abstract: Abstract Whether hyperscale data centres (DCs) warm their surroundings divides current evidence: a coarse-resolution satellite preprint attributes ∼2 °C of land-surface-temperature (LST) warming to facilities worldwide (Marinoni et al 2026 arXiv: 2603.20897v3 ), while peer-reviewed transects near Phoenix measure +0.7–0.9 °C of near-ground air warming a few hundred metres downwind (Sailor et al 2026 J. Eng. Sustain. Bldgs. Cities 7 024501). Prospective anthropogenic-heat models remain untested against long-term observations, and no major DC market assesses local temperature impact before construction. We provide the first ex-post, controlled satellite test for Japan’s largest DC concentration, the Inzai and Tama clusters near Tokyo, whose staggered build-out (twelve facilities, 2011–2025) yields a three-phase event study with replication. The test combines daytime Landsat (2013–2026), 70 m day/night ECOSTRESS and 1 km MODIS with matched pre-2013 controls, facility-level energy disclosures and minimum-detectable-effect analysis, gated by an air-temperature energy-balance ceiling (∼0.35 °C, cluster scale, night) that bounds LST a fortiori . Commissioning cools the daytime LST by 1.8 °C–2.2 °C—significant under all three reference types, a radiative-property signal opposite in sign to the viral claim. Deep-night facility-scale LST changes are indistinguishable from zero (bounded below ∼0.6 °C–1.2 °C), and the cluster-scale night LST bound (0.24 °C–0.29 °C, autocorrelation-corrected, two platforms) closes beneath the air-temperature ceiling. The exclusion of warming at the claimed magnitude rests primarily on energy balance—+ 2 °C, even in air, would require 6–43 times the available waste heat—with observations supplying consistent bounds at every scale they resolve. Arid- and continental-climate consistency checks (Phoenix and DeKalb) reproduce the decomposition: in both, night surface warming is largely in place during construction—before any server load—and matches neighbouring non-DC development; conversion, not exhaust. Near-source air warming is real where rejection density is high and climates dry; kilometre-scale surface warming from waste heat is unattainable. The protocol is the ex-post verification tool siting regimes lack.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb621.title: Evaluating mangrove establishment trajectories and carbon recovery potential using a spatial age-based framework
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb621.authors: Zhao, Y., Li, T., Zheng, B., Wang, X. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb621.abstract: Abstract Mangrove restoration is a vital nature-based solution for climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation. However, large-scale mangrove restoration success is predominantly evaluated using area-based metrics, which fail to capture the complex temporal trajectories of forest structural and functional recovery. Stand age directly determines structural heterogeneity and carbon stocks, making it a key indicator for monitoring recovery trajectories and estimating carbon stocks. We developed a spatial age-based framework to map established mangrove stands and quantify the existing carbon stock and remaining potential. To this end, we combined an optimized LandTrendr change-detection algorithm with age-stratified logistic growth models using Landsat time-series data. We generated a 30-m resolution age map of all established mangroves from 2000 to 2023 across tropical Hainan Island, China. Our results identified 337 ha of established mangroves as of 2023. Notably, >50% (173 ha) of the detected stands are ⩽7 years old yet have already attained 43% of mature forest carbon stocks, whereas only 4% of them have reached ⩾15 years. Under continued protection, these forests are expected to store an estimated 33 668 Mg C (27 971–38 902 Mg C), with the greatest potential concentrated in the Dongzhaigang area. Conversely, the limited extent of older forests (4% of the established area) already secures significant recovered carbon stocks, warranting urgent protection. This contrast underscores the necessity of differentiated management strategies calibrated to both restoration scale and stand development stage. Ultimately, this spatially explicit framework informs evidence-based management to improve restoration outcomes and provides actionable baselines for national carbon credit markets.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba01.title: Impact of different on-road vehicle emissions inventories on downstream air quality, exposure, health, and equity assessments
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba01.authors: Shlipak, K., Lang, V., Santiago, M., Tessum, C. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba01.abstract: Abstract Emissions from on-road vehicles are a pervasive source of air pollution, contributing to inequitable pollutant exposure and adverse health outcomes. Numerical air quality models are used to characterize traffic-related pollutant concentrations and impacts. However, model outputs rely on underlying emissions inventories whose formulations can differ substantially. Here, we leverage the widely used Intervention Model for Air Pollution (InMAP) to examine how four different on-road emissions inventories used at three different spatial resolutions (1, 1.3, and 4 km) influence simulated fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) population exposure, health impacts, and equity outcomes in a freight-heavy urban setting—the Greater Chicago Region. We find that population-weighted exposure and attributable mortality differ up to 72% and 69% across inventories, compared to only 14%–17% across resolutions. While all inventories result in higher estimated PM 2.5 exposure and mortality among Black, Hispanic, and Asian populations compared to non-Hispanic White populations, the magnitude and relative ordering of disparities across racial groups vary with both inventory choice and spatial resolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that characterizing exposure inequities using emissions colocation can yield substantially different disparity estimates (up to 20%) from pollutant concentration-based estimates due to atmospheric transport and chemistry— a divergence that likely represents a lower bound given InMAP’s reduced-complexity parameterizations. This work builds on recent studies showing that model resolution influences air quality, health, and equity assessments by demonstrating that on-road emissions inventory choice introduces even greater differences than spatial resolution.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb148.title: Modeling freshwater use for direct lithium extraction from geothermal brines in the Salton Sea
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb148.abstract: Abstract Global lithium demand is projected to more than double by 2035, to about 715 kt per year (3.8 Mt lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) per year) under the International Energy Agency Stated Policies Scenario, intensifying the need for new, sustainable extraction routes. Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal brines is of particular interest because co-location with closed-loop geothermal operations avoids the large land footprint of evaporation ponds and the carbon intensity of hard-rock mining. The Salton Sea Known Geothermal Resource Area (SS-KGRA) hosts geothermal plants with co-located pilot-scale DLE facilities and is one of the most advanced regions for geothermal lithium extraction. Though these operations are expected to reduce land and carbon intensity, they require freshwater inputs across multiple unit operations; this demand has been reported only as facility-wide aggregates, without process-level resolution, even though the SS-KGRA lies in an arid region where water supply is largely committed to agriculture. Existing estimates do not track the internal fate of process water, which determines the net volume drawn from external sources. Herein, we present LiHydroSim, a process-based model that translates publicly available process descriptions into a facility-level freshwater balance through a three-layer architecture separating gross unit-operation demand, internal recovery, and net external supply. Applied to a representative adsorption-based facility processing 7000 gallons per minute of geothermal brine, the model estimates net external freshwater demand of 1719 acre-feet per year (152 m 3 t − 1 LCE; 0.12 AF/t LCE), below the 189–355 m 3 t − 1 LCE (0.15–0.29 AF/t LCE) reported by Salton Sea developers, consistent with auxiliary demands outside the process boundary. The eluant for lithium elution dominates the water balance, accounting for 92% of gross internal process-water demand, while internal recycling offsets roughly one third of that gross demand. Total demand depends mainly on eluant volume: across two patent-specified operating modes, it ranges from 870 to 1719 acre-feet per year.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebaa1.title: Deep learning reveals severe shelterbelt degradation in eastern Ukraine due to the war
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebaa1.authors: Myroniuk, V., Khan, Y., Sovakov, O., Matsala, M. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebaa1.abstract: Abstract Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has caused extensive damage to forests, particularly in eastern and southern regions with sustained combat, where field shelterbelts have often been used as cover and subsequently heavily destroyed. This study presents a systematic region-scale assessment of pre-war shelterbelt area and war-related loss between 2021 and 2025 using 3 m PlanetScope imagery and deep learning. We evaluated three input datasets—monthly PlanetScope RGB mosaics, multiseasonal PlanetScope RGB stacks, and surface reflectance (SR) PlanetScope imagery—in combination with two semantic segmentation architectures: a convolutional U-Net with a ResNet-34 encoder and a transformer-based SegFormer with a MiT-B0 backbone. Across all input configurations, the U-Net consistently outperformed SegFormer, achieving the highest F 1 scores. Monthly RGB mosaics delivered accuracy comparable to more complex multiseasonal and SR inputs in pixel-based evaluation and are a cost-efficient option for mapping narrow shelterbelts. The RGB-based model trained on July 2021 mosaics reached an F 1 score of 0.71 and retained values of 0.58–0.67 for other months of the same leaf-on season. Temporal transfer to 2025 resulted in lower but still reasonable performance with F 1 scores of 0.53–0.63. Error-adjusted mapping estimated the shelterbelt area in 2021 at 254 ± 14.5 thousand ha, equivalent to a mean density of 2.6 ha km −2 . By 2025, this area had been reduced by approximately 41 thousand ha, or 16% of the pre-war area. Losses were strongly concentrated along frontlines where local losses exceeded 1.5 ha km −2 compared to an average loss of 0.5 ha km −2 across the entire study area. The resulting maps complement the existing forest monitoring framework in Ukraine and provide a spatially explicit basis for prioritizing post-war remediation and assessing losses in protective functions and carbon accumulation.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys..title: To VR or not to VR? Lessons learnt and future pathways for developing Virtual Reality in experimental urban research
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys..authors: Tuuli Toivonen, Elias S. Willberg, Reza Aghanejad et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys..abstract: The use of Virtual Reality (VR) in experimental urban studies is increasing rapidly. Scholars from a broad range of disciplines, such as geography, environmental psychology, urban planning, and health research, are increasingly using VR for studying peoples' preferences and behaviour in varying urban conditions. While VR provides novel possibilities for experimental research, setting up a VR environment is resource-intensive and requires careful planning across multiple phases, including project inception, environment creation, testing, empirical implementation, and packaging for later use. In this paper, we focus on aspects often left out from empirical research articles: the technical and practical decisions needed to establish a VR environment for experimental research. We synthesize lessons learnt from 13 European projects that have employed VR to investigate human preferences and behaviour in varying urban conditions. The experiences were collected from involved researchers through a survey, and the lessons and recommendations where further refined in a joint workshop. Based on this collective experience and knowledge, we discuss critical technical and administrative aspects in VR development and implementation, such as the choice between in-house versus outsourced development, the integration of realistic environmental features, minimizing cybersickness among participants, and ensuring the longevity of the project. We present a framework for VR development as part of empirical urban studies and offer concrete recommendations, with the aim to lower barriers for using VR in experimental research. We conclude by providing directions for a more scalable, collaborative, and inclusive future for VR in urban research.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2026..title: WBGT assessment in transitional urban spaces using a radiation-resolved framework extended from indoor to outdoor conditions
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2026..authors: Behrooz Khalili Nasr, Shayan Mirzabeigi, Alireza Khodayarkhani, Andrea Giovanni Mainini
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2026..abstract: Outdoor heat stress assessment in transitional urban spaces depends on spatially varying shortwave and longwave radiation, particularly under partial shading. This study extends a framework linking radiation inputs to WBGT, previously developed for indoor solar exposure, to an outdoor transitional corridor between two buildings in Milan. Hourly shortwave irradiance incident on a discretized human manikin was calculated using a geometry-resolved model accounting for direct, diffuse, transmitted, and reflected components. Time-varying exterior surface temperatures from a building energy simulation determined longwave mean radiant temperature. The shortwave and longwave components were combined through a shortwave adjustment and propagated through a tailored WBGT calculation against activity-dependent reference limits. Sensitivity was evaluated across six canopy configurations, six air speeds, three ground surfaces, and dry-bulb temperature increments of +2, +4, and +6°C. At the central position and 0.5 m/s, the share of working-hour records with no limit exceeded rose from 69.9% (no canopy) to 92.0% (opaque canopy), while the share with all limits exceeded fell from 8.4% to zero. Increasing air speed reduced WBGT exceedance most under the no-canopy condition, with a smaller effect beneath the opaque canopy. Ground-surface differences were concentrated under exposed conditions. A 90%-transmittance canopy changed exceedance little because longwave emission offset reduced shortwave exposure. Prescribed warming shifted WBGT distributions upward, while the 50%-transmittance canopy lowered exceedance at every warming level. The framework provides a common radiation-resolved screening basis linking this outdoor assessment to the previous indoor framework, without implying equivalent subjective comfort in both environments pending field validation.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ufug.2026.1297.title: Classifying type-specific green space using satellite imagery and LiDAR to assess associations with diabetes prevalence
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ufug.2026.1297.authors: Scarlett B. Rakowska, Haoxuan Ge, Matthew Adams
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ufug.2026.1297.abstract: Abstract Urban green space is often measured by using greenness indices, such as the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, but these indices do not distinguish among green space types. This study integrated 3-metre spatial resolution multispectral imagery and LiDAR-derived normalized Digital Surface Models (nDSM) to classify type-specific green spaces across Mississauga, Ontario, and examine their associations with diabetes prevalence. We tested eight combinations of spectral bands, vegetation and water indices, and structural data using an object-based random forest and found that the best-performing model included all the bands, indices, and nDSM, achieving 88% overall classification accuracy. The classification identified deciduous trees, coniferous trees, shrubs, grass, and marsh/wetland, which were then linked to census tract-level diabetes prevalence using local and neighbourhood beta regression models by sex and age group, and adjusted for socioeconomic covariates. Deciduous trees, coniferous trees, and shrubs were more consistently associated with lower diabetes prevalence, particularly among adults aged 45 years and older. NDVI-based models showed weaker associations with diabetes prevalence after adjustment, while type-specific models retained associations. These findings suggest that type-specific green space and structure provide more informative measures of exposure than greenness alone. Integrating high spatial resolution multispectral imagery and LiDAR provides a methodological framework for health research examining relationships between urban green space and chronic diseases.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70388.title: The Aftermath of Almost: Communicating Risk Amid Community Narratives of Near Misses
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70388.authors: Ray, E., Schramm, A., Merle, P.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70388.abstract: ABSTRACT Unpredictable weather means that serious threats do not always unfold as forecast. Hurricane near misses create an especially challenging communication context: The absence of harm may invite community explanations that make the event feel less threatening, even as future risk persists. This study examines how community narratives and post‐event risk messages shape risk perception, collective efficacy, preparedness intentions, message sharing, and credibility after hurricane near misses. In an online experiment, Florida residents ( N = 405) viewed social media posts about a hurricane that shifted away from a coastal community. The posts varied by explanation type, comparing a symbolic community narrative with a factual account, and by response source, comparing emergency management, peer, and control messages. Results show limits and leverage points for post‐event risk communication: In the primary analysis, neither community narratives nor risk messages significantly shifted perceived risk; however, supplementary analyses accounting for regional residence revealed a small reduction in perceived risk following narrative exposure. Risk messages increased sharing and collective efficacy, and organizational sources were more credible than peer sources. These findings suggest that post‐event risk communication after near misses may not readily recalibrate individual risk perceptions but can shape how risk information circulates and how communities perceive their capacity to respond. The study advances understanding of near misses as ambiguous risk events in which communication matters even when harm does not occur.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70398.title: Identification and Governance Strategy of Urban Systemic Risk Induced by Extreme Rain–Snow–Ice Weather in Southern China
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70398.abstract: ABSTRACT China's rapid urbanization has expanded urban spatial scale and increased the concentration of population, wealth, and infrastructure. Against the background of climate change, urban systemic risk induced by extreme rain–snow–ice weather (USR–RSI) in southern China has repeatedly disrupted critical infrastructure and public services, generating cascading impacts across interconnected urban systems. This study examines the generation and evolution of USR–RSI and develops a corresponding resilience governance strategy. Building on conceptual analysis, complex network theory and system vulnerability theory are integrated to construct the theoretical framework. A causal loop diagram is used to characterize risk diffusion and feedback mechanisms based on the 2008 and 2024 RSI disaster cases. Semi‐structured interviews and documentary materials are further analyzed using a structured data analysis approach to identify sensitivity and adaptive factors associated with node and path vulnerability. On the basis of these findings, a whole‐process resilience governance framework is proposed, covering resilience construction, integration of warning and response, rapid recovery, and long‐term adaptive optimization and transformative reconfiguration. The study provides an empirical and analytical basis for understanding and governing USR–RSI from the perspective of interconnected urban socio‐technical systems.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70378.title: Risk‐Oriented Differentiated Governance for Ambiguous Information
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70378.authors: Ni, P., Zhu, J., Zhang, H.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70378.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has led to an exponential increase in false information, especially ambiguous information. Hampered by resource constraints, conventional governance approaches fall short of enabling efficient and precise risk management. In response, this paper innovatively proposes a risk‐oriented tiered governance framework tailored to ambiguous information. Specifically, we quantify epistemic uncertainty via multi‐level semantic features, combine it with network propagation features to determine latent influence scores, and construct a risk function capturing their synergy. Critical and acceptable boundaries are introduced to categorize ambiguous information into discrete risk levels, tier‐specific governance strategies are devised, and a propagation throttling (limiting each user's successful forwards per ambiguous information) strategy is innovatively proposed for medium‐risk information. Finally, we simulate differentiated governance strategies across risk levels of ambiguous information, systematically assess governance effectiveness, and offer a comparative discussion grounded in fairness and ethics. This study offers an operational analytical framework for refined risk governance of ambiguous information, contributes methodological innovations in risk quantification modeling and tiered governance strategies, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for risk management authorities in designing differentiated measures.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70401.title: Hybrid Semi‐Quantitative Risk Assessment for Aging Offshore Platforms: A HAZOP–FMEA–Bow‐Tie Framework With Sensitivity Analysis and KRI‐Based Governance
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70401.authors: Saleem, M., Baseer, M., Tariq, Q., Khan, A.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70401.abstract: ABSTRACT Aging offshore installations increasingly operate beyond their original design life, yet conventional periodic risk assessments capture barrier degradation only intermittently. This study presents a barrier‐conditioned semi‐quantitative risk‐assessment workflow that integrates Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and bow‐tie barrier analysis. The workflow combines decomposed residual likelihood and consequence scoring with threshold‐stability testing and a Key Risk Indicator (KRI)‐based update rule. Its principal contribution is the governance linkage: an explicit rule set that maps barrier condition and KRI threshold breaches to changes in residual likelihood, residual consequence, and risk band between formal safety‐case reviews. To ensure transparency and reproducibility, the workflow is demonstrated through a fully synthetic scenario representing a life‐extended semi‐submersible installation; all inputs are constructed and explicitly identified throughout as scenario assumptions. Under the illustrative scoring assumptions, a 19‐hazard register spanning seven hazard categories yields two high, nine medium, and eight low residual risks, with blowout/well‐control failure and hydrogen sulfide release remaining the highest residual risks. Per‐perturbation threshold‐stability analysis and distribution‐based Monte Carlo propagation indicate that 16 of the 19 residual risk ratings are sensitive to classification boundaries, suggesting that the reported scores should be interpreted as central estimates subject to uncertainty. The proposed workflow provides a transparent tool for risk screening and governance support, complementing full quantitative risk assessment (QRA) while preserving its essential analytical role.

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02776.title: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02776.authors: Laura Gibbs, CHRIS D. JONES, ﻿Colin Jones et al.
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02776.abstract: Abstract When anthropogenic CO 2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. The resulting global temperature change, the zero emissions commitment, is central to carbon budget assessments and understanding reversibility of global warming, yet its dependence on prior warming levels remains unclear. Here we show, using zero-emission simulations with the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.2) across global warming levels of 1.5–5 K, that the zero emissions commitment stays near zero up to 2 K but becomes positive at higher warming levels, reaching 0.4–0.6 K after ~ 150 years. This dependence indicates that stabilizing or reversing warming becomes progressively more difficult as peak temperature rises. We identify the mechanism behind this behaviour: stronger warming from higher radiative disequilibrium and weakening carbon sinks, driven by saturated land carbon uptake and the reduced radiative impact of CO 2 drawdown at higher background CO 2 concentrations. Higher peak warming therefore commits the planet to additional warming, limiting temperature-overshoot reversibility.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08490.title: Hurricane disturbance leads to elevated wildfire activity in the Gulf Coast region U.S.A.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08490.authors: Harper Steele, Richard S. Vachula, Peter C. Ryan
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08490.abstract: Abstract Building on long-standing hypotheses of a hurricane-fire interaction, this study assesses empirical evidence for hurricane-driven increases in wildfire activity along the Gulf Coast of the United States. It has been proposed that wildfire risk is elevated post-hurricane due to increased fuel accumulation and alterations to forest microclimates associated with treefall (e.g., increased radiation, temperature, aridity). While isolated studies have identified evidence supporting this relationship using premodern proxy data, an analysis using modern empirical data is lacking. This study addresses this gap by using spatial analysis of contemporary hurricane and wildfire data to evaluate changes in wildfire activity following hurricane landfall events. Thirty hurricanes that made landfall between 1992 and 2019 (Category 1 to 5) were analyzed alongside wildfire data surrounding their path of destruction from the five years before and after each storm. In the five years after hurricanes, increases were seen in both the number of wildfires and total area burned, though spatial and temporal variation are apparent along the coastline. Of the three subregions studied, the Florida Peninsula experienced the largest increase in wildfire activity, primarily in the two and three years following hurricanes. Wildfire activity following select hurricanes is compared to fire weather index data to ensure observed trends are attributable to hurricane damage rather than background climatic factors. These results support the hypothesis of a hurricane-fire interaction and demonstrate that hurricanes continue to influence Gulf Coast fire regimes in the modern era, despite widespread fire suppression and prescribed burning efforts.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08456.title: Transferable machine learning prediction of urban pluvial flood water depth using multi-resolution digital elevation models
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08456.authors: Babak Razdar, Ilenia Manco, Pasquale Giovanni Schiano et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08456.abstract: Abstract Machine learning methods, particularly Random Forest (RF), present an effective solution for predicting urban pluvial flood water depth, especially in data-scarce regions where traditional hydrological and hydraulic observations are lacking. This study proposes a DEM-centric RF framework for predicting spatially continuous urban flood water depth across various precipitation return periods, emphasizing its robustness to terrain resolution degradation and spatial transferability. The model is trained and validated in Milan using a 1 m LiDAR-derived DEM and evaluated with a coarser 5 m EU-DEM to assess sensitivity to reduced resolution. Transferability is tested by applying the trained model to Cologne using independent 1 m LiDAR data. Model performance is assessed across five precipitation scenarios (5–100-year return periods) using absolute error metrics, tolerance thresholds, spatial diagnostics, and confidence-stratified analyses. Results show stable performance, with mean absolute errors below 0.30 m and over 58% of grid cells within ± 0.25 m of reference flood depths. Prediction errors are mainly found in hydraulically complex areas, while the majority of the urban domain shows well-constrained predictions. Confidence diagnostics indicate that high- and very-high-confidence predictions comply with tolerance thresholds under both DEM resolution degradation and spatial transfer. These findings suggest that relative terrain structure governs urban pluvial flooding patterns, enabling reliable flood depth predictions with medium-resolution DEMs. This framework offers a scalable tool for urban flood screening, hazard assessment, and climate adaptation planning in areas with limited data.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08499.title: Synoptic analysis and WRF sensitivity experiments of SACZ-driven extreme rainfall over Petropolis, Brazil
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08499.authors: Miguel Amoedo, Fabrício Polifke da Silva
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08499.abstract: Abstract Extreme rainfall in the mountainous region of Petrópolis (Brazil) is frequently associated with South Atlantic Convergence Zone (SACZ) episodes, low-level moisture, and complex terrain. Despite its operational relevance, the sensitivity of numerical forecasts to physical parameterizations under these high-impact environments remains poorly understood. This study evaluates the performance of the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model for five SACZ-driven extreme rainfall events using a 27–9–3 km nested configuration and an ensemble of 64 combinations of microphysics and cumulus schemes. A two-stage verification approach was applied, combining spatial qualitative assessment and quantitative metrics based on mean error, hourly root mean squared error (RMSE), temporal correlation, covariance, and POD–FAR diagnostics. The configurations highlighted in the spatial and temporal rainfall comparisons combined Ferrier microphysics (M5) with Tiedtke (C6) for 01–02 January 2012 and with New Simplified Arakawa–Schubert (C14) for 17–18 March 2013; WRF single-moment 5-class microphysics (M4) with New Tiedtke (C16) was highlighted for 08 March 2014. The 3-km grid generally preserves the shape of cumulative rainfall, but the mean daily bias changes from − 18 mm at 27 km to + 8 mm at 9 km and + 13 mm at 3 km. The present comparisons do not isolate the physical source of the 3-km bias. The findings demonstrate that the evaluated configurations and grid spacing both affect precipitation estimates for these five SACZ-related events. This study highlights key sources of uncertainty in operational forecasting over southeastern Brazil and provides guidance for optimizing physics configurations in similar mountainous, moisture-rich environments.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.title: Evaluating urban street views through collective emotional perception from multimodal social media cityscape posts: An R-ECoT-based interpretable framework
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.authors: Jianyu Fu, Xukang Wang, Jue Ma et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.abstract: Urban street views shape everyday urban experience, yet their assessment still relies largely on researcher-defined indicators and structured elicitation, with limited use of naturally occurring public responses. This study develops an interpretable framework that transforms social-media image–comment interactions into eight-dimensional collective emotional appraisals of urban scenes. Under approved access, 1078 Facebook and Instagram cityscape posts and 20,546 comments were retrieved through the SOMAR Virtual Data Enclave. Comment-derived Plutchik labels were assessed through human validation and robustness tests, then used as weak supervision for R-ECoT, which jointly predicts emotion intensities and generates emotion-specific grounding maps from images. The trained CLIP-based model was applied to 610,017 ZENRIN street-view images in Setagaya Ward, Tokyo, and predictions were aggregated to 10 m road segments. Comment-derived labels agreed more closely with an independent post-level human reference than the strongest image-only estimate (Pearson 0.818 versus 0.751). CLIP-R-ECoT achieved the best performance in hierarchical benchmarks, with a KL divergence of 0.329, an MSE of 0.0106, and a balanced accuracy of 0.757. Its grounding maps showed greater random-corrected masking faithfulness than Grad-CAM (0.083 versus 0.049), higher perturbation stability, and lower spatial fragmentation. Street-level mapping revealed differentiated emotional patterns, while emotion-specific high-response regions in the images were associated with distinct semantic, color-atmospheric, and depth-structural attributes. By converting dispersed public reactions into spatially continuous and interpretable evidence, the framework supports fine-grained streetscape screening, helps identify locations warranting closer inspection, and directs design attention toward the visible conditions associated with different public responses.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02485.title: Forest landscapes determine their pests: jack pine budworm spatial dynamics under host scarcity
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02485.authors: Barry J. Cooke, Brian R. Sturtevant, Dan Kneeshaw et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02485.abstract: Abstract Context Jack pine budworm (JPBW), Choristoneura pinus pinus, is a major defoliator in Canada, yet remains absent from theoretical discourse on outbreak synchrony, despite sharing key life history traits with the archetypal “cross-scale” pest, spruce budworm (C. fumiferana). JPBW has primarily been studied in host-rich landscapes, raising questions about its behavior in host-sparse regions. Objectives We asked whether scale-crossing JPBW outbreaks are contingent on host density, and whether reduced outbreak incidence in host-sparse landscapes reflects synchronized or desynchronized population limitation. Methods We applied a systematic framework for analyzing spatiotemporal tree-ring data, adapted from recent reconstructions of spruce budworm and forest tent caterpillar. This framework integrates temporal and spatial methods to evaluate periodicity, coherence, and landscape-scale synchrony. Results In the pine-sparse Border Lakes region (~30,000 km 2 ), we identified 14 growth disturbances between 1910 and 2006, typically recurring every seven years and affecting 30% of trees annually at peak. Reanalysis of data from a host-rich site in Manitoba confirmed strong correspondence between JPBW defoliation and growth reductions. Nine episodes in the host-rich site coincided with published outbreaks, whereas signals in the host-sparse Border Lakes remained spatially variable and weakly correlated across sample areas. Conclusions Despite high fecundity and dispersal potential, JPBW in host-sparse landscapes behaves endemically. Pest status, we argue, is not a fixed insect trait but an emergent property of host availability and spatial scale. The JPBW system constitutes a third example from the Border Lakes region where the “catastrophe” theory of outbreak origin is more consistent with data than a “clockwork” theory of spatially synchronized cycling.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Non-land-use forcing significantly drives projected trends of atmospheric black carbon over Africa: Implications for mitigation strategies
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Matthews Nyasulu, Genesis Magara, Fabiano Gibson Daud Thulu et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Black carbon (BC) plays a critical role in climate forcing and poses significant health risks, yet its trends and drivers remain poorly constrained across Africa. Here, we quantify the relative contributions of land-use and non-land-use forcing to the projected trends of BC using the Meteorological Research Institute Earth System Model version 2.0 (MRI-ESM2-0) under the Aerosol Chemistry Model Intercomparison Project (AerChemMIP). A variance decomposition framework is applied to SSP370SST and SSP370SST-SSP126Lu simulations to isolate land-use from non-land-use forcing. The MRI-ESM2-0 model reproduces spatial patterns well (r > 0.8, p < 0.05), although spatially heterogeneous biases persist over Central Africa. Elevated BC concentration (>0.7 μg m −3 ) occurs in Central and West Africa, while low (<0.1) concentrations occur in parts of North Africa and the island of Madagascar. Projected trends reveal a statistically significant increase in BC (p < 0.05) over North and West Africa, whereas Central and Southern Africa show decreasing trends in BC until 2100. The projected trends are primarily driven by non-land-use emissions, with the influence of hydroclimatic changes, while land-use forcing is most pronounced in Central and Southern Africa. These findings highlight the need for region-specific mitigation strategies to control future BC concentrations across Africa effectively.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Interactions among land use, climate, leaf litter traits, and consumers shape large-scale patterns of decomposition in streams of SW Europe
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Diana Rojo, Javier Pérez, Naiara López‐Rojo et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Habitat degradation is one of the primary drivers of biodiversity loss and ecosystem alteration. In streams, leaf litter decomposition plays a key role in energy and nutrient cycling, which is influenced by leaf litter quality, microbial and invertebrate consumers, and environmental conditions. Land use changes alter stream habitats and can modify decomposition rates and dynamics, but large-scale assessments of these anthropogenic impacts remain limited. We explored the consequences of major land use changes (tree plantations, agricultural land, and urban settlements) on stream ecosystems by comparing sites in human-impacted catchments with reference unimpacted sites (i.e., surrounded by native vegetation) across several regions of southwestern Europe encompassing a wide climatic gradient. We quantified decomposition rates of multiple leaf litter types to evaluate the interaction between leaf litter traits and environmental variation, exploring changes in associated invertebrate assemblages. Overall, land use changes reduced total and microbial decomposition rates, with agriculture exerting the strongest effects, and caused marked shifts in invertebrate assemblages including replacement of sensitive by tolerant species and reduced detritivore richness, mainly in urban streams. Climatic variability seemed to modulate these responses, with seasonal climates showing higher vulnerability to impacts. Lastly, leaf litter types differed in their sensitivity to detect degradation, although no consistent trait-based patterns were observed. Our results show that land use changes alter stream ecosystems across climatic gradients, highlighting the urgent need to integrate environmental and biological drivers across spatial scales in watershed management and to provide actionable baselines to optimize riparian restoration and buffer the effects of ongoing climate change.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Operationalising connectivity in the spatial management of mangroves
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Gabriela Thompson-Saud, Séverine Choukroun, Adam Douglas Canning et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Mangroves form highly interconnected ecosystems, where natural rehabilitation often relies on propagule dispersal to recolonise degraded or fragmented areas where suitable hydrological and substrate conditions exist. Yet, dispersal and connectivity are rarely integrated in the spatial planning of mangroves due to limited data and a lack of operational guidance. To address this gap, we developed and tested a decision support framework that integrates mangrove connectivity and condition to guide spatial management prioritisation. Using the central Great Barrier Reef, Queensland (Australia) as a case study, we simulated dispersal of two mangrove species: Rhizophora stylosa and Bruguiera gymnorhiza, using a biophysical model driven by oceanographic currents (SLIM) and parameterised using experimentally derived propagule viability and floating duration data (IBM). Network analysis was applied to the dispersal outputs to identify mangrove sub-population importance (centrality) and key dispersal pathways that sustain connectivity processes. Habitat patches defined by five connectivity-driven management objectives were then mapped and assessed alongside satellite-derived mangrove condition (NDVI) to generate an urgency index for spatial management prioritisation. Our results identified critical areas of replenishment sources or connectivity corridors that overlapped with degraded mangrove habitats, highlighting these areas for targeted management. This framework demonstrates how explicitly incorporating connectivity into spatial planning can improve the identification of areas that may contribute to mangrove recovery and persistence under accelerating climate change and coastal development.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: Classifying perceived shaking in post-earthquake social media with large language models for rapid estimation of seismic intensity-affected areas
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.authors: Qingle Cheng, Zhengxuan Song, Maosen Yang, Linlin Xie
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: Rapidly characterizing the spatial extent of earthquake impacts and perceived shaking is essential for emergency response and seismic-intensity assessment. Although social media can provide abundant public feedback shortly after an earthquake, its colloquial, noisy, and sparsely geolocated content is difficult to translate into reliable impact indicators. To address the scarcity of publicly available annotated Chinese post-earthquake social media data, the limited cross-event generalization testing of existing classification models, and the insufficient integration of classification outputs with seismic-intensity estimation, this study developed a Chinese post-earthquake social media dataset containing more than 64,000 annotated Weibo comments from 12 selected earthquakes. A four-level perceived-shaking text classifier based on DeepSeek-7B and task-specific low-rank adaptation (LoRA) was developed and evaluated using an independent-event test and multiple leave-one-event-out tests. A population-adjusted perceived-shaking label index was further constructed to support rapid estimation of seismic intensity-affected areas. On the independent test set, the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 91.34%, a weighted-average F1-score of 91.40%, and a macro-average F1-score of 89.78%, outperforming conventional machine-learning models, BERT-based models, and a zero-shot large language model. Across the multiple event tests, the macro-average F1-score ranged from 0.898 to 0.980. Compared with unclassified social media indicators, the classified perceived-shaking label indices provided better estimates of intensity-zone areas. Perceived-shaking information accumulated primarily within the first 30 min after an earthquake. The task-fine-tuned model effectively converts noisy public feedback into interpretable indicators, providing complementary support for rapid preliminary estimation of seismic intensity-affected areas.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: Bottom-up estimates of population exposure and damage from floods: A case study on Malawi's 2015 floods
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.authors: Simon Peter Ngorok, Thomas K. J. McDermott, Jeremy S. Pal
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: Despite the growing impacts of floods worldwide, data on their economic damages remain limited. For the universe of flood events that occur worldwide, only a subset enter standard databases such as the Emergency Events Database, and only a fraction have damage estimates. Filling this gap matters for local flood risk assessment, adaptation planning, and better accounting of climate change effects, particularly in developing countries. This paper adapts and extends the Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment Framework and Toolbox (CLIMAAX) workflow to estimate localised population exposure and direct damage from flood events. The workflow integrates the three components of flood risk: hazard, with water depths reconstructed from a satellite-derived flood extent using terrain data; exposure, from building footprints and gridded population layers; and vulnerability, through depth-damage functions. Applied to Malawi’s 2015 floods, the workflow yields rapid, localised estimates of structural damage and exposed populations in a data-scarce setting. A Radarsat-2 flood extent generated from a humanitarian emergency activation underpins the preferred estimate. The analysis indicates approximately 124,000 people exposed and direct structural damage to buildings and their contents of US$312 million (2015 US$). At matched sectoral scope, structure-only estimates of US$117–166 million bracket the US$136 million housing-sector damage reported in Malawi’s Post-Disaster Needs Assessment. Sensitivity analysis, including calibration against unit costs derived from the assessment, shows that valuation assumptions shift aggregate damages while leaving the spatial pattern of losses broadly unchanged. These bottom-up estimates complement ground-truthed post-disaster assessments and media reporting and help paint a richer picture of flood impacts.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfe.abstract: Abstract Working with societal stakeholders is vital in addressing the adaptation limits and impacts of climate overshoots (exceeding the 1.5°C global warming limit). To achieve this, the paper argues that research on climate overshoots needs to be grounded in diverse methodologies that open possibilities for non-scientists to bring on board knowledge that is valuable in terms of depth (in each societal context) and comparability (across societal contexts). A reflexive approach to addressing climate overshoot impacts is proposed with the aim of shining light on how stakeholder contributions can be incorporated in projections and response actions (Singletary and Sterle, 2020; Dobre and Faldi, 2025).

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcff.title: HydroSPI-ARX for explainable multi-scale drought early warning over Türkiye from ERA5 and ERA5-Land reanalyses
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcff.abstract: Abstract Machine-learning drought studies typically regress a smooth, autocorrelated index at single stations and report near-perfect fits. Temporal leakage is rarely controlled, and the skill the index already carries in its own history is rarely separated out. Here we present HydroSPI-ARX, an autoregressive and explainable framework for drought early warning over Türkiye. It recasts the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) as a leakage-controlled, lead-resolved classification target built from ERA5 and ERA5-Land hydroclimatic fields. Five drought targets are evaluated at leads of one, three, six and twelve months, with feature selection and scaling recomputed inside every training fold. The moderate-or-worse warning reaches a macro-F1 of 0.853 one month ahead, 0.794 at three months and 0.709 at six months. At twelve months it falls to 0.486, where no configuration retains skill. Naive persistence is ahead at one month; against it the framework gains 0.038 macro-F1 at three months and 0.066 at six, with year-block bootstrap intervals that exclude zero. Against a per-cell linear autoregression on the index's own memory, the gain is measurable only at six months (0.043, 95% interval 0.010 to 0.078). Exogenous hydroclimatic fields add 0.007 at one month and nothing beyond. Skill is therefore carried by the multi-scale memory of the index, and the learned model earns its place at the six-month horizon. Scoring the same held-out forecasts against station-derived labels lowers agreement (Cohen's kappa of 0.30, 0.26 and 0.21 at one, three and six months). The ranking of the forecasts survives, so the advantage is not an artefact of verifying against the same reanalysis. ERA5 and ERA5-Land are equivalent within a margin of 0.02 macro-F1 set in advance, and a model trained without a climate zone still forecasts inside it. A Mann-Kendall analysis shows rising three-month drought frequency over 1981 to 2025.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfb.title: Delayed seasonal march of East Asian summer monsoonal rain belt during Heinrich Stadials
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfb.authors: Jinzhe Zhang, Ting Wei, Chuncheng Guo, Qing You Yan
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfb.abstract: Abstract The timing and duration of monsoon rainfall shape regional hydroclimate, yet their response to abrupt climate change remains poorly constrained. Here, we use 25-km-resolution climate simulations to investigate the seasonal migration of the East Asian summer monsoon rain belt during Heinrich Stadials, periods associated with collapsed Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC). We find that the rain belt migrated northward 18 days later than during interstadials. This delay kept the monsoon front longer over central China, prolonging early-summer rainfall despite an overall weaker monsoon. The delayed migration was linked to later northward advances of the western North Pacific subtropical high and upper-level westerly jet. North Atlantic cooling contributed to these circulation changes through Rossby wave propagation and a weakened land–sea thermal contrast. Our results suggest that abrupt Atlantic changes can reshape both the amount and seasonal timing of East Asian summer rainfall. These findings offer a palaeoclimate perspective on potential changes in monsoon seasonality under future AMOC weakening.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfd.title: A scoping review of psychosocial factors of climate change inaction: Implications for climate change communication and education
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfd.authors: Nicole M. Ardoin, Alison W. Bowers, Kathleen O’Connor, Marcia McKenzie
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfd.abstract: Abstract Climate change communication and education efforts often focus on the cognitive aspects of addressing climate change, emphasizing that a key path to solving climate change-related challenges may be achieved through an educated public that better understands the science of this issue. However, despite decades of information-heavy communication and education efforts, designed with knowledge-related outcomes in mind, meaningful and sustained action to address climate change has yet to occur at a broad scale. This lack of effective, sustained action has motivated researchers from a range of fields to examine other factors that prevent climate change action. We undertook a systematic scoping review of peer-reviewed, empirical studies (n = 92) focusing on psychological and sociological (psychosocial) factors associated with climate change inaction. Through thematic analysis, we identified trends and patterns across the studies, but also noted that no obvious list of discrete psychosocial factors leading to climate inaction emerged. Political ideology and emotions were the most common factors discussed as influencing climate change inaction. Other psychosocial factors receiving notable attention included climate change perceptions, trust in institutions and leaders, values, and efficacy beliefs. The most-recommended strategies for improving effectiveness of climate change communication and education were attending to climate-related emotions; addressing issues of ideology and trust; and targeting systemic and structural barriers. Findings also emphasize that quality climate communication and education must acknowledge and build on people's unique relationships with their places, communities, and stories.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfc.title: Structuring decision-making for systemic climate-financial risk.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfc.authors: Tanya Fiedler, Monica Trezise, A. J. Pitman, Ben Rhodri Newell
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebcfc.abstract: Abstract Physical climate risks are a source of vulnerability in financial systems, yet existing risk measurement approaches struggle to translate them into decision-relevant metrics, reflecting a mismatch between how climate risk evolves and how financial risk is assessed. Drawing on workshops and interviews with 35 finance and risk professionals (33 from a large financial institution, two from a global insurance broker), we identify six interacting risk domains through which physical climate risk cascades to credit loss, creating decision bottlenecks where routine practice breaks down. Integrating storylines and dynamic adaptive policy pathways, we develop a qualitative–analytical framework that allows decisions to proceed within these bottlenecks. Whereas scenario analysis and stress testing estimate losses under specified futures, the storylines developed here trace how risk reaches the portfolio through the responses of insurers, households and regulators and the institution itself. The pathways identify which signals to monitor and when to reconsider action, organising risk appetite as sequences of contingent actions. Because its effects lack historical precedent and a robust link to default, emerge gradually and often unseen across interacting domains, and rebound on the institution through the responses its own actions provoke, climate-financial risk is as much a problem of decision structuring and adaptive governance as of measurement.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebd00.title: Significant albedo-induced cooling effects across tropical and subtropical dryland biomes
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebd00.authors: Hongze Pei, Jieming Chou, Chaoyang Wang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebd00.abstract: Abstract Terrestrial ecosystems can significantly regulate climate through carbon uptake and alterations in surface albedo. However, current climate mitigation assessments largely focus on carbon sinks while overlooking albedo-induced radiative effects. We developed an integrated framework to quantify the net climate effect of global terrestrial ecosystems from 2001 to 2019 by combining net ecosystem productivity with albedo-induced radiative forcing. We estimated the Net Equivalent Carbon Dioxide Stock Change (NESC), which incorporates both Net Cumulative Carbon uptake Equivalent (NCCE) and the Emission Equivalent of Shortwave Forcing (EESF). Results show that global terrestrial ecosystems generated a net cooling effect of 397.52 Gt CO2e during the study period. Among biomes, tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas and shrublands, and deserts and xeric shrublands, contributed a cooling effect of 95.33 Gt CO2e due to increased albedo, nearly one-quarter of the total NCCE across the 14 biomes, largely driven by declines in photosynthetic vegetation and soil drying in Land use and land cover (LULC) non-conversion areas. These findings provide new perspectives for re-evaluating the climate value of terrestrial ecosystems and a scientific basis for incorporating surface albedo into future nature-based solutions for climate mitigation.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aea352.title: GEDI spaceborne lidar for protected areas monitoring
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aea352.authors: Cotrina-Sanchez, A., Moudry, V., Laurin, G., Coomes, D. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aea352.abstract: Abstract Protected areas (PAs) are the cornerstone of global terrestrial biodiversity conservation, yet systematic, scalable assessment of their vegetation structural condition remains limited. NASA’s Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI), a spaceborne full-waveform lidar mission, offers a unique opportunity to consistently quantify vegetation structure within PA boundaries at near-global scales. This review synthesises 45 peer-reviewed studies published between January 2018 and May 2026 that use GEDI to study PAs within 26 countries on five continents. Estimates of canopy height, canopy cover, and vertical structure from GEDI’s L2A and L2B products were most widely used. Aboveground biomass density was also frequently derived, often through L4A or multi-sensor modelling. Studies of vegetation structure, carbon storage, methodological integration and multi-sensor fusion dominate the evidence base, while analyses of disturbance, biodiversity proxies, and PA effectiveness remain more limited, with only 16 studies addressing these topics. Most studies combine GEDI with optical imagery, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), airborne lidar and spaceborne lidar, field plots, or terrestrial laser scanning to support spatial mapping and validation. GEDI-derived structural metrics can support monitoring under the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Paris Agreement, and biodiversity assessments led by the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), including reporting aligned with the Essential Biodiversity Variables (EBV) framework. However, this review shows that their operational use still requires stronger biodiversity linkages, clearer validation protocols, and better testing across ecosystems. Future research could further strengthen PA monitoring by integrating GEDI with new SAR and forthcoming lidar missions, and analyses using geospatial foundation models.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ae962b.title: Increase of tropical cyclone-induced coastal flooding due to historical sea level rise
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ae962b.authors: Mengel, M., Sauer, I., Otto, C., Treu, S. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ae962b.abstract: Abstract Surges from tropical cyclones (TCs) cause significant damage in coastal areas. However, the contribution of historical sea level rise (SLR) to surge heights and thus the flooded areas has not been quantified on a global scale. Here, we use an open-source shallow water equation solver to estimate the impact of historical SLR on coastal flooding induced by all historical TCs with landfall from 1950 to 2025, according to the International Best Tracks Archive. We isolate the SLR effect through the comparison of factual simulations accounting for observed changes in sea level to counterfactual simulations without long term trends in sea levels. Results show that SLR has steadily increased the coastal area affected by TC-induced surges, from about 5% in 1950–1954 assuming mean tide levels (7% and 5% for minimum and maximum tide levels, respectively) to about 18% in 2021–2025 (22% and 13% for minimum and maximum tide levels, respectively) in comparison to the areas affected without SLR. The increase differs along coastlines, with maxima in relative increases of surge flooding along the North American Atlantic coastline and the Southeast Asian coastline. To put the numbers into perspective, we also estimate the associated increases assuming 1 m of local SLR and no changes in TC tracks and wind fields, reaching 146% under mean tide assumptions (192% for minimum tide levels and 92% for maximum tide levels). Results show that this is higher than expected assuming a linear relationship between SLR and relative increases in flood extents. Our analysis demonstrates the significant increase in flood extent induced by SLR already today. The generated data sets of factual and counterfactual coastal flooding extend ISIMIP3a climate-related forcing data, allowing for the evaluation and attribution of additional coastal impacts.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aea9ad.title: Evaluating inter- and intra-regional air pollution inequalities in a decarbonized world
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aea9ad.authors: Sampedro, J., Rodés-Bachs, C., Van de Ven, D., Tonne, C. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aea9ad.abstract: Abstract Ambient PM 2.5 exposure remains a major global health challenge. While pollution has declined in developed economies, it has increased in developing regions, exacerbating cross-country inequalities. Within-country disparities have narrowed in some contexts but remain significant. This study assesses how these inequalities evolve under alternative decarbonization futures, co-designed with stakeholders and aligned with current climate policy. Using an integrated assessment and air quality modelling framework, we find that international inequality in mortality burden widens over time even as income inequality across countries narrows, and that a country’s emission contribution is only moderately associated with its own exposure burden, driven more by aggregate scale than per-capita intensity. Within countries, wealthier deciles disproportionately drive emissions, but the contribution-exposure relationship shows no consistent direction, and exposure inequality itself varies enormously by country independent of income. These findings call for climate policies explicitly integrated with air quality, health, and equity objectives, tailored to where responsibility and impact diverge across scales.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb81e.title: Initial affect shapes risk-benefit information processing and public support for carbon dioxide removal technologies
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb81e.authors: van Veen, J., Rahmani Azad, Z., Wong Parodi, G., Hahnel, U.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb81e.abstract: Abstract Given the accelerating climate crisis, carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies are becoming increasingly important, while public support may play a relevant role in their implementation. This support is influenced by how citizens inform themselves about the technology. While prior research has examined public support under conditions of no or predefined information provision, little is known about the factors that shape how individuals actively select information about CDR and integrate it into their preferences about the technology. Here, we investigate how initial affect towards CDR shapes laypersons’ selection and evaluation of benefit-related versus risk-related information about the technology and how these processes influence subsequent policy support. In a preregistered study with 714 U.S. participants, we introduced a novel information-sampling task, in which participants could freely choose which information about CDR to attend to, followed by a policy choice experiment assessing public support of CDR technologies. In line with our hypotheses, participants’ initial affect influenced their information search: more initial positive affect towards CDR was associated with a higher likelihood to select benefit-related versus risk-related information about CDR. This confirmatory information search, in turn, was associated with immediate changes in affect towards the technology, especially when the information was perceived as persuasive. These affective changes across information search carried over to subsequent decisions to support climate policies in general and policy portfolios including CDR in particular. Overall, our findings highlight the reciprocal relationship between affect, endogenous information search, and support for CDR technologies.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb682.title: Incivility in public health policy discussions spills over to public engagement with climate issues: evidence from English-language social media
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb682.authors: Narimanzadeh, H., Badie-Modiri, A., Smirnova, I., Chen, T.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb682.abstract: Abstract Affective polarization and political sorting drive public antagonism around climate change and other issues at the science-policy nexus. We study cross-domain spillover of incivility in public engagements with climate change and public health on English-language Twitter and Reddit using the COVID-19 period as a case study. To assess whether spillover exists between these two policy domains, we examined how the incivility of climate discussions on social media varied by their co-occurrence with COVID-19 content and temporal coincidence with pandemic events. We find strong evidence of the signatures of affective polarization surrounding COVID-19 spilling into the climate change domain. Across different social media systems, COVID-19 content is associated with incivility in climate discussions. These patterns of increased antagonism were responsive to pandemic events that made the link between science and public policy more salient. We also looked at how climate discussions about international organizations and elites changed with the pandemic’s onset to show that the observed incivility spillover activated along overlapping pre-pandemic political cleavages, specifically anti-internationalist populist beliefs that linked climate policy opposition to vaccine hesitancy. Our findings show how affective polarization in public engagement with science becomes entrenched across policy domains, which has implications for how the public engages with and communicates about issues such as climate change and public health.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb558.title: Projecting potential population exposure to the invasive malaria vector Anopheles stephensi
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb558.authors: Sun, Y., Liu, W., Jing, Y., Liu, T. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb558.abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a major global public health threat, and the recent invasion and rapid spread of Anopheles stephensi across Africa pose new challenges for disease control. To assess future risks, we estimated the distribution of An. stephensi habitat suitability under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs, SSP126, SSP245, SSP370 and SSP585) across 2021–2100 using a boosted regression tree model, and quantified population exposure through a contribution decomposition framework separating environmental, population and joint effects. The results showed that the proportion of urban land was the most important predictor (17.17%), followed by mean temperature of the wettest quarter (BIO8, 9.24%) and the annual mean temperature (BIO1, 8.24%). Suitable habitats expanded consistently under all scenarios. Notably, SSP370 generated the highest population exposure, and there would be approximately 205.51 million people living in high suitability habitats for An. stephensi by 2081–2100. From the contribution decomposition framework, population change dominated the total exposure increase, outweighing environmental effects and joint effects. However, the individual contributions of population and environmental effects gradually declined over time, while their joint effect increased. These findings demonstrated that population growth, rather than climate change alone, is the primary driver of future exposure to An. stephensi . The increasing joint effect of population and environmental factors further underscores the need for integrated, region‐specific interventions that address their combined influence on transmission risk.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2026..title: Legionella Risk Management in Building Water Systems: Current Perspectives from Industry Practitioners
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2026..authors: Hao Xi, Kirstin Ross, Greg Falzon et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.buildenv.2026..abstract: Building water systems are internationally recognised reservoirs for opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens, including Legionella, the causative agent of Legionnaires’ disease. Inadequate design, operation and maintenance can promote Legionella proliferation and expose building occupants to potentially fatal infection. Effective management is therefore critical; however, there is limited international evidence regarding how guidelines for controlling Legionella risk are implemented in practice. Despite extensive Australian guidance, little is known about the practical management of Legionella risk in building water systems. This study explored current practices among hydraulic engineers, facility managers, plumbers, and water retreatment consultants. An online survey with follow-up interviews was conducted and the responses were then compared with existing guidelines and historical case studies published in the literature. Key findings indicated that current practice is predominantly risk-focused, with monitoring, system disinfection, routine maintenance, and targeted engineering modifications forming the core control measures. Case studies demonstrated substantial variability in how practitioners select and apply interventions, reflecting the complexity and diversity of building water systems. Insufficient maintenance and poor system design emerged as the leading contributors to Legionella proliferation, while control measures failed primarily due to incorrect or inappropriate selection. Budget constraints and lack of knowledge were identified as the major barriers to implementing effective and sustained control strategies. These findings are of international relevance, highlighting the need for control measures underpinned by risk assessment and comprehensive system monitoring and providing an evidence base to strengthen guidelines for effective Legionella management in building water systems globally.
