https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd5.title: Enhanced influence of the North Pacific Meridional Mode on the western North Pacific tropical cyclones in a warming climate
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd5.authors: Liu, B., Jia, F., Gan, B., Cai, W. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd5.abstract: Abstract Western North Pacific (WNP) tropical cyclone (TC) activity is strongly modulated by the North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM), yet how this influence responds to global warming remains unclear. Using observations and high-resolution atmosphere-only simulations that reproduce the observed NPMM-related environmental and TC responses, we investigate how warming alters the NPMM influence on TC genesis and tracks and the underlying physical mechanisms. We show that global warming strengthens and reshapes the NPMM-related TC response through an amplified tropical Pacific atmospheric response. Increased sensitivity of atmospheric convection to NPMM-related sea surface temperature anomalies enhances the convective response over the tropical central Pacific (CP), strengthening low-level cyclonic vorticity and increasing mid-tropospheric moisture over the southeastern WNP, thereby favoring TC genesis. Meanwhile, preferential strengthening of the southern portion of the NPMM-induced easterly steering flow directs TC activity and landfalls toward lower latitudes, producing a southward redistribution of NPMM-related TC tracks. Across simulations, stronger convective enhancement over the tropical CP is consistently associated with larger increases in TC genesis and lower-latitude track density. These results demonstrate that global warming can reshape regional TC risk not only by altering the mean climate state, but also by strengthening and spatially redistributing the influence of internal climate variability on TC genesis and subsequent movement.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb27a.title: Biodiversity conservation and its associations with economic performance, inequality, and peace
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb27a.authors: Peereman, J., Orenstein, D., Chen, G., Lin, T.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb27a.abstract: Abstract Biodiversity conservation is increasingly recognized as a product of coupled social–ecological systems shaped not only by ecological processes, but also by economic capacity, social inequality, and geopolitical stability. Here, we examined whether national conservation performance is systematically associated with economic prosperity, income inequality, peace, and the importance of natural resources in the national economy across 142 countries. Conservation performance was represented using the Nature Conservation Index (NCI), a composite metric integrating biodiversity threats, land management, governance capacity, and future environmental trends. We analyzed relationships between NCI, Gross National Income per capita, the Gini coefficient, the National Peace Index, and the total nature resources rents using a generalized additive model that accounted for nonlinear relationships and income stratification. Together, these societal variables explained deviance of 52.2% for the NCI model. Economic prosperity was positively associated with NCI, although the relationship was nonlinear across income groups, suggesting that conservation capacity does not increase uniformly with development. Counter to commonly assumed relationships between inequality and biodiversity loss, income inequality showed a positive multivariate association with NCI scores. This result suggests that high national conservation performance can coexist with unequal social conditions, potentially reflecting centralized or exclusionary conservation systems that elevate institutional conservation metrics without necessarily improving equitable biodiversity outcomes. We also found that more peaceful countries consistently exhibited higher conservation performance, supporting the view that geopolitical stability provides enabling conditions for sustained conservation governance and institutional continuity. We further suggest that national conservation indices may partly capture governance capacity, reporting infrastructure, and political commitment rather than ecological condition alone, while telecoupled trade systems may allow wealthier nations to externalize environmental pressures beyond their borders. Although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, our findings highlight the need to interpret global conservation indicators cautiously and to incorporate social equity and externalized environmental impacts more explicitly into international biodiversity assessment frameworks.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd2.title: Higher prevalence of rising climate-driven snowmelt potential of rain-on-snow events in the Eastern continental US
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd2.authors: Salvi, K., Ghosh, M., Kumar, M., Hao, D. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd2.abstract: Abstract Rain-on-snow (ROS) events have significant hydro-geomorphological consequences. While these events have been widely studied, their meteorological capacity to thermodynamically alter or melt snow when unconstrained by snow amount, hereafter referred to as snowmelt potential (SMP), remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to its long-term trends. Here, we evaluate climate-driven trends in SMP, estimated as the snowmelt-inducing total surface energy flux transferred during ROS events assuming unlimited snow availability, across 8 991 sites in snow-affected regions of the continental United States over a 39-year period (1981–2019). Overall, SMP exhibits an increasing trend at ∼63% of the sites with the proportion of sites showing positive trends rising from 54.4% in the Western region, to 64.6% in the Central region, and 78.4% in the Northeastern United States. The spatial pattern of SMP trends remains robust to uncertainties arising from omitted radiative fluxes and dampened wind-speed trends. High-energy ROS events are found increasing at majority of stations, with the positive trends becoming more widespread as the energy threshold rises. SMP trends are primarily governed by changes in net radiation and sensible heat flux, modulated in large part by trends of event air temperature and wind speed. Findings suggest growing meteorological hazard potential from ROS events, especially at high-SMP sites, highlighting increased risk with continued climate warming.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd8.title: Decadal variability reveals contrasts in solar-resource stability across China
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd8.authors: Meng, Y., Qiu, K., Wu, X., Wei, Z.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd8.abstract: Abstract Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of decadal variability in downward surface solar radiation (DSSR), commonly known as global horizontal irradiance in the solar energy sector, across China’s seven major power grids during 1960–2024. We find pronounced regional contrasts in decadal DSSR variability, with the Central, Eastern, and Southern grids exhibiting greater variability, whereas the Western and Tibetan grids combine high solar resource abundance with comparatively low variability. The Central and Eastern grids also contribute disproportionately to national variability relative to their geographical area. By converting DSSR variability into indicative photovoltaic yield, we further illustrate that resource-driven yield uncertainty is substantially higher in the volatile eastern regions; however, spatial diversification across weakly correlated grids can reduce portfolio variability by up to 29%. These findings emphasize that the geography of solar-resource climatic stability differs from resource abundance, highlighting the critical need to incorporate decadal stability and spatial diversification into long-term renewable-energy and inter-regional transmission planning.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd3.title: Electricity retail pricing as incentives for load optimization in Vietnam
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd3.authors: Doan, T., Portilla-Paveri, M., Lobos, N., Negrete-Pincetic, M.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd3.abstract: Abstract Vietnam’s pathway to net-zero emissions by 2050 has so far relied primarily on large-scale renewable energy investments, with limited use of demand-side management. This study evaluates how alternative retail electricity pricing schemes—flat tariffs, time-of-use (TOU), critical peak pricing (CPP), and a TOU–CPP hybrid—shape demand flexibility, system costs, emissions, consumer welfare, and reliability in Vietnam. The analysis uses SWITCH 2.0, an integrated capacity expansion and dispatch model with an iterative demand-response (DR) module, to Vietnam’s electricity system in 2050. Relative to flat pricing, the modeled TOU designs reduce total system costs by up to 15% and CO 2 emissions by 17.2%–37.5%, while increasing consumer welfare. Consecutive TOU blocks capture substantial benefits, whereas adding CPP produces little additional improvement. Endogenous block assignment achieves the lowest system cost and reduces storage investment, but does not yield the lowest emissions or highest consumer welfare. Sensitivity analysis confirms lower unit costs and emissions and higher consumer welfare under consecutive TOU than under matched flat-pricing cases across seven DR parameter combinations. However, the magnitude of these benefits depends strongly on the share of load available for within-day rescheduling. Demand shifting toward solar-rich hours also changes transmission utilization, relieving pressure on some corridors while increasing it elsewhere. The findings support a staged transition toward TOU pricing with simple consecutive blocks, accompanied by enabling technologies and coordinated transmission planning. The results represent conditional system-level outcomes rather than estimates of realized consumer responses or distributional effects.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.authors: Xinghui Tao, Zehao Ye, Guangming Wang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.abstract: Segmenting segmental tunnel-lining point clouds supports automated inspection, but expert-tuned pipelines can degrade as conditions change. This paper presents R4Tun, a framework for bounded, deployment-label-free parameter adaptation of an expert-designed segmentation pipeline, guided by large language models (LLMs) using memory ( m ), state ( s ), and knowledge ( k ). On 30 selected Seg2Tunnel subsets (13 regular, 17 complex), three LLMs using full context increased mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) from 0.18 to 0.43–0.48 and overall accuracy from 0.42 to 0.59–0.65 over the static baseline. Near-reference regular (staggered) subsets reached mIoU 0.784–0.796 across LLMs. Ablations showed that m + s accounted for most of the adaptation gains. These results support R4Tun as a controlled, label-free, cross-LLM adaptation mechanism for the tested setting, with each parameter change auditable via logged rationales. Adaptation remains constrained by the pipeline’s fixed algorithms and design assumptions. R4Tun is therefore positioned as a mechanism-level contribution rather than a deployable inspection system.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70381.title: Public Risk Judgments of Endocrine‐Disrupting Chemicals: Psychometric Structure, Exposure Pathways, and Cross‐National Differences
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70381.authors: Simonsen, N., Pravednikov, A., Lagerkvist, C., Perkovic, S.
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70381.abstract: ABSTRACT Endocrine‐disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are pervasive in everyday life and pose well‐documented public health risks, yet little is known about how lay perceptions of EDC risks are structured and how they vary across exposure pathways and regulatory contexts. Drawing on the psychometric paradigm of risk perception, we conducted a large cross‐national survey () in Denmark, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Participants evaluated 18 EDC‐related exposure scenarios across nine canonical risk attributes, ranked perceived health risks by exposure pathway (consumption, inhalation, and dermal contact), and reported perceived severity, susceptibility, overall health risk, institutional trust, and sociodemographic characteristics. Across all three countries, risk perceptions exhibited a robust two‐dimensional structure corresponding to affective‐dread and cognitive‐deliberate dimensions. However, the relative salience of these dimensions varied systematically: cognitive‐deliberate cues accounted for more variance in Denmark, whereas affective‐dread cues were more prominent in the United Kingdom and the United States. Perceived risk also varied consistently by exposure pathway, with consumption judged the most risky, followed by inhalation and dermal contact, a hierarchy that showed minimal cross‐country variation. At the individual level, greater knowledge of EDCs consistently predicted higher perceived susceptibility, while gender, year of birth, income, parenthood, and institutional trust showed context‐ and outcome‐specific associations. By extending the psychometric paradigm to chronic, diffuse chemical hazards embedded in everyday activities, this study demonstrates that EDC risk perceptions reflect shared affective‐cognitive dimensions while remaining sensitive to exposure pathways and governance contexts, offering theoretically grounded insights for risk communication and policy design.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08485.title: From participation to data: collaborative mapping in the context of natural hazards and risks
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08485.authors: Mara Remi, Marco La Salandra, Francesco Lovergine et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08485.abstract: Collaborative mapping has emerged as a key approach for collecting, analysing, and sharing geospatial information on natural hazards and risks. By integrating Citizen Science (CS) and Volunteered Geographic Information (VGI), it incorporates local knowledge, real-time observations, and crowdsourced data collection into risk assessment and management processes, where traditional data sources are limited or outdated. This study provides a systematic overview of collaborative mapping applications for natural hazards, including hydrogeomorphological (floods, landslides, coastal erosion), climate and weather related (storms and cyclones, wildfires, droughts and heat waves) and geophysical (earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions) as well as multi-hazards contexts, examining how different terminologies, actor types, and technological approaches are represented across the literature. A total of 105 peer-reviewed studies were selected following a screening process based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, starting from major scientific databases. The results highlight an uneven distribution of research efforts, with a focus on floods and multi-hazard contexts. Furthermore, collaborative mapping is predominantly applied in mitigation, preparedness, and response phases. In terms of technologies, while traditional GIS-based methods dominate, computational approaches like Machine Learning (ML) are gaining traction. These approaches increasingly rely on the combined use of complementary geospatial sources: satellite and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery commonly serves as a basemap guiding the digitisation of features in OpenStreetMap (OSM), whose data are then extracted and integrated into hazard and risk analyses. This integration enables spatial datasets to be rapidly created and updated where authoritative data are scarce or outdated, thereby supporting disaster management across its different phases. By providing a structured synthesis of key elements, this review contributes to a better understanding of the current state of collaborative mapping in natural hazards and risks, identifies key gaps and directions for future research.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Reuse of effluent from the paint industry for the production of Anadenanthera peregrina seedlings: A silvicultural and ecotoxicological study
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Lidiane Brito de Sousa, Thainara Lima Araújo, Agostinho Cardoso Hlavanguane et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Increasing water scarcity and the need for sustainable waste management have necessitated the reuse of industrial effluents, particularly when aligned with the specific characteristics of each industrial sector. Forest nurseries represent a promising setting for this practice, as their automated irrigation systems prevent the risk of over-application and reduce effluent mobility in the soil through deep percolation. This study evaluated the feasibility of reusing effluent generated by a paint-manufacturing facility in the production of red angico (Anadenanthera peregrina) seedlings. Plant growth and development and the ecotoxicological response associated with effluent application were analyzed. Two effluent concentrations (E50% and E100%) were tested, with well water as the control. Plant-free substrate irrigated with undiluted effluent (E100% without plant) was monitored to investigate the influence of plant presence on substrate characteristics. After 100 days of irrigation, seedling growth, Dickson Quality Index values, physicochemical changes in the substrate, and ecotoxicity assays using Eisenia fetida earthworms were evaluated. Notably, the effluent, particularly at a concentration of 100%, restricted early seedling development, reducing biomass accumulation and quality indices relative to the control and demonstrating clear phytotoxicity to A. peregrina. Therefore, although the effluent can aid fertigation, its application in the production of A. peregrina seedlings requires dilution to mitigate its phytotoxic effects. However, substrate analyses revealed that undiluted effluent increased microbial activity, as indicated by basal substrate respiration, and exerted an attractant effect on earthworms. These findings indicate that A. peregrina may contribute to the phytoremediation of soils contaminated with paint industry effluents.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Balancing nutrients and metal contaminants: sustainable land application rates for livestock manures in Ireland
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: S. Farid, L. Morrison, M. Danaher et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Livestock manures are valuable nutrient sources for crop production, but variable composition and inappropriate application rates can cause nutrient imbalance, phosphorus accumulation and trace-metal loading, increasing the risks to water quality and the wider environment. This study evaluated manure-specific application rates by considering nutrient and trace-metal composition, crop requirements and soil phosphorus status. It was applied to cattle, sheep and chicken manures used for perennial ryegrass ( Lolium perenne L.) and spring wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) under Irish nutrient-management recommendations. Maximum application rates ranged from 0.96 to 7.62 t dry matter ha −1 yr −1 for perennial ryegrass and from 0.99 to 9.76 t dry matter ha −1 yr −1 for spring wheat across Morgan's soil phosphorus indices 1 to 3, representing increasing soil phosphorus status. No manure application was permitted at index 4. Cattle manure permitted the highest application rates because of lower total phosphorus concentration, whereas sheep manure supported the lowest. The governing nutrient constraint varied with manure composition, crop nutrient requirements and soil nutrient status, with phosphorus generally limiting cattle and sheep manure application, while nitrogen limited chicken manure application under specific conditions in TN-based calculations. Regulated trace-metal loadings remained below the annual permissible limits. Zinc and copper reached approximately 31% and 14% of their respective limits, while cadmium remained below 10% and chromium, nickel and lead below 2%. These findings demonstrate the importance of considering manure nutrient composition, crop requirements, soil nutrient status and trace metal loading limits together when determining manure application rates to protect crop productivity and water quality.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec031.title: Viewing extreme precipitation intensification through an absolute-change lens
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec031.authors: Jiayi Ni, Changrui Zhu, Qun Yue et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec031.abstract: Abstract While relative fractional changes are widely used to characterize extreme precipitation intensification under climate warming, absolute changes provide a complementary perspective that more directly quantifies the magnitude of extreme precipitation intensification, with direct implications for assessing potential impacts. By analyzing annual maximum daily precipitation in climate models, we show that the geographical patterns of the strongest extreme precipitation intensification identified from absolute changes differ from those highlighted by relative changes, and that the most intense annual maxima exhibit substantially larger absolute increases than weaker annual maxima despite only modest differences in their relative changes. Although thermodynamic moistening produces broadly similar relative increases in stronger and weaker annual maxima, it leads to substantially larger absolute increases in stronger maxima, primarily owing to differences in climatological intensity. Dynamic contributions reinforce this intensity-dependent contrast in some regions, particularly in the South and East Asian monsoon regions and equatorial Africa. These contrasts highlight the value of considering absolute changes alongside relative changes to better characterize the magnitude and geographical patterns of extreme precipitation intensification and inform assessments of potential impacts under climate warming.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba00.title: Climate risk assessment in tropical wetlands through integrated hydroclimatic, land cover, and community knowledge
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba00.authors: Estrada-Zuleta, J., Meneses Bernal, J., Avila-Diaz, A., Quesada, B.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba00.abstract: Abstract Climate-risk assessments in tropical wetlands increasingly combine hydroclimatic and land-cover data, but rarely integrate them with structured community evidence on experienced impacts and adaptation priorities. We address this gap in six communities around the Complejo Cenagoso de Zapatosa, a Ramsar site, and the Morales wetland in the Colombian Caribbean. We integrated hydroclimatic records and climate-extreme indices (1991–2020), land-cover change and runoff-potential analysis (1991–2020), flood-susceptibility modeling, and structured participatory evidence from 106 participants. Mean annual temperature increased by 0.4 °C decade −1 , while warm nights and warm days increased by 17.1% and 17.3% decade −1 , respectively; precipitation and precipitation-extreme indices showed no significant domain-mean trends. Forest cover declined by 1 122.9 km 2 , whereas flooded non-forest formations, agriculture/pasture mosaic, and oil palm increased by 800.9, 254.4, and 244.2 km 2 , respectively, altering runoff potential. Flood susceptibility was concentrated along floodplains and wetland margins (AUC = 0.95). Of 50 valid community-reported extreme-event records, 76.0% matched the expected sign of annual instrumental anomalies; both heat records matched, while agreement reached 91.3% for floods and 53.8% for droughts. Drought mismatches indicate that annual rainfall anomalies incompletely capture wetland drought, where dry-spell persistence, water-level change, and livelihood disruption shape local experience. Community priorities emphasized wetland restoration, hydrological connectivity, fisheries governance, livelihood diversification, and monitoring. Integrating technical and community evidence therefore revealed complementary climate-risk signals and the conditions under which ecosystem-based adaptation may be locally feasible.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb710.title: Influence of natural and anthropogenic forcings on western US winter fire weather and the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb710.authors: Srivastava, A., Risser, M., Ullrich, P., Wehner, M.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb710.abstract: Abstract Winter fire weather is shaped by interactions between anthropogenic climate change and natural climate variability, yet how the combination of human and natural forcings influences winter fire weather conditions remains poorly quantified. This study uses a multiple linear regression framework that removes long-term CO 2 -related trends to examine the influence of natural modes of variability on the December–February monthly fire weather index over the western United States (WUS), with the January 2025 Los Angeles (LA) fire risk as a motivating case study. Results show that the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Pacific North American pattern (PNA) and Atlantic Meridional Mode (AMM) significantly influence winter fire weather across the WUS, whereas the influence of CO 2 is more pronounced and generally significant over the interior regions, but less evident along the coastal areas of the WUS. Positive phases of the PNA and AMM, combined with La Niña–like conditions during December 2024 and January 2025, significantly elevated fire weather risk across southern California, including LA County. The elevated fire-weather conditions preceding the January 2025 fires in LA and surrounding regions were aggravated by the combined influence of the natural and anthropogenic modes. Our study also shows that anthropogenic CO 2 is associated with an estimated 10%–20% increase in the chances of the 2024–25 fire weather over the WUS coastal states, although this contribution is not statistically significant, while La Niña and positive PNA significantly increase these chances by at least 20% across California and by more than twice across much of the WUS, including southern California and neighboring states. We find that large-scale natural climate modes combined with increases in greenhouse gas concentration provide valuable information for understanding and predicting WUS winter fire weather.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd1.title: Movement characteristics of persistent extreme precipitation events over China during the warm season using high spatiotemporal resolution data
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd1.authors: Liu, K., Mao, J., Wang, X., Ren, J.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd1.abstract: Abstract Moving persistent extreme precipitation events (PEPEs) can cause severe disasters along their tracks. However, a PEPE typically consists of multiple rain cells that evolve and move differently from one another, rendering the conventional single-center tracking method incapable of capturing their respective characteristics. Here we use a multi-rain cell tracking method to characterize the movement of PEPEs during the warm season (May to September) over China, utilizing high-resolution precipitation data at half‐hourly temporal and 0.1° spatial resolutions for the period 1998–2024. Based on the movement distance and direction, PEPEs are clustered into the long-distance eastward-moving, short-distance eastward-moving, northeastward-moving, and westward-moving types, which are most prevalent over Southeast China, the Tibetan Plateau (TP), Northeast China, and the southern China, respectively. Temporally, the frequency of these four types of events peaks progressively from May to August, and the PEPEs with longer movement distances tend to occur in the early morning. In terms of large-scale circulation patterns, long-distance eastward-moving PEPEs are favored by the southwestward extension of the Western Pacific Subtropical High (WPSH); short-distance eastward-moving PEPEs are associated with a meridional dipole of geopotential height anomaly around the TP; the northeastward-moving type is likely influenced by a wave-train circulation pattern in high latitudes; westward-moving PEPEs occur more frequently when the WPSH extends northwestward. These findings provide a comprehensive climatology of PEPE movement and highlight distinct circulation controls, which may aid in the prediction of moving extreme precipitations.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb369.title: High-resolution soil moisture forecasts for drought early warning in Germany
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb369.authors: Najafi, H., Boeing, F., Thober, S., Rakovec, O. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb369.abstract: Abstract Drought early warning increasingly relies on high-resolution monitoring, but the skill of daily soil moisture forecasts at lead times of 1–2 weeks driven by real-time meteorological ensembles has rarely been evaluated directly against an operational drought-monitoring framework. The Hydrological Sub-seasonal Forecasting System (HS2S) extends an established national drought-monitoring framework into high-resolution probabilistic soil moisture forecasts up to two weeks ahead for Germany at 0.015 625 ∘ resolution. We evaluated a daily-initialised HS2S configuration using the 51-member real-time forecast ensemble from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts during the exceptionally dry spring and summer of 2025 against the operational, model-based German Drought Monitor (GDM), generated within the same mesoscale Hydrologic Model (mHM) framework using observation-based meteorological forcing. The assessment combined drought onset/recovery transition diagnostics with probabilistic (Brier skill score) and categorical verification against an initialised two-state Markov persistence benchmark, and continuous verification against an mHM soil moisture climatology. HS2S reproduced the timing and mean magnitude of GDM-indicated drought onset and recovery. It showed positive probabilistic skill relative to the initialised Markov benchmark and positive continuous skill relative to the 1950–2017 mHM climatology at both lead times. For moderate drought ( SMI 0.20 ), the critical success index improved by 15.0 and 15.5 percentage points at lead weeks 1 and 2, respectively. The probability of detection of GDM-indicated drought was 95% and 89% at the same lead times. Given HS2S and the GDM share the same mHM–Soil Moisture Index framework and initial states, the verification is model-consistent and evaluates skill in anticipating the GDM-indicated drought state rather than validating absolute soil moisture accuracy. The added value of real-time meteorological forecasts relative to historical meteorological sequences was not assessed. Within this operationally relevant framework, HS2S showed forecast skill up to two weeks ahead during the 2025 drought, highlighting the potential of high-resolution probabilistic soil moisture forecasts to complement national drought monitoring with forward-looking information.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70411.title: When Scientific Uncertainty is Linked to Lower Information Avoidance: Motivational Pathways to Public Engagement With Climate Risk Information
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70411.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how scientific uncertainty is associated with both appetitive and aversive motivations, as well as its direct and indirect associations with risk information avoidance (RIA). Drawing on Liu and Chen's (2026) appetitive–aversive motivational framework, based on the Planned Risk Information Avoidance (PRIA) model, we investigate how uncertainty relates to information avoidance through risk perception, perceived information insufficiency, informational efficacy, information overload, information‐seeking norms, and negative emotions. Using structural equation modeling with a US adult sample, the findings indicate that scientific uncertainty is negatively associated with information avoidance and is linked to multiple motivational pathways. Specifically, higher scientific uncertainty is associated with greater risk perceptions and information insufficiency, and with lower levels of information overload, which in turn correspond to reduced avoidance intentions. These findings provide insight into the role of scientific uncertainty in shaping RIA, highlighting its potential to reduce avoidance in the context of climate change.

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02790.title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02790.authors: Tong Li, Francis W. Zwiers, Xuebin Zhang, Qiaohong Sun
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02790.abstract: Global temperatures have averaged 1.2 °C above pre-industrial levels over the past decade, yet regional warming patterns and remaining warming budgets under Paris Agreement limits remain uncertain owing to insufficient historical observations. Here we quantify and attribute warming across all IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) regions since pre-industrial times using a Bayesian framework combining multi-model simulations with observations, enabling robust estimates in data-sparse regions. Regional warming is already pronounced. By 2025, attributed regional warming had reached about 90–94% of the levels expected at 1.5 °C global warming and 65–76% of those expected at 2 °C. Attribution confidence is the highest in tropical regions, including much of Africa, where low internal variability enables robust results. Attributed warming is the greatest in northern high-latitude regions, exceeding 2.5 °C. Greenhouse gases dominate, partially offset by aerosol cooling. These results reveal that current warming is already indistinguishable from a 1.5 °C world, highlighting the shared urgency of adaptation across all regions. Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08507.title: Governing wildfire insurance under mortgage constraints: an availability-affordability-capacity framework with decision-oriented evaluation for California, 2018–2024
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08507.authors: Lu Chao, XiaoXi Ma, Sun ShuiMiao
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08507.abstract: Abstract Catastrophe insurance economics has long recognized that disaster insurance markets fail on both sides of the market, with households under-insuring low-probability high-consequence risks and insurers unable to diversify or price correlated catastrophe exposure. The resulting debate between risk-based pricing and affordability has been conducted almost entirely within single margins: demand studies treat coverage as an annual household choice, supply studies treat insurer withdrawal as a market outcome, and government-intervention studies treat residual instruments as add-ons to a functioning market. This paper argues that all three assumptions are inadequate for mortgaged homeowners in wildfire-exposed regions, where coverage is a continuing contractual condition and the residual market is capacity-constrained. It develops an availability-affordability-capacity framework in which the offer margin, the budget margin, and the capacity margin are determined jointly under a mortgage covenant, and it evaluates the framework with a calibrated structural model estimated on a county panel for California from 2018 to 2024. The theoretical contribution is a formal allocation model that derives when each margin binds and when policy instruments are substitutes or complements, and a decomposition showing why the risk-pricing-versus-affordability debate persists: the sign of the joint response depends on local income densities and capacity binding, so it is ambiguous in theory and must be resolved empirically. The empirical contribution includes a temporal holdout, a cross-region transfer to Oregon and Colorado, and a decision-oriented evaluation protocol that shows how predictive accuracy and decision outcomes can rank pricing regimes differently. A full-profile scan of the 6,185 articles published in this journal between 2015 and 2025, together with a coded synthesis of the 135 articles on fire hazards and insurance governance, documents that the fragmentation the framework predicts is visible in the journal's own output. The model reproduces the observed trajectory of the California FAIR Plan share in-sample and tracks it out-of-sample through 2023, identifies the 2024 acceleration as a decision-relevant signal, and shows that capacity rationing becomes binding under sustained supply tightening.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08504.title: Development and validation of a Lake Michigan compound flood model
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08504.authors: Benjamin Nelson-Mercer, Jeremy D. Bricker, Michael Notaro et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08504.abstract: Abstract Compound flooding threatens communities along the coastline of the Laurentian Great Lakes, where intense rainfall and high lake levels can occur simultaneously, creating large flood impacts. Understanding the extent and impact of these floods is important for planning and assessing risk in areas with vulnerable populations and infrastructure. To increase knowledge of Great Lakes compound flooding, this study develops and tests a coupled hydrodynamic-wave model for the Great Lakes, using Berrien County, Michigan and Milwaukee, Wisconsin as test cases. The model simulates a set of historical compound flood events that occurred during a period of high Lake Michigan levels. While hydrodynamic models offer important insights into​ flood risk, evaluating their performance is often challenging due to a lack of in situ data of flooding events. To overcome this challenge, this study incorporates location-specific feedback from local experts to guide model development and validate the modeled inundation. Data shared by these experts include​s geolocated images taken during a flood event as well as feedback provided through public participatory GIS (PPGIS) that are used to qualitatively and quantitatively validate the compound flood model’s performance. This showcases useful techniques for flood model validation that can be applied to other data-scarce areas and events.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: Catastrophe-insurance research has established that availability, affordability, mortgage finance, and public backstops are connected, but it seldom solves the resulting allocation when the residual market can itself bind. We develop an availability-affordability-capacity framework for mortgaged homeowners and evaluate it with a structural California model for 2018–2024. The four structural parameters are fitted jointly to independently constructed FAIR Plan ratios for 2018–2021 only; 2022–2023 is a true temporal holdout, and 2024 is an estimate. Calibration MAE and RMSE are 0.0770 and 0.0779% points; holdout MAE and RMSE are 0.1796 and 0.2193 points. In 2023 the allocation is 79.818% voluntary coverage, 3.444% residual coverage, and 16.739% model-implied force-placement exposure. Exposure is 2.73% points below its 2018 level and 0.61 points above its 2021 level; the post-2021 movement is modest and does not restore the earlier level. Across nine predeclared open-bin mappings, 2023 exposure spans 15.529–18.081%. Counterfactuals, the affordability surface and the decision grid are recomputed from the same structure. The 2023 baseline covenant-feasible coverage is 83.261%; an $850 voucher raises it to 84.798%, whereas a supply tightening lowers it and makes the 6% capacity bound bind. All four weighting schemes in the decision grid select the lower boundary lambda = 1.6, so we report a boundary choice and do not claim an interior optimum. Florida Citizens supplies a pre-specified directional contraction test, and Texas TWIA supplies a statutory funding-waterfall stress map. The third state is a modelled exposure to lender-protection action, not an observed servicer action or uninsured rate. The literature layer is supported by a query-logged audit: 28 executions, 2,643 records retrieved, 1,545 unique candidates screened, and 402 records included. The contribution is narrowed to a capacity-constrained residual-market allocation with decision-oriented evaluation.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.authors: Haoyu Hu, Jianfa Shen, Hengyu Gu et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.abstract: Urban rail transit is an integral component of urban morphology, which plays a role in guiding the spatial distribution of urban populations. Understanding this dynamic is essential for rational urban planning to mitigate uncontrolled urban sprawl and promote sustainable transit-oriented development. While urban population density models are widely used to quantitatively capture these spatial distribution patterns, the existing literature lacks comprehensive studies integrating city-level and station-level analyses to elucidate how rail transit networks associate with these density dynamics. Using grid-level population data from China’s seventh national census, this study estimates a generalised urban population density model for cities with operational rail transit. We employ XGBoost models to investigate the statistical associations between rail transit features and population density patterns at both the overarching city level and the localised station level. Within the generalised model, we define two key parameters: the Peak Location Index (D), which determines the peak position of the population density curve; and the Decay Radius (r 0 ), which reflects the flatness of overall population density decay. The results show that the population coverage and scale expansion contribute to D and r 0 separately. Station-level studies further corroborate that metro stations are more conducive to population uplift in places far from the city centre. Apart from the effects of built environment factors, station location within the network and years of operation also exhibit notable predictive importance regarding population density. This sheds light on the need for policymakers to rationalise rail transit planning as a tool for urban population redistribution.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Should we predict wildlife–vehicle collision hotspots from road and landscape characteristics?
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Federica Castagnoli, Emanuele Fior, Valeria Rossi, Stefano Leonardi
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Wildlife-vehicle collisions (WVCs) represent a global challenge for human safety and biodiversity conservation. This study investigates the environmental and road characteristics that influence WVC risk, using the province of Parma (Northern Italy) as a representative case study. We analysed 693 collision events recorded between 2013 and 2018, most of which involving roe deer (Capreolus capreolus, 86%) and wild boar (Sus scrofa, 10%). Spatial and temporal analysis revealed how collisions are not randomly distributed, peaking on busy major roads where high average speeds coincide with fragmented landscapes. Higher collision frequency was observed near croplands and riparian corridors, particularly at the peri-urban interface. Temporal patterns confirm that most WVCs occur during crepuscular and nocturnal hours, aligning with peak ungulate activity. Our research identifies critical road segments from environmental predictors, providing a robust spatial baseline to identify priority locations for mitigation measures, such as wildlife underpasses and road signage, to enhance both habitat permeability and drivers' safety.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Chemical pretreatments for odorant emission control of poultry byproducts and dynamic reactions during soil application
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Edward T. Drabold, Will Neville, Anna Mayes et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Presently, many meat byproducts are land-applied as fertilizer. Expansion of this practice has led to significant public outcry over odorous emissions. Unlike biosolids or manure application, which have been well studied, land application odor control for mostly undigested meat byproducts has received little attention. In the case of the poultry industry, the most land-applied meat byproduct is dissolved air flotation (DAF) solids. In this work, chemical pretreatments, including addition of agricultural lime, quick lime, acid, or oxidizers were considered for DAF solids odorant emission control of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). VOC odorant emissions were quantified by analytical means (GC/MS), not human perception. The application method for quick lime was also considered - including pre-mixing versus surface application of quick lime after DAF solids. These experiments were conducted in controlled mesocosms with real soil, environmental perturbation to understand moisture effects, and were performed until odor extinction (∼200 h) to capture longer-term behavior. The results revealed that pre-mixed quick lime (pH of 12) removed volatile fatty acid (VFAs) emissions below detection without worsening sulfur-organic emissions (a common issue with liming). Meanwhile, agricultural lime delayed VOC odorant emissions and other chemical treatments either increased emissions or had no significant effect. A follow-up mechanistic study determined that VFA volatilization in mesocosm systems was likely due to percolation of liquid from DAF solids and acidification in the soil. Complete mixing with the acidic soil amplified odorant emissions. This study provides important insights into mechanisms that lead to malodors in meat byproduct land application.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Praveena Pachaiappan, Laura Torrent, Bruno Valentim et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Herein, we report the formulations of composite beads to be used as adsorbent materials for water treatment, based on acid-treated sewage sludge ash (ASSA), obtained from mono-combustion, combined with polysaccharide-based biopolymers (chitosan, carboxymethylcellulose and TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TOCNF)), with glutaraldehyde (GA) or sodium alginate (SA) as cross-linkers. The resulting materials were characterized by SEM-EDS, both on the surface and in the inner section, and by tomography, highlighting the homogeneous distribution of ashes in the polysaccharide matrix and a highly porous network. The composites were tested as adsorbents for water treatment via batch adsorption experiments to evaluate their removal capacity for textile dyes and heavy metals. Comparative analyses revealed that beads reinforced with polymeric networks exhibited markedly higher adsorption efficiencies than corresponding blank formulations and raw ash-based sorbents. Notably, composite beads fabricated with TOCNF, SA, and ASSA displayed enhanced adsorption performance and mechanical integrity. Adsorption performances were described by the Langmuir isotherm model, indicating monolayer adsorption on uniform sites, whereas pseudo-second-order kinetic fits suggested chemisorption-dominated processes. Overall, the TOCNF-SA-ASSA composite beads demonstrate superior adsorption efficiency and operational robustness across multiple pollutant classes, underscoring their potential for advanced water treatment.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Cyanobacterial biomass pretreatment strategies enhance biogas production and alter the anaerobic microbial community
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Yixin Yan, Qingyu Shang, Nikoletta Tsiarta et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms pose severe environmental challenges in surface waters on a global scale. Although mechanical harvesting is an effective bloom mitigation strategy, sustainable utilization of the harvested biomass remains a major challenge. Anaerobic digestion (AD) offers an attractive valorisation alternative; however, relatively low methane yields limit its practical application. This study evaluated the effects of four pretreatment methods (grinding, ultrasonication, thermal, and thermochemical) on the AD performance of two bloom-forming cyanobacteria ( Aphanizomenon flos-aquae and Microcystis aeruginosa ), focusing on cell morphology, methane production and microbial community composition. Biomethane potential assays showed that ultrasonication produced the highest methane yields for both species (308.42 ± 37.67 and 376.95 ± 13.96 mL CH 4 g −1 VS for A. flos-aquae and M. aeruginosa , respectively), while grinding achieved comparable performance for A. flos-aquae , reflecting its filamentous morphology. In contrast, the colonial structure and glycocalyx of M. aeruginosa reduced the effectiveness of grinding while favouring ultrasonication and thermal pretreatments. Lower methane yields were observed at the higher organic loads assessed, suggesting substrate overloading under the tested experimental conditions. Optical microscopy demonstrated distinct species-dependent morphological responses to pretreatment, while microbial analysis revealed shifts in the relative abundance of bacterial and archaeal taxa associated with AD. These microbial observations indicate correlations between pretreatment, community composition and methane production. Overall, pretreatment enhanced methane yields by up to 94.8% compared with untreated biomass, demonstrating the importance of selecting pretreatment strategies according to cyanobacterial biomass characteristics to improve AD performance.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Advancing resilient and sustainable project portfolio management
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Niloufar Bagherifam, Robert Moehler
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Environmental disruptions, economic volatility, digital transformation, resource constraints, and increasing sustainability pressures have fundamentally reshaped the strategic role of project portfolio management (PPM). As organizations seek to balance long-term value creation with adaptability under uncertainty, resilience and sustainability have become critical portfolio capabilities. Despite growing scholarly interest, research in this area remains fragmented across project management, sustainability, strategic management, and risk management, limiting a comprehensive understanding of its intellectual development. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric, science mapping, and thematic synthesis of resilient and sustainable PPM research published between 2006 and 2026. Following a PRISMA-guided screening process, 277 journal articles were retrieved from the Scopus database and analysed using bibliometric performance analysis, bibliographic coupling, country collaboration, and keyword co-occurrence techniques. The findings reveal a marked acceleration of research after 2020 and identify three major knowledge domains shaping the field: portfolio decision analytics, risk, uncertainty and portfolio resilience, and strategic portfolio adaptation. The review also demonstrates a conceptual shift from traditional portfolio optimisation towards adaptive governance, resilience, sustainability, and data-driven portfolio decision-making. By integrating fragmented research into a coherent intellectual structure, the study advances theoretical understanding of resilient and sustainable PPM, identifies key research gaps, and proposes a future research agenda. The findings further provide portfolio managers and policymakers with evidence-based insights for designing more adaptive, resilient, and sustainable project portfolios in increasingly uncertain environments.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebfaf.title: A bottom-up social cost of carbon for Latin America: Municipality-level heat-mortality damage functions from 30 million daily death records
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebfaf.abstract: Abstract Temperature–mortality response functions have been quantified across many climate zones, but for most of the developing world they have not been translated into country-specific economic damages at sub-national resolution. This study estimates bottom-up mortality social costs of carbon (SCC) for five Latin American countries at municipality resolution. We assemble 30 million daily death records across 10,214 municipality-equivalent units in Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Ecuador and Peru (2000–2023) and merge them with the ARCO-ERA5 reanalysis sampled at every unit centroid. Country-specific Poisson exposure–response functions, estimated separately by country with municipality, year, month and day-of-week fixed effects, recover same-day heat-mortality semi-elasticities of 10.9% (Brazil) and 13.0% (Mexico) at a daily maximum temperature of 35 °C or above, relative to a 20–25 °C reference. Translating these functions along the SSP2-4.5 warming path, with the transient climate response to cumulative emissions, an income-driven attenuation of the response, a value-of-statistical-life path that rises with projected income, and population ageing, yields central mortality SCCs of about USD 0.5/tCO₂ in Brazil and USD 0.3/tCO₂ in Mexico at a 2% discount rate, with a small negative value for cool-climate Chile and near-zero values for Ecuador and Peru. These bottom-up, mortality-only estimates are a fraction of full-system country-level SCCs but share their cross-country ordering and signs, and the underlying damage functions imply a substantial annual heat-mortality burden that the sparse regional evidence in global assessments does not capture.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd9.title: Assessing demand-side policy impacts on US urban passenger transport
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd9.authors: Xiangwen Fu, Christoph Bertram, Page G. Kyle
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd9.abstract: Abstract Demand-side policies could significantly mitigate energy use and carbon emissions of urban passenger transport. However, previous integrated assessment modeling studies often failed to fully evaluate their mitigation potential in the absence of explicit representation of urban transport dynamics. Here we adjust the global integrated assessment model GCAM to disaggregate passenger transport in the US region into the urban and inter-city subsectors. We analyze the impacts of transformative demand-side policies on US urban passenger transport service demand, mode share, energy use, and carbon emissions. We consider six demand-side policies (compact urban development , speed limit, shared mobility, remote working, fuel tax, and congestion fee) as well as a technology policy of vehicle electrification. We find that all demand-side policies could collectively reduce urban transport energy use and carbon emissions by approximately 60% from the baseline in 2050 by shifting and reducing transport demand. We also find that demand-side policies could deliver strong synergies with electric vehicle (EV) deployment. Under ambitious EV deployment, although most direct urban passenger transport emissions are mitigated, electricity demand would increase by 718 TWh from 2021 to 2050, as much as 16% of current US total electricity consumption. A full portfolio of demand-side policies could limit the increased electricity use for urban transport to 299 TWh in 2050, providing substantial benefits for energy savings. Our study shows that demand-side policies and vehicle electrification can be complementary in achieving decarbonization and other sustainability goals.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebb4d.abstract: Abstract Deforestation footprints rely on information on import flows. The standard procedure converts imports of semi-processed commodities into commodity equivalents. The paper distinguishes between product yields and conversion factors. It is conversion factors, which relate the commodity requirement for unit production of the semi-processed product, that are the required to estimate deforestation footprints. The simple reciprocal relationship between yields and conversion factors breaks down when there are jointly produced products such as soybean oil and meal. The paper also examines the treatment of processing waste in footprint estimation. Alternative procedures are examined and applied to the footprints of EU imports of cocoa, oil palm and soy products.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd7.title: Biases and predictability limits of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones in subseasonal prediction systems
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd7.authors: Li, S., Yang, J., Liu, A., Lu, M. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd7.abstract: Abstract Subseasonal prediction of Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclones (ETCs) is critical for anticipating associated weather extremes, yet biases and predictability limits of ETC activity in current forecast systems remain insufficiently quantified. Here, using hindcasts from ten state-of-the-art subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) prediction systems within a Lagrangian tracking framework, we uncover a common and pervasive bias: the multi-model ensemble consistently predicts fewer and weaker cyclones at a one-month lead, underestimating frequency by 10%–18% and intensity by approximately 13%, with more pronounced frequency deficits exceeding 26% specifically for winter bomb cyclones. These biases are dynamically driven by misrepresented meridional temperature gradients, which contribute to weaker and meridionally displaced upper-tropospheric jets and reduced peak baroclinic instability, thereby suppressing ETC formation and intensification. We further reveal that regional ETC frequency prediction skill during their respective peak seasons is limited to approximately 9–18 d, with substantial regional contrasts: the longest predictability horizon extends over the North Pacific, whereas the horizon is shortest over the North Atlantic. These regional differences are associated with variations in the dominant large-scale atmospheric drivers and their predictability over different regions. These findings establish an event-based benchmark for evaluating subseasonal ETC predictions and underscore key forecast bottlenecks in current S2S systems. Improving the representation of large-scale baroclinic environments and further unravelling the interactions between regional ETC activity and predictability sources will be essential for advancing reliable subseasonal predictions of ETC-related hazards.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba9f.title: Victoria mode drives the strengthening of tropical Atlantic SST influence on El Niño–Southern Oscillation since the mid-20th century
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba9f.authors: Zheng, Y., Chen, S., Kug, J., Wang, Z. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeba9f.abstract: Abstract Spring tropical North Atlantic (TNA) sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies serve as an important precursor of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) development in the following winter. The influence of TNA SST on ENSO has strengthened significantly since the mid-20th century, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Using large-ensemble simulations, AGCM experiments, and the PCMCI algorithm, we demonstrate that the North Pacific Victoria Mode (VM) is the key modulator of the recent enhancement of TNA SST influence on ENSO. Since the mid-20th century, the North Pacific climate state has shifted toward the negative VM phase, strengthening northeasterly trade winds and enhancing wind–evaporation–SST (WES) feedback over the subtropical northeastern Pacific. This background change amplifies the subtropical Pacific SST response to TNA-induced atmospheric anomalies, facilitating their subsequent extension into the tropical Pacific through WES feedback and ultimately modulate ENSO development via tropical air–sea interaction. Our results reveal that decadal variation in the North Pacific climate system substantially modulates the tropical Atlantic–ENSO teleconnection.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb9fd.title: Scale-aware emergent constraints on Tibetan Plateau warming: contrasting global and regional predictors
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb9fd.authors: Wang, J., Du, J., Wang, C., Dong, W. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aeb9fd.abstract: Abstract Emergent constraints are increasingly used to reduce uncertainty in regional climate projections by exploiting relationships across models between observable historical predictors and projected changes. However, the choice of historical window and predictor scale can strongly affect constraint performance. Using the Tibetan Plateau (TP), a region of complex terrain, as a testbed, we compare two widely used predictors for constraining future TP warming: large-scale global mean surface air temperature (GSAT) and regional TP surface air temperature (TPSAT). We show that GSAT-based constraints are sensitive to the temporal evolution of external forcing and are strongest for windows beginning around 1980, consistent with the differing historical effects of greenhouse gases and aerosols. In contrast, TPSAT-based constraints generally become stronger with longer windows, indicating that extended records help suppress internal variability and better reveal the regional forced signal. At the local scale, GSAT performs better in lower-elevation regions, whereas TPSAT is more skillful over high-elevation and topographically complex areas where regional process-related signals, including cryosphere-related feedbacks, may be more important. Motivated by this spatial contrast, we develop a scale-aware constraint framework that selects the locally preferred predictor at each grid point and reduces projection uncertainty relative to either single-predictor approach over large parts of the Plateau. These findings highlight the importance of scale-aware observational constraints and may inform constrained projections in other high-elevation and topographically complex regions.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdb.title: How intermittent piped water supplies impact households and coping strategies: a systematic review
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdb.authors: Broyles, L., Chavarria, K., Weston, S., Amankwaa, G. et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdb.abstract: Abstract More than a billion people globally use a piped water system that is an intermittent water supply (IWS), where water is often unavailable from the network. Previous reviews have summarized relationships between IWS, water quality, human health risks, and coping costs. Yet, beyond these documented impacts, IWS bears additional—often invisible—burdens on users comprising both financial and non-financial costs and social and health burdens. We conducted a systematic review to document these burdens by searching databases for publications that described human impacts of IWS and coping or adaptive management strategies at the household or individual level. We used a novel codebook of coping strategies and adaptive management to synthesize 140 studies meeting our inclusion criteria conducted in 36 countries between 1994–2023. The most frequently reported impacts were increased household spending, poor water quality, time lost managing water, livelihood disruptions, and hygiene/sanitation interruptions. We also found evidence of links between IWS and respiratory infections, vector-borne diseases, dietary changes, physical strain and injuries, dehydration, sleep disruption, psychosocial stress, and interpersonal violence. The most common coping strategies were related to water storage, purchasing, and acquisition costs. Unpredictable IWS was most commonly linked to a small set of household impacts. This review demonstrates that the impacts of IWS on households are more diverse than previously synthesized and highlights the importance of interdisciplinary work to support sustainable solutions that mitigate adverse household impacts of IWS systems.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Mapping climate change research: a bibliometric and topic modelling analysis
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: Climate change research has expanded at an unprecedented pace, generating a vast and fragmented body of scholarship that often obscures broader intellectual patterns and critical gaps. This study employs a large-scale bibliometric analysis combined with Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling to map the field’s intellectual structure and evolution. Analyzing 346,589 peer-reviewed articles from the Web of Science, the research proceeds in two stages. First, an analysis of the entire corpus identifies 17 consolidated research patterns, synthesized into six thematic clusters: Earth System Dynamics & Modelling; Ecosystem Resilience, Biodiversity & Carbon; Human Behavior, Vulnerability & Perceptions; Governance, Policy & Institutional Responses; Technological Innovation & Methodological Development; and Regional & Urban Climate Research. Second, a focused analysis of recent literature (2020–2024) reveals nine emerging trends, highlighting a shift towards urban infrastructure, biodiversity dynamics, compound risks, and the socio-technical dimensions of decarbonization. The findings illustrate both the consolidation of established domains and the diversification of new priorities. By providing a systematic map of the climate change research landscape, this study contributes to a more integrated and actionable research agenda, helping to inform effective and equitable global responses to the climate crisis.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02489.title: Manifesting inspired landscapes: Implementing a plural valuation framework for landscape restoration in South Africa
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02489.authors: Ancois Carien de Villiers, Jessica J. Cockburn, Marja J. Spierenburg, Karen  Joan Esler
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02489.abstract: Abstract Context Plural valuation frameworks integrate different values of sustainability and could help navigate the often messy and contentious nature of multistakeholder collaborations to restore multifunctional landscapes. However, several literature reviews have concluded that this potential has not yet been realised in practice. Objectives To understand this theory–practice gap, a realist case study was implemented to explore the experience of a non-profit company, Living Lands, in adapting Commonland’s 4Returns framework to the contested and complex context of two South African landscapes. The framework is intended to enable a long-term perspective on landscape restoration, and deepen understanding on how livelihoods are supported by ecological, economic, and social outcomes emergent from social-ecological relationships. Methods Interviews with and participant observations of Living Lands, landscape community members, and other stakeholders were used to assess the implementation and outcomes of projects based on the framework. Data analysis included thematic coding of transcripts, fieldnotes, and documents. Results The 4Returns framework enabled collective sensemaking, and broadened the value of restoration. However, participants highlighted pitfalls of oversimplified linear understandings of complex challenges, particularly in terms of securing financial returns, engaging marginalised people as fellow stewards, and the role of inspiration (i.e. visioning, learning, and innovations). Conclusions To manifest the potential of plural valuation frameworks, implementation requires an active and continuous reflexive process to support practitioners in engaging with social-ecological relationships. This includes recognising marginalised community members as stewards and not passive beneficiaries of projects, and managing expectations while maintaining inspiration to weather setbacks inherent to transformative processes for landscape sustainability.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Development and application of a risk characterisation and categorisation approach for predicted road runoff concentrations
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Lian Lundy, Mike Revitt, Bryan Ellis
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Road runoff is a key source of pollution entering receiving waters yet identifying where its discharge is prejudicial to water quality remains a challenge. Addressing this need is an emerging policy and practical issue, with the recast EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive requiring identification of locations where separately piped runoff poses a risk to the environment or public health. As a contribution, this study presents a novel approach for the risk characterisation and categorisation of road runoff outfalls based on the comparison of predicted environmental concentrations (PECs) with derived predicted no-effect concentrations (PNECs). Specifically, an established emissions-based approach was used to predict concentrations of total suspended solids, zinc, copper, lead and cadmium in road runoff discharging from 126 sections of road under three rainfall scenarios (i.e. PECs). The development of PNECs involved the translation of water quality threshold values into equivalent runoff concentrations through a stepwise process incorporating bioavailability and partitioning behaviour (as appropriate), and a range of receiving water dilution factors (from 2:1 to 50:1). This allowed the calculation of risk characterisation ratios, enabling road runoff outfalls to be allocated into risk categories. Results indicate that total suspended solids and zinc present the greatest risk across sites, with dilution factors of 50:1 insufficient to mitigate impacts for all road sections under all scenarios. The proposed approach provides a transparent, adaptable tool to support the identification and prioritisation of high-risk road runoff outfalls, offering an evidence base for targeting where to install mitigation measures within integrated urban water management planning.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Quantifying the relationship between prescribed burning and wildfire severity in south-eastern Australia
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Charlie Hart, Luke Collins, Tom A. Fairman et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: High-severity wildfires can pose a critical threat to society and forest ecosystems. While prescribed burning is widely applied to mitigate these risks, evaluation of its effectiveness at the landscape level remains challenging. Factors hindering these assessments include a lack of spatial data quantifying the amount of fuel treatment within burns, and challenges in controlling for variation in environmental conditions (e.g., weather, topography) that affect wildfire severity. We evaluated the effect of historical prescribed burns on wildfire severity in south-eastern Australia. We accounted for spatial variation in fuel treatments by objectively classifying the severity of ∼1300 prescribed burns conducted in the decade preceding each wildfire. Using a Random Forest modelling approach, we identified the key drivers of wildfire severity and employed counterfactual scenarios to quantify the landscape-scale influence of these prescribed burns while controlling the influence of environmental covariates. Overall, fire weather and aridity were the strongest drivers of wildfire severity. Recent prescribed burning reduced the extent of higher severity classes, relatively consistently across climatic conditions. Counterfactual scenarios showed that prescribed burning reduced the total area of the two highest wildfire severity classes (high canopy scorch and canopy burnt) by 6.2% (2882 ha) and nearly doubled the area that remained unburnt within treated areas. Our findings support the strategic use of prescribed burning to reduce the extent of high-severity fire. However, managers must remain mindful of the ecological trade-offs from increased frequency of low intensity prescribed fire, to ensure that fuel reduction prescriptions support forest resilience in an ever-warming climate.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Life cycle assessment of marine biodiversity restoration: Case study of European flat oyster (Ostrea edulis) in Nora Lagoon
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Erica Gagliano, Stefano Spotorno, Gianni Brundu et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Marine ecosystem restoration is increasingly recognized as a key strategy to reverse biodiversity loss and support the recovery of ecosystem services. However, the environmental burdens generated by restoration activities are rarely quantified. This study investigates whether Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) can support the design and management of environmentally sustainable marine restoration interventions. Using the restoration of the European flat oyster ( Ostrea edulis ) in the Nora Lagoon (Italy) as a case study, a cradle-to-deployment LCA was performed, including adult collection, hatchery stage at laboratory scale, transportation, and field deployment. Environmental impacts were assessed and complemented by LCA-based biodiversity indicators, sensitivity analyses, and an evaluation of shell-based carbon sequestration potential. Results showed that the deployment phase was the main contributor to global warming potential, marine eutrophication, and biodiversity impacts, whereas hatchery stage dominated cumulative energy demand and water use. The nursery stage of laboratory rearing and the use of imported commercial feed emerged as major hotspots. Alternative scenarios based on renewable electricity and modified transport logistics reduced several impact categories, with local feed production providing potentially the most balanced improvements. Although restored oysters stored biogenic carbon, sequestration remained negligible compared with project emissions over a 10-year period. The study demonstrates that LCA is an effective decision-support tool for identifying environmental hotspots, optimizing restoration strategies, and integrating sustainability considerations into marine biodiversity restoration planning.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gloenvcha.2026.title: Relevance of traditional knowledge of food preservation for disaster preparedness and climate change adaptation in Pacific Islands: A case study from Nabuna Village, Koro Island
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gloenvcha.2026.authors: Filipe Veisa, Viliamu Iese, Rosiana Lagi, Hilda Waqa-Sakiti
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gloenvcha.2026.abstract: Pacific Island communities face significant challenges from climate-related hazards, particularly tropical cyclones, which can disrupt food systems and undermine food security. Traditional Knowledge (TK) provides locally grounded knowledge of environmental conditions, seasonal patterns, food preservation and weather observation, but its transmission and use are changing alongside sociocultural and technological developments. This study examines traditional food preservation, seasonal knowledge and weather forecasting in Nabuna Village, Koro Island, Fiji, with particular attention to their use and transmission across generations. A qualitative case study was conducted, informed by resilience theory and socio-ecological systems (SES) thinking. Data were collected through six age-and gender-stratified focus group discussions with 30 participants aged 18–89 years and analyzed thematically to examine food preservation practices, seasonal indicators, weather forecasting and intergenerational knowledge transmission. Participants described pit storage of root crops, drying and smoking of fish, and seasonal preservation and use of breadfruit and yams in relation to the Fijian traditional calendar ( Vula Vakaviti ) and environmental indicators. Older participants described using ecological cues, including changes in cloud patterns, wind direction, bird behavior and food availability, when anticipating weather conditions and preparing food and water. Younger participants reported greater reliance on radio, television, mobile phones and social media for formal weather information, alongside varying familiarity with traditional indicators. The findings indicate the continued coexistence of traditional and formal sources of environmental information, while transmission and use of traditional knowledge vary across generations. The study highlights the context-specific relevance of traditional food preservation and environmental knowledge for understanding community responses to climatic and sociocultural change, while recognizing that the qualitative evidence does not independently establish causal effects on food security, adaptative capacity or disaster outcomes.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: This article examines the effect of women’s political empowerment on climate change vulnerability, from a sample of 39 sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries observed over the period 1995–2023, by mobilizing a fixed-effects country and time model estimated by the Two-Way Fixed Effect (TWFE). Two main results emerge: on the one hand, women’s political empowerment directly reduces climate vulnerability in SSA; on the other hand, political stability, democracy, and corruption control amplify this effect, while religion, ethnic, and linguistic fractionalization mitigate it. The model remains sensitive to digital, environmental, and socioeconomic variables. These results suggest strengthening women’s political empowerment, consolidating formal institutions, adapting policies to cultural and religious contexts, and integrating socioeconomic and environmental dimensions into climate adaptation strategies.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149962.title: Veganism in the city: Capitalist assimilation or multispecies resistance?
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149962.abstract: Cities are spaces in which consumerism, culture, and protest must often comingle. Often concentrated in urban spaces, veganism—which advocates alternative consumption, multispecies multiculturalism, and resistance to harmful foodways and unequal multispecies relationships—offers an interesting case study of urban consumerist dynamics. Using semiotic analysis of signs, posted menus, advertisements, and window displays collected between 2021 and 2022 in one university town in southeast England, it is considered how veganism might be able to persist, perhaps even thrive, in capital-serving cityscapes. Findings suggest that veganism is strained by the marketplace function of the city. Veganism is reduced to a form of consumption that aligns with capitalist interests, and anti-speciesist representations of veganism are lacking. Yet, this study also considers if the prevalence of vegan signage could be moderately subversive in normalizing veganism. These complexities are considered in the context of geographical and sociological research on cities as sites of both corporate co-optation of protest and social change.
