https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150579.title: Provisioning otherwise: Platform co-operatives and the reworking of platform urbanism
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150579.abstract: Urban life is increasingly organised through platforms, but platform urbanism has largely been understood through corporate intermediation, extraction and regulation. This article asks what becomes visible when platformisation is approached instead through the politics of provision. Drawing on 31 semi-structured interviews across a translocal platform co-operative ecosystem, it examines how co-operatively governed digital infrastructures make shared provision workable across places. The article develops platformed mutual provisioning to describe a recursive process through which dispersed capacities are assembled around situated needs, extended through federation and kept collectively governable through maintenance, democratic learning and data stewardship. The findings show that platform co-operatives matter less as ownership alternatives in themselves than as fragile experiments in organising the coordinating capacities on which food systems, logistics and civic economies increasingly depend. Their significance lies in keeping those capacities revisable as they become infrastructural to everyday provision. The article argues that this opens a wider politics of co-operative infrastructural urbanism, in which digital urbanisation is judged not by growth or technological novelty, but by whether the power to coordinate provision remains answerable to those who depend upon it.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150348.title: Companions, not just services: What do experiences of time teach us about urban vegetation?
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150348.abstract: Urban nature literature often describes urban vegetation in terms of its ‘ecosystem services’ such as carbon sequestration, air filtering, noise reduction and soil permeability, among others. Studies also note that green spaces foster social cohesion by providing places for social encounters and activities. Nevertheless, the bodily and sensorial relationships that urban dwellers create with urban vegetation are overlooked within these accounts. From an anthropological view that understands places as human and other-than-human entanglements, urban dwellers’ relationships with vegetation are poorly captured by the more transactional concept of ‘ecosystem services’. In this commentary, I bring to light shared temporalities between urban walkers and vegetation to argue for a closer look at the intertwined complexities of human and more-than-human cohabitation. Based on ethnographic research in Osorno, a small city in southern Chile – often referred to as a ‘green city’ because of its abundant vegetation – I delve into the experiences and narratives that emerge from people’s everyday contact with urban vegetation through their everyday journeys on foot. They invite us to rethink what urban nature does to urban places and what it means for these walkers, which is more than just providing humans with some ‘services’. Here, I show how everyday encounters with urban vegetation invite people to experience time differently. People can attune to more-than-human temporalities through senses and affects, allowing them to recall past times and also be part of a cyclical time we – humans and other-than-humans – all share.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150349.title: Time as a commons: Collective temporal practices and the making of urban care infrastructures
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150349.abstract: The contemporary care crisis has prompted a surge of scholarly attention to urban care commons and bottom-up care infrastructures, with particular emphasis on their socio-spatial dynamics. By contrast, the temporal dynamics through which such formations are sustained have received limited attention. While previous research has engaged urban and institutional temporalities in relation to processes of commoning, the commoning of time itself remains underexplored as a pathway towards urban transformation. This article turns to the urban co-production of time, focusing on the temporal patterns that sustain one of the largest self-organised collective kitchens in crisis-ridden central Athens. The kitchen mobilises dozens of residents in daily food provisioning and redistribution, preparing and sharing hundreds of warm meals 6 days a week. The scale and continuity of the initiative provide a unique empirical lens for understanding the organisational and meaning-making practices, at the temporal level, that make informal urban care infrastructures possible. Drawing on 10 months of ethnographic fieldwork, the article illuminates both the temporal resources (clock-time hours) and the temporal orientations (valuations of time beyond clock-time) that underpin alternative arrangements of social provisioning. The findings introduce the concept of collective time work to describe how otherwise temporally fragmented urban communities pool time and remake temporal norms to create cohesive community care. Conceptually, the article advances time as a relational, co-produced good, rather than an individually managed resource, to foreground the politics of time as a vital vector for transforming how care is organised and sustained in cities.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149718.abstract: In contemporary urbanism, healthcare real estate plays the dual role of essential social infrastructure and financial asset. On the one hand, healthcare real estate functions as a vital form of social infrastructure, shaping patterns of accessibility, belonging, and resilience in cities. On the other hand, it is increasingly governed as a financial asset through public-private partnerships (PPPs), real estate investment trusts (REITs), and institutional investment. This article conceptualises healthcare real estate as a form of financialised social infrastructure situated at the intersection of public service provision, financial investment, and urban governance. Drawing on evidence from the UK healthcare estate, the article examines how healthcare real estate has become increasingly embedded within circuits of capital accumulation and integrated into broader processes of financialised urbanism. The analysis demonstrates that financialisation has reshaped the financing and governance of healthcare real estate, expanding the role of institutional investors and private capital and reinforcing investment logics within healthcare provision. While these developments can mobilise capital for infrastructure investment and estate modernisation, they may also generate governance challenges relating to ownership, accountability, accessibility, and spatial equity. The article contributes to urban studies by advancing understanding of healthcare real estate as a form of financialised social infrastructure and examining its implications for health equity and sustainable urban development. It further explores the potential of impact investment as a mechanism for reconciling financial and social objectives, highlighting the importance of impact evaluation frameworks in aligning private capital with broader social and spatial outcomes.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150418.authors: Renata Motta, Anne Cathrin Ziegler, Maria Eugênia Trombini
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150418.abstract: This article examines urban food commons by tracing the emergence of food cultivation and preparation initiatives in urban peripheries, including occupied and contested territories. Nutritional studies often classify urban occupations and housing projects as food deserts or food swamps. Drawing on feminist political ecology, decolonial feminist perspectives on urban commons and care and Black Food Geographies, our research reframes these environments not as deficient but as care infrastructures where commoning practices among plants, people and place are enacted. The research focuses on community gardens and solidarity kitchens in the Brazilian metropolitan region of Belo Horizonte, based on fieldwork and focus groups with members from a state–society network of food activists that have shaped the alternative food system in Belo Horizonte in the last three decades. Beyond the binary of ‘social fixes’ for capitalist urbanisation and localised prefigurative spaces of post-capitalist difference, we treat community gardens and kitchens as spaces for (re)organising social reproduction, reproducing a socio-natural network and providing care that can unlock transformative potentialities. Furthermore, we claim that these urban food commons sparked renewed state commitment, transforming not only the political ecology of food and the urban landscape in the peripheries of Belo Horizonte but also state policies, aiming at promoting state-commons. Tensions remain, however, considering the relationships between autonomy in commoning practices and the state. Our article contributes to discussions of urban food commons by examining their relational dynamics with the state.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150345.title: Remembering what is: Indigenising reflections of an urban landscape
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150345.abstract: Melbourne city as it exists today is a colonial project with a history of destruction, exclusion and denial of local First Nations sovereignty on Wurundjeri Country. This fact is taken for granted in the urban environment today whereby acknowledgement of Wurundjeri presence in this location is presented as in the past, with little explanation or accountability offered as to the transition from Wurundjeri custodianship of Country to present modern urbanity. Country, as understood by Wurundjeri people, extends beyond the landscape to include social, temporal and spiritual dimensions. Recent efforts to reconcile Melbourne’s colonial history reflect these multiple dimensions. In this brief article, I reflect on place-making and historical narrative in urban Melbourne on Wurundjeri Country from a non-Indigenous perspective. To combat narrow colonial understandings of Melbourne’s history, and complement reconciliatory efforts, Country is discussed as a multidimensional conceptual framework which could be applied to encourage a greater sense of appreciation for Wurundjeri Country, the past, and an inclusive social future on common ground.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149800.title: Blind spots of state spatial selectivity: The left-behind secondary cities in Chinese mega-regionalisation
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149800.authors: Yizhao Du, Rodrigo Viseu Cardoso, Roberto Rocco
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026149800.abstract: Chinese intra-regional unevenness remains unresolved, despite mega-regionalisation being promoted as the main instrument of state spatial selectivity aimed at alleviating polarisation and peripheralisation in secondary cities. We argue that a largely overlooked intermediate stage of such processes is partly responsible for the uneven outcomes of mega-regionalisation in tackling these challenges. This stage bridges mega-regional visions initiated by top-level authorities and practical interventions at the local scale, organised in action plans that determine relations between core and secondary cities by state actors at the provincial level. We select three representative Chinese mega-regions and examine the yearly reports from 2006 to 2024 of their provincial governments (acting as mega-regional coordinators) to summarise the various mechanisms and periodic trends of these plans through the analytical lens of historical institutionalism. We find that the intermediate stage, focused on spatial reconfiguration, redistribution of urban functions, and improving regional accessibility, emphasises cores as the driving force, leaving blind spots that allow only a few secondary cities to integrate and benefit from mega-regionalisation, whereas many more are further polarised and peripheralised. This is evidenced in all cases despite their different trends in specific action plans. We highlight the impact of intermediate-stage action plans on secondary cities to extend spatial selectivity theory to multi-scalar state-led regionalisation processes and call for policy and governance attention to intermediate-stage coordination mechanisms that allow representation of secondary cities in mega-regional planning.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02499.title: How fire mosaics influence landscape connectivity and genetic diversity of two Australian bat species
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02499.authors: Amanda Lo Cascio, Robyn E. Shaw, Holly Sitters et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02499.abstract: Abstract Context Dispersal is a fundamental ecological and evolutionary process, influencing population dynamics, and shaping biodiversity. Spatial and temporal variation in fire mosaics can influence gene flow and genetic diversity through effects on individual dispersal. Objectives We investigated the influence of fire mosaics on effective dispersal in two Australian microbat species with contrasting mobility, Chalinolobus morio and Vespadelus vulturnus , to predict species’ capacities to persist in changing environments. Methods In the heathy woodlands of south-east Australia, we used genomic, spatial and environmental data at multiple scales. We examined population level and within population fine-scale genetic structure, and landscape connectivity, which together serve as indirect proxies for effective dispersal (dispersal followed by successful reproduction). These analyses allowed us to assess how fire mosaics influence dispersal pathways and identify potential barriers or sex-biases to dispersal. Results Both species showed limited population subdivision. Vespadelus vulturnus exhibited isolation by distance and fine-scale genetic structure consistent with dispersal limitation, whereas C. morio showed only weak fine-scale structure and no isolation by distance. Spatial genetic patterns were consistent with each species’ scale-dependent responses to the fire mosaic: in C. morio genetic distance decreased with the amount of late-successional habitat at the 3 km scale (a weak signal consistent with enhanced gene flow), whereas in V. vulturnus genetic distance decreased with fire-age diversity and edge density, and increased with late-successional habitat. Genetic diversity showed no significant response to fire mosaics in either species, although weak negative associations with the amount of long-unburnt vegetation in V. vulturnus at broader scales (5–6 km) may indicate that habitat features limiting movement erode diversity over longer timeframes. Conclusions Fire-mediated differences in habitat suitability can influence gene flow, shaping genetic structure and landscape connectivity. Microbat genetic structure is consistent with the species’ traits and ecological requirements, thereby linking post fire habitat succession to genetic response in fire-prone landscapes.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Interpretable machine learning for seasonal nitrate and total phosphorus concentrations integrating hydrologic, land-use, and ecological indicators
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Gbenga Daniels, Meghna Rajbhandari, Amanda Carneiro Marques
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Diffuse nutrient pollution remains difficult to assess because nutrient concentrations reflect interacting watershed, hydrochemical, ecological, and hydrologic conditions that vary across space and time. Although machine-learning models incorporate multiple environmental predictors, the contribution of different predictor domains can be difficult to distinguish when all variables are evaluated simultaneously. This study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework to predict seasonal nitrate and total phosphorus concentrations across seven watersheds in southeastern Pennsylvania using observations from 2002 to 2024. Physicochemical, land-cover, ecological, climatic, and hydrologic information were progressively integrated through four predictor scenarios, allowing the added predictive value of each domain to be evaluated. Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were independently optimized for each scenario. Predictive performance improved as broader environmental information was incorporated, with the largest gain occurring after land-cover variables were added to the physicochemical baseline. The environmental-only M4 XGBoost models achieved test R 2 values of 0.858 for nitrate and 0.770 for total phosphorus, with RMSE values of 0.624 and 0.170 mg L −1 , respectively. Repeated site-stratified validation of the nitrate M4 model yielded a mean test R 2 of 0.834 ± 0.026, indicating stable performance across alternative partitions. SHapley Additive exPlanations identified forest cover, developed land cover, and specific conductance as dominant predictors for both nutrients, while discharge contributed more strongly to nitrate and dissolved oxygen to total phosphorus prediction. These reveal that land-cover composition offers significant prognostic insights beyond in-stream conditions, whereas hydrochemical and hydrologic factors aid in differentiating nutrient-specific trends. The framework could guide the prioritizing of watershed monitoring and the evaluation of nutrient dynamics.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f3.title: The accelerating northward expansion of the South Asian High has slowed regional sea ice melt in the Arctic
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f3.authors: Bingyi Wu, Siqin Xie, Yuqing Sha et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f3.abstract: Summer Arctic sea ice affects Arctic shipping, the regional ecological environment, atmospheric blocking highs, and even the subsequent East Asian winter monsoon variability; consequently, the mechanisms governing its evolution have received extensive attention. This study investigates impacts of the South Asian High (SAH) on the slowdown of Arctic regional sea ice melt through diagnostic analyses and nudging experiments. Results show that the northward expansion of the SAH has strengthened Arctic tropospheric westerlies and intensified the polar vortex over the Arctic Ocean and the Pacific sector of the Arctic. These changes have slowed summer sea ice melt in the Pacific sector of the Arctic by reducing surface net shortwave radiation and enhancing anomalous sea ice drift into the region. More importantly, the coupling between the northward expansion of the SAH and the changing Arctic has systematically strengthened since the early 2000s. This northward expansion acts as the key driver in the dynamical linkage between the intensified Arctic tropospheric westerlies and the occurrence of extreme heatwaves in the region from the Yangtze River basin to the south of Japan. On decadal timescales, this study reveals an identical turning point of both the northward expansion of the SAH and the Arctic summer 500-1000 hPa thickness pattern, which corresponds well to the onset of accelerated oceanic warming in the North Pacific. Simulation experients show that global sea surface temperatures has driven the accelerating northward expansion of the SAH, rather than Arctic sea ice melt. The findings of this study suggest that the northward expansion of the subtropical systems has profound implications for the changing Arctic ecosystem.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdc.title: Biodiversity credits hold promise, yet credit-generating protocols require safeguards to realize potential
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdc.authors: Katherine A. Culbertson, Sarah Federman, Lucia Catherine Camp, Matthew D. Potts
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdc.abstract: Given the existing gap in biodiversity funding, mobilizing private finance will be essential to achieving global biodiversity conservation goals, especially across lower- and middle-income countries with limited capacity and public finance. The emerging voluntary biodiversity market (VBM) holds promise to leverage private finance for biodiversity, but credit-generating protocols must be robust to prevent greenwashing and maximize effectiveness. In this study, the first to move beyond theoretical critiques and general market assessments of the VBM, we extracted details of program structure and crediting issuance from protocols for 13 relatively well-established biodiversity-crediting organizations. With these data, we evaluated protocols’ alignment with both conservation and restoration biology principles and lessons learned from the voluntary carbon market (VCM). We find that action must be taken to improve quantification of biodiversity impacts, especially incorporating patch size and connectivity in crediting and assessing projects on ecologically relevant timelines. Further, safeguards for additionality, leakage, risk, and verification from the VCM must be more robustly integrated in the VBM, and deep engagement and investment in local communities must be improved to ensure durable biodiversity-positive outcomes.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f4.title: Mitigating downstream thermal stress and hydropeaking through reservoir operation in Alpine systems
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f4.authors: Maria Elena Alfano, Davide Poggi, Laura Savoldi, Marta Zaniolo
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f4.abstract: Multi-objective reservoir optimization plays a key role in managing water scarcity and growing uncertainty in hydrological inputs in sensitive mountain environments. While existing computational frameworks for multi-objective operation are effective in balancing traditional competing uses such as hydropower production and water supply, they often provide a simplified representation of environmental impacts. In particular, operationally driven alterations of flow regimes (hydropeaking) and downstream water quality, especially water temperature, are rarely incorporated as explicit objectives, despite representing some of the most critical stressors on Alpine riverine ecosystems. In this work, we advance the representation of environmental impacts in reservoir operation frameworks by coupling a classic hourly mass balance with a physically based energy balance, which explicitly resolves reservoir-induced water temperature alterations. We design reservoir operating policies that seek to minimize thermal stress and hydropeaking, and maximize hydropower revenue and irrigation reliability through Evolutionary Multi-Objective Direct Policy Search. Applied to the Ceresole reservoir in Gran Paradiso National Park (Italy), the framework generates a Pareto front that balances the four objectives. The revenue cost of reducing hydropeaking and thermal stress grows steeply as the two objectives approach their minima, while in the rest of the front the three non-economic objectives are loosely coupled and can be improved together. The most effective strategies mitigate thermal stress by advancing winter drawdown and managing summer storage levels to buffer the seasonal stratification cycle, achieving a substantial reduction in thermal alteration at a modest cost to hydropower revenue. Relative to the historical operation, policies with revenue within 1% of the baseline value reduce irrigation deficit, thermal stress and hydropeaking by up to 63%, 32% and 33%. Ecosystem-aware operation can therefore reduce several stressors while preserving economic value, an approach that can be tested in other Alpine systems under climate pressure.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f2.authors: Lei Jin, Yixiong Lu, Jianping Tang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f2.abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) power is central to China’s carbon neutrality strategy, but the extent to which mitigation reshapes the climate resource base for PV generation remains uncertain. Here we combine Earth system simulations with a 0.1°-resolution deep learning downscaling framework to quantify changes in China’s meteorological PV potential under divergent emission pathways. This asymmetric response reduces interprovincial disparities in solar resource availability. Factor-separation analyses attribute most changes to shortwave radiation rather than temperature or wind speed, consistent with aerosol-related brightening under stringent mitigation. Our findings reveal that carbon neutrality functions not merely as a climate corrective but as a potential driver of energy security, potentially contributing to a solar landscape with greater spatial equity and resilience.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f6.title: Diagnostic analysis of the prolonged 2022 South Asia heatwave
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f6.authors: Narayana Reddy Karrevula, Binisia Sanatan, Diana Francis et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f6.abstract: The 2022 South Asian heatwave was among the most extreme events recorded in the past half-century, with temperature anomalies exceeding 6°C in several regions. However, the large-scale processes governing its evolution, persistence, and spatial expansion remain insufficiently understood. Using reanalysis, satellite, and observational datasets, this study investigates the synoptic- and planetary-scale conditions associated with two distinct phases: 11–30 March and 31 March–20 April 2022. Phase-I was characterized by enhanced quasi-geostrophic stationary wave activity, a persistent heat dome over South Asia, and vertically coherent warm anomalies extending through much of the troposphere. Phase-II featured the spatial expansion of the heatwave from Southwest Asia toward Central and South Asia, coinciding with a transition of the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) from its positive to negative phase. The contrasting phases also exhibited distinct surface energy-budget characteristics, with Phase-I associated with enhanced radiative forcing and Phase-II characterized by stronger sensible heating, enhanced downward longwave and net radiation, and comparatively weak latent heat flux, consistent with reduced evaporative cooling. The broader-domain analysis further indicates that the Phase-II response extended beyond the core heatwave region. These findings highlight the potential role of NAO-related circulation variability in the regional evolution of the heatwave and demonstrate that its contrasting phases were associated with different combinations of large-scale atmospheric dynamics and land–atmosphere interactions.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f5.title: Anthropogenic warming intensified the July 2023 North China extreme rainfall event: Roles of moisture transport and convective organization
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f5.authors: Yuting He, J. B. Wang, Jinming Feng et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec4f5.abstract: In late July 2023, North China experienced a devastating extreme precipitation event, resulting in severe flooding and massive economic losses. While extreme circulation patterns, abundant moisture transport, and local topography have been identified as the key drivers, the specific role of anthropogenic warming remains elusive. By comparing hindcast simulations of the actual event with a counterfactual scenario representing a climate without anthropogenic interference, we calculate that human-induced warming increased total precipitation by 7.6% and amplified the risk for extreme precipitation at the 400 mm threshold by 9.6%. We further find that anthropogenic warming enhanced water vapor transport to North China, with the largest contributions from the South China Sea and Central China. Additionally, warming facilitated the development of more organized convective systems, characterized by fewer but larger convective clusters, alongside increased precipitation intensity and spatial extent. Our findings reveal the roles of moisture transport and convective structure associated with anthropogenic warming during this extreme rainfall event, highlighting the escalating threats posed by such extremes to communities, infrastructure, and economies.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.authors: Jose Maria Castillo-Secilla, José M. Palomares, Joaquín Olivares
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.abstract: Pavement crack analysis is a representative benchmark problem for intelligent visual inspection, requiring detection of thin, low-contrast, topologically irregular structures under severe class imbalance. Existing surveys remain fragmented across levels of abstraction, typically addressing algorithmic performance, data acquisition, or management systems in isolation. This survey provides a system-oriented synthesis based on a unified taxonomy with three functional layers: (i) data acquisition and sensing; (ii) crack detection and analysis algorithms, from classical vision to advanced Deep Learning, including foundation models, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Vision-Language Models (VLMs); and (iii) downstream applications, comprising predictive maintenance and Digital Twins. Public datasets and evaluation practices are reviewed, examining how task formulation, annotation granularity, sensing modalities, and acquisition conditions affect evaluation validity and generalization. Computational and deployment considerations (efficiency, interpretability, scalability, and robustness) are then discussed to guide the development of pavement crack analysis solutions that are both scientifically rigorous and practically deployable.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70390.abstract: Time‐based rates are widely used in risk communication, yet little is known about how their framing shapes perception and behavior. This article distinguishes between two common frames of rate—the average‐time frame (e.g., “one death every 30 seconds”) and the average‐outcome frame (e.g., “two deaths every minute”). Four studies were conducted to examine the rate framing effects on perceived risk and behavioral intention. A pilot text analysis of Weibo posts showed that the average‐time frame was relatively more prevalent in COVID‐19 risk communication and generated higher user engagement. Across three studies ( N = 979), we found that the average‐time frame elicited higher perceived risk than the average‐outcome frame, and such a rate framing effect weakened as the objective risk level increased. Moreover, framing information in an average‐time format effectively promoted intentions to limit sedentary behavior. These findings identify a new framing effect in risk communication and offer practical implications for designing persuasive public health messages.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08513.authors: Ekky Amiral Faqi, Ragil Andika Yuniawan, Samuel Jonson Sutanto
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08513.abstract: Landslides are one of the most devastating hazards globally, including in Indonesia. To reduce casualties, Indonesia has established the Blueprint of Indonesian Landslide Early Warning System (BILEWS). This system currently relies on rainfall-induced landslide thresholds for issuing the warning signals derived from historical landslide occurrences in Java, Sumatra, and Kalimantan Islands. However, landslide occurrence is strongly influenced not only by rainfall but also by antecedent soil moisture conditions and soil characteristics. Therefore, BILEWS still faces technical challenges in accurately predicting landslides, especially in Sulawesi and Papua Islands, where Java’s threshold is applied there. This study aims to enhance the existing rainfall thresholds and incorporate soil moisture into a multi-variable threshold framework. Specifically, rainfall thresholds, soil moisture thresholds, and the combination of rainfall-soil moisture thresholds are developed. In addition, the relationship between soil moisture and landslide occurrence is evaluated across different soil textures. The results indicate that the optimal thresholds vary across islands. The existing rainfall thresholds yield the highest performance in Java and the Sumatra Islands with Youden Index of 0.545 and 0.740, respectively. In Sulawesi Island, the best performed threshold is the newly developed rainfall threshold with a Youden Index of 0.477. The rainfall-soil moisture thresholds show optimum performance for Kalimantan (0.465) and Papua (0.458) Islands. Furthermore, soil moisture significantly affects landslide risks in sandy clay loam and loam soil textures. Developing thresholds based on significant soil textures improves the performance of landslide prediction.

Its predecessor, GFM v1, was already an open-access, globally operational web portal for rapid, analysis-ready flood mapping that runs entirely in the browser without coding, downloads, or data preprocessing; GFM v2 builds on this foundation without sacrificing that ease of use. Unlike fully-automatic monitoring services, which publish precomputed output from fixed, provider-set detection parameters and do not process every Sentinel-1 acquisition, GFM v2 gives users direct control over which acquisitions are processed and how: users can compare pre- and during-flood imagery, adjust detection thresholds and terrain masks to local conditions, and select any area and date, so that small-scale or localized events can be mapped more flexibly, whether or not an automated monitoring service has covered them. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08477.title: Projection of tropical cyclone wind-speed hazard curves under future climate scenarios for coastal design and resilience planning
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08477.authors: Jiahao Wang, Norberto C. Nadal-Caraballo, Yi Zhao et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s11069-026-08477.abstract: Abstract To reduce the impact of tropical cyclones (TCs) under uncertain future climate projections, developing TC hazard curves across a range of potential climate scenarios is essential for risk-informed resilience planning in coastal regions. Probabilistic TC hazard analyses typically rely on synthetic TC datasets, generated by full-track TC models that include genesis, track, and intensity/decay components. However, simulating the entire TC life cycle can accumulate biases from genesis and intensification stages, requires extensive environmental inputs and computational resources, and may inadequately represent landfall characteristics. To reduce these limitations, this study applies the synthetic TC datasets obtained from the ImpeRIal College Storm (IRIS) model. IRIS focuses exclusively on the post-lifetime maximum intensity (LMI) evolution. In addition, many prior studies primarily rely on two-dimensional (2D) slab TC wind field models or simpler models to expedite hazard analyses. This further reduces the reliability of the hazard analyses since 2D slab models integrate vertically across the boundary layer and treat the flow as height-invariant. This study leverages newly developed synthetic TC datasets and a height-resolving three-dimensional (3D) TC wind field model that accounts for intercity land-cover differences, and applies the peak over threshold–generalized Pareto distribution (POT-GPD) statistical model to generate TC hazard curves for various future climate scenarios at the state and city levels; and then assesses the changes in TC frequency and intensity under these scenarios. The results suggest an overall intensification of TCs and an increase in the total number of landfalling TCs, especially stronger TCs, under warmer climate scenarios.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Flood risk assessment frameworks under climate change: a review
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: Flood risk assessment (FRA) has become increasingly important under climate change, yet its conceptual and methodological foundations remain heterogeneous. This paper presents a systematic literature review, structured according to the ROSES reporting standards, that synthesises foundational, policy, general, sector-specific and site-specific approaches to FRA, with particular attention to the EU Floods Directive (2007/60/EC) and to highly influential flood-risk literature. Rather than judging specialised frameworks against a single universal model, the review distinguishes transferable methodological elements from context-dependent design choices. FRA is generally organised around combinations of hazard, likelihood, exposure, vulnerability, consequences and capacity, but these components are defined and operationalised differently across scales, sectors and decision contexts. Site-specific GIS and multi-criteria studies provide locally useful workflows whose indicators and weights require recalibration elsewhere, while infrastructure frameworks appropriately incorporate sector-specific data such as inspections, network criticality and operational thresholds. Methodological diversity is therefore partly necessary and becomes problematic mainly when definitions, assumptions and aggregation rules are not reported transparently. The synthesis links flood mechanisms to their analytical emphasis, users and decision purposes; outlines practical options for treating non-stationarity, including non-stationary frequency models, climate-model ensembles, joint-probability methods, stress testing and periodic updating; and proposes five design principles for future FRA. The review concludes that the appropriate goal is structured comparability, that is, transparent reporting of the flood mechanism, decision purpose, likelihood method, vulnerability construction, uncertainty and transferability conditions, rather than methodological homogenisation.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Scenario-based typhoon disaster risk and resilience assessment for universities in China
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: As representatives of climate-related catastrophes, typhoon disasters pose a significant threat to human well-being due to their high frequency, destructive nature, and complexity. Universities are pivotal and integral components of the social system, bearing the responsibility not only for traditional community functions but also for social education. Consequently, a novel requirement emerges to analyze typhoon disaster resilience within the context of university campuses, necessitating the establishment of a tailored and applicable resilience assessment framework. In response to these challenges, this paper formulates a university resilience assessment framework tailored explicitly to typhoon disasters, comprising five key dimensions: critical infrastructure, institutions, society, ecology, and economy. Subsequently, this study employs a cloud matter-element model (CMEM) to carry out a university resilience assessment, addressing the challenges associated with the fuzziness and randomness of resilience classification boundaries. As a case study, the resilience assessment of Shanghai Normal University under the impact of Severe Typhoon Muifa is utilized to validate the efficacy of the proposed framework. The research findings demonstrate that this framework is systematic and comprehensive, effectively integrating dynamic and static resilience aspects specific to typhoon disasters in universities, thereby providing fresh insights for enhancing university resilience. https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Detection of debris-flow-prone drainage basins through decision tree analysis based on debris-flow fans
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: Debris-flow fans serve as key geomorphic indicators of past debris-flow activity and potential future debris-flow hazards. This study tests the transferability of an existing decision tree developed using debris-flow fan distribution to independent drainage basins. The study area is located in the western Hidaka Mountains, Hokkaido, Japan, where numerous debris flows were triggered by heavy rainfall in 2003. The presence or absence of debris-flow fans was estimated using decision tree analysis based on drainage-basin morphology. The decision tree correctly classified fan presence or absence in 80% of the 235 drainage basins analyzed, including 76% of the 145 extension basins. Overestimation of debris-flow fans occurred in several basins; however, field surveys confirmed the presence of debris-flow deposits from the 2003 event, indicating that the decision tree could successfully identify hazardous basins even where fans have been eroded or artificially modified. Morphological indicators in most basins where debris-flow fans and occurrences were overlooked were close to the threshold for fan formation, demonstrating that decision tree analysis enables the effective identification of error sources, which is a clear advantage over more complex machine learning methods. Because debris-flow fans represent the long-term accumulation of debris-flow deposits, this approach can reliably detect hazardous basins, even in regions with low debris-flow frequencies. Furthermore, the topographic data required for debris-flow fan detection are more readily available than historical records of debris-flow occurrences. Therefore, decision tree analysis based on debris-flow fan distribution offers a practical, interpretable, and widely applicable tool for identifying drainage basins with high debris-flow potential.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: A multi-variable threshold approach to landslide prediction: integrating rainfall, soil moisture, and soil texture in Indonesia
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: Landslides are one of the most devastating hazards globally, including in Indonesia. To reduce casualties, Indonesia has established the Blueprint of Indonesian Landslide Early Warning System (BILEWS). This system currently relies on rainfall-induced landslide thresholds for issuing the warning signals derived from historical landslide occurrences in Java, Sumatra, and Kalimantan Islands. However, landslide occurrence is strongly influenced not only by rainfall but also by antecedent soil moisture conditions and soil characteristics. Therefore, BILEWS still faces technical challenges in accurately predicting landslides, especially in Sulawesi and Papua Islands, where Java’s threshold is applied there. This study aims to enhance the existing rainfall thresholds and incorporate soil moisture into a multi-variable threshold framework. Specifically, rainfall thresholds, soil moisture thresholds, and the combination of rainfall-soil moisture thresholds are developed. In addition, the relationship between soil moisture and landslide occurrence is evaluated across different soil textures. The results indicate that the optimal thresholds vary across islands. The existing rainfall thresholds yield the highest performance in Java and the Sumatra Islands with Youden Index of 0.545 and 0.740, respectively. In Sulawesi Island, the best performed threshold is the newly developed rainfall threshold with a Youden Index of 0.477. The rainfall-soil moisture thresholds show optimum performance for Kalimantan (0.465) and Papua (0.458) Islands. Furthermore, soil moisture significantly affects landslide risks in sandy clay loam and loam soil textures. Developing thresholds based on significant soil textures improves the performance of landslide prediction since no single threshold fits all.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Projection of tropical cyclone wind-speed hazard curves under future climate scenarios for coastal design and resilience planning
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: To reduce the impact of tropical cyclones (TCs) under uncertain future climate projections, developing TC hazard curves across a range of potential climate scenarios is essential for risk-informed resilience planning in coastal regions. Probabilistic TC hazard analyses typically rely on synthetic TC datasets, generated by full-track TC models that include genesis, track, and intensity/decay components. However, simulating the entire TC life cycle can accumulate biases from genesis and intensification stages, requires extensive environmental inputs and computational resources, and may inadequately represent landfall characteristics. To reduce these limitations, this study applies the synthetic TC datasets obtained from the ImpeRIal College Storm (IRIS) model. IRIS focuses exclusively on the post-lifetime maximum intensity (LMI) evolution. In addition, many prior studies primarily rely on two-dimensional (2D) slab TC wind field models or simpler models to expedite hazard analyses. This further reduces the reliability of the hazard analyses since 2D slab models integrate vertically across the boundary layer and treat the flow as height-invariant. This study leverages newly developed synthetic TC datasets and a height-resolving three-dimensional (3D) TC wind field model that accounts for intercity land-cover differences, and applies the peak over threshold–generalized Pareto distribution (POT-GPD) statistical model to generate TC hazard curves for various future climate scenarios at the state and city levels; and then assesses the changes in TC frequency and intensity under these scenarios. The results suggest an overall intensification of TCs and an increase in the total number of landfalling TCs, especially stronger TCs, under warmer climate scenarios.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Detection of a meteotsunami in the Colombian Caribbean and its role as a driver of coastal morphodynamics
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: On July 19, 2017, a high frequency sea-level fluctuation was observed in Santa Marta, Colombia, causing local coastal inundation. Local authorities attributed these tsunami-like waves to a submarine landslide, through no scientific study confirming this interpretation has been published. In this paper, we present an alternative hypothesis: that the tsunami-like waves were triggered by the passing of a squall line, which resulted in rapid, localised pressure disturbances, triggering sea surface level oscillations that were amplified to a meteotsunami via resonance effects in the shallow coastal waters of an abandoned delta lobe of the Magdalena River. We present GOES satellite observations and ERA-5 Reanalysis data to characterize the squall line and test whether resonance could have taken place. The persistence of strong wind and intense up- and downdrafts even in the hourly averaged ERA-5 data, the coincidence of the arrival of the system in shallow water with the detection of the tsunami-like waves in tide gauges, and the detected travel-speed of the system that supports resonance development lend support to the hypothesis. To our knowledge, no previous meteotsunamis have been reported in the Colombian Caribbean. To assess the geomorphic impact of such an event, this study analyzes wave-run-up and total water levels (TWL) associated with the event, finding that they are comparable to those observed during moderate storms in the area. We further show that the event drove significant geomorphic change by inducing breaching of a lagoon.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Global Flood Mapper v2: open-access flood mapping and exposure assessment with Sentinel-1 SAR
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: We present Global Flood Mapper v2 (GFM v2), which adds flood depth estimation, on-demand GeoTIFF export, cloud-based impact assessment against high-resolution land cover and five global population datasets to quantify exposure uncertainty, and parameter-encoded URLs for reproducibility and sharing. Its predecessor, GFM v1, was already an open-access, globally operational web portal for rapid, analysis-ready flood mapping that runs entirely in the browser without coding, downloads, or data preprocessing; GFM v2 builds on this foundation without sacrificing that ease of use. Unlike fully-automatic monitoring services, which publish precomputed output from fixed, provider-set detection parameters and do not process every Sentinel-1 acquisition, GFM v2 gives users direct control over which acquisitions are processed and how: users can compare pre- and during-flood imagery, adjust detection thresholds and terrain masks to local conditions, and select any area and date, so that small-scale or localized events can be mapped more flexibly, whether or not an automated monitoring service has covered them. By providing these capabilities in the browser without sacrificing user control, GFM v2 supports timely, evidence-based flood response and management.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.title: Mind the gap: Quantifying vegetation-gap frequency and length along least-cost routes among urban green spaces
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landurbplan.20.abstract: Urban green infrastructure planning for enhancing biodiversity can benefit from information about the connectivity between large green spaces and existing small, vegetated patches embedded within cities. While the importance of habitat connectivity for biodiversity is well established, the size and frequency of vegetation gaps between green spaces may influence functional connectivity within cities. LiDAR-derived vegetation height data were used to map potential vegetated corridors linking publicly managed green spaces in New York City, USA. Least-cost path models identified routes that preferentially followed high (>5 m), medium (1–5 m), and low (0.3–1 m) vegetation while excluding buildings and assigning higher costs to gaps in the selected vegetation class. Across 77,116 park pairs, routes were completed for 98.4–99.1 % of pairs, depending on vegetation class, but their gap patterns differed significantly. Mean (± SE) gap counts were 12.1 ± 0.3, 17.5 ± 0.3, and 25.6 ± 0.4 per route in high, medium, and low vegetation, respectively. Mean within-route gap lengths ranged from 11.9 ± 0.3 m (medium vegetation) to 15.1 ± 0.3 m (high vegetation), and 5.6–8.1 % of routes contained gaps exceeding 100 m. Short gaps accumulated, however: total gap length exceeded 100 m on 56–77 % of routes. These results suggest that existing urban vegetation forms potential corridors among public green spaces, but with extensive gaps in individual vegetation classes. By locating larger gaps and areas with limited vegetated access, this type of modeling can help direct habitat assessment and greening toward opportunities to improve ecological connectivity.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02483.title: Biodiversity and ecosystem services in changing landscapes: a biome level scenario assessment for continental Ecuador
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02483.authors: Hongmi Koo, Janina Kleemann, Pablo Cuenca et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02483.abstract: Abstract Context Ecuador hosts remarkable biogeographical areas, including the Coast, the Andes and the Amazon, which represent distinctive biomes. However, a comprehensive assessment accounting for biome-specific differences in the landscape as well as in biodiversity and ecosystem services (BES) across Ecuador is still lacking. Objectives This study tested an integrative approach that combines spatial modeling and participatory methods for the impact assessment of future scenarios (deforestation and afforestation) on BES. Important ecosystem services included food, drinking water, service water, soil erosion control, water flow regulation, pollination, macro climate regulation, and landscape aesthetic/amenity. Methods The BES were identified by experts through surveys and workshops. Additionally, the experts were involved in developing simulation conditions for the scenarios, which were applied in the spatially explicit modeling platform based on Geographic Information System and Cellular Automaton modules. Results The scenario impacts were visualized as changes in landscape configuration and BES capacities at the biome level. Regarding the deforestation scenarios, the Amazon biome showed the most notable change, with 11–13% of loss in most BES except food provision. However, the BES of the Andean biome presented the most evident trade-offs between BES by the afforestation scenarios with an approximately 10% decrease in food provision, while there was a 20–30% increase in other BES. BES capacity maps for all three biomes clearly showed that BES hotspots were reduced by the deforestation scenarios, whereas the afforestation scenarios expanded BES hotspots. Conclusions Experts’ feedback on the applied methods and the results confirmed the usefulness of the BES assessment for future landscape management with further consideration of how to transfer the findings into policy-related information.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Drivers of biodiversity in mineral extraction sites – a cross-taxa analysis with implications for management and restoration
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Katharina Schwesig, Vera Marie Alida Zizka, Christoph Scherber, Norbert Hölzel
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Extraction sites are often considered sources of environmental damage. However, in intensively used and nutrient-enriched landscapes they may also provide exceptional secondary habitats, shaped by disturbance and nutrient depletion. Their contribution to biodiversity across taxonomic groups remains insufficiently understood, and integrated guidelines for managing biodiversity during active extraction are needed. We examined terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity across twelve active German extraction sites of limestone, gypsum, sand and gravel. Data on vascular plants, soil parameters and six insect groups were collected via vegetation relevés, soil samples, DNA metabarcoding from trap samples and transect walks on 103 terrestrial plots. Aquatic diversity (Amphibia and Odonata) was assessed at 75 water bodies using transect walks and eDNA metabarcoding. Across all sites, we recorded 2054 species, including 168 threatened in Germany. Species composition varied strongly across substrate types and between plots. Terrestrial insect diversity increased with plant species richness, while higher latitude, which was correlated with sampling year, and the proportion of shrubs had negative effects. The respective insect groups showed group-specific responses to plot age, the proportions of open soil, active extraction area and surrounding grassland. To maximise conservation value, particularly for terrestrial insects, site management should promote habitat heterogeneity and allow the formation of temporary habitats through natural succession. Increasing vascular plant richness boosts local insect diversity. Embedding biodiversity management into the regional context can create networks of valuable secondary habitats. Extraction sites thus bear a high but so far underused potential to advance restoration targets beyond existing protected areas.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd4.title: Spatially distributed air quality and health impacts of data center electricity demand in the United States
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd4.authors: Yuang Chen, Shen Wang, Juan Ramon L Senga, Andrew Scott White, Anthony YH Wong, Lyssa M Freese, Michelle L Bell and Noelle E Selin
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbd4.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is driving substantial growth in electricity demand from data centers in the US, yet how the resulting air quality and public health impacts are distributed remain poorly quantified. To trace the ambient air pollution and associated premature mortality impacts of grid-supplied data center electricity demand in 2023, we couple the United States Electricity Generation Optimization model with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model. We compare hourly, unit-level electricity dispatch with and without data center demand to quantify changes in power-sector emissions, ambient PM and ozone, and associated premature mortality. Our results show that electricity generation attributable to data center demand is largely supplied by fossil fuel units across multiple regions, resulting in additional annual mean PM concentrations of 0.02–0.08 g m (local peak concentrations up to 0.2 g m ), and regionally varying ozone responses characterized by wintertime depletion and summertime enhancement. These impacts are most pronounced in the Midwest United States, where marginal emissions from coal-fired units and ammonia-rich atmospheric conditions enhance secondary particulate formation. We estimate that this grid-supplied demand is responsible for 513 (95% CI: 469–557) annual premature mortalities from PM and an additional 137 (95% CI: 90–183) annually from maximum daily 8 h average ozone (MDA8- ) in the contiguous US. State-level analysis reveals a systematic geographic mismatch: states hosting the largest data center loads do not necessarily experience the highest attributable mortality rates, while some states with little data center demand bear substantial burdens. This mismatch arises because of dispatch across interconnected electricity regions, regional differences in generation and emissions, and atmospheric chemistry and transport, which together separate the locations of demand from those of exposure and mortality. These findings highlight the importance of considering both air quality impacts and their spatial distribution in data center and macro-energy system planning.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: This Special Issue brings together fifteen contributions that examine how climate adaptation knowledge is generated, shared, and translated into action in the context of the EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change. https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Communicating heat risk: the psychological impact of naming and ranking heatwaves on threat perception & protective behavior
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: Extreme heat has emerged as the most lethal weather-related threat globally, yet warning systems often fail to motivate protective behavior, creating a critical gap in climate adaptation policy. Guided by the Extended Parallel Process Model, this study experimentally tests whether two communication cues borrowed from other hazard domains, personalized naming and categorical ranking, enhance public threat perception and protective intentions. A 2 × 2 randomized survey experiment ( N = 1,047) was conducted with a U.S. online sample, manipulating the presence of each cue in a standardized heatwave warning. Single-item Likert scales administered immediately after exposure measured the model’s three threat appraisal components (Perceived Severity, Perceived Vulnerability, and Fear) and Protective Behavioral Intentions. Linear regression models assessed main and moderation effects, controlling for demographic and climate belief covariates. Categorical ranking significantly increased all three components of threat appraisal. Naming had no measurable effect. Combining both cues was less effective than categorical ranking alone, suggesting a cognitive interference effect that may undermine complex messaging. The analyses also identified heterogeneity in how threat appraisal translates into protective intentions: men responded more strongly to fear and women to perceived vulnerability, while political affiliation moderated responses to perceived severity. These findings suggest that cognitive simplicity, not personalized naming, makes heat warnings more effective at raising perceived threat. They offer preliminary guidance for designing heat warning systems, pending replication across populations and real-world settings.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cities.2026.10.title: Assessing just access to urban ecosystem services through spatial multi-criteria decision modeling: Evidence from a Global South city, Dhaka
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cities.2026.10.abstract: Recent urban development in Dhaka has created injustices in access to Urban Ecosystem Services (UES), affecting resilience, health, and well-being. This study evaluates the status of justice in access to UES through spatial modeling. Four UES were analyzed: recreation and tourism (cultural), urban cooling (regulating), habitat quality (supporting), and water yield (provisioning), using the InVEST model. Accessibility within a 15-minute walk from ward centroids was assessed with the Enhanced Two-Step Floating Catchment Area method. In addition, a multidimensional environmental justice framework was operationalized to examine justice scenarios in Dhaka, using the Best–Worst Method. Finally, a composite Justice in Access to UES (JAU) Index was constructed by integrating UES supply, accessibility, and justice indicators through a fuzzy overlay operation. The findings highlight significant injustices in access to UES across Dhaka. The highest proportions of very low JAU values were observed for Cultural (51%) and Supporting (47%) UES. A clear divide emerged, with Dhaka South consistently lagging behind Dhaka North across all services. Dhaka North Ward 19 (Hatirjheel area) and Dhaka South Ward 03 (near Hatirjheel) recorded the highest JAU values across all UES types, yet large portions of the city remained underserved. Overall, the results demonstrate that justice in access to UES depends not only on supply or accessibility, but also on the interplay of spatial configuration, social vulnerability, and structural barriers. Addressing these injustices requires equity-focused urban planning to strengthen services in marginalized neighborhoods and promote inclusive, sustainable urban development in Dhaka.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ufug.2026.1297.title: Urban forests can be ecologically similar to the natural forests for sustaining flower-visitation network structure in highly urbanized South China
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ufug.2026.1297.authors: Kai Hao, Long-Long Chen, Ze‐Yu Tong et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ufug.2026.1297.abstract: Urban green spaces have been suggested to be the refuge for pollinator conservation amid the negative impacts of urbanization on insect richness and abundance. However, the extent to which urban green spaces are ecologically similar to the "natural" ones remains poorly understood. In the present study, species richness and community composition of plants, flower visitors, and the interacting network structure were compared between four natural forest communities and four urban forest communities in highly urbanized southern China. The effects of geographic distance and community composition of plants and visitors on species turnover, rewiring, and interaction variation were further examined. Our results suggested that both natural and urban forests exhibited generalized and nested flower-visitation networks, with Asteraceae plants serving as core species underpinning network structure. Compared to natural forests, urban forests exhibited significantly lower family-level species richness—but remarkably similar community composition—in both plant and flower-visitor assemblages. The interaction variation was positively correlated with geographic distance and visitor community dissimilarity across eight sites. In natural forests, visitor community dissimilarity and species turnover were identified as the significant factors contributing to interaction dissimilarity between networks. However, all these associations involving in spatial distance and network dissimilarity was absent in urban forests. These results highlighted the potential of urban green spaces, which can be similar on community structure and ecological function to the "natural" ones, for protecting wild pollinators in highly urbanized regions.

https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70413.title: Risk Assessment and Mitigation for International Multimodal Container Transport Networks Under Compound Flood and Tropical Cyclone Events
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70413.authors: Yifan Zhu, Ran Yan, Ran Yan
https://doi.org/10.1111/risa.70413.abstract: International multimodal container transport networks (IMCTNs) play a critical role in supporting modern logistics systems and global trade, yet they are increasingly exposed to the risk of climate extremes, particularly compound flood and tropical cyclone (TC) events. The cross-modal impact of such events and the resulting systemic risk to IMCTNs remain insufficiently understood. This study proposes a comprehensive methodological framework for assessing and mitigating risks in IMCTNs under compound flood-TC events. By integrating multimodal transport and multisource data with climate hazard information, the framework enables probabilistic simulations of compound events ranging from frequent disturbances to rare extreme events and multi-scale risk quantification at both the network and county levels. The framework proposes multiple component reinforcement strategies based on their criticality and disaster-specific failure characteristics, thereby informing the design of targeted risk mitigation strategies. Applying the framework to a real-world IMCTN in Mainland China, the results show that the relationship between network performance losses and events of different exceedance probabilities varies across probability ranges. Moreover, spatial heterogeneity is observed in that identical event probabilities lead to divergent losses across counties, which highlights the need for stratified monitoring frameworks for risk management. Finally, risk mitigation strategies accounting for both segment criticality and failure characteristics achieve superior effectiveness. The findings offer actionable guidance for risk mitigation in IMCTNs.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02458.title: Differentiated responses of ecosystem service supply and demand to urbanization across urban–rural gradients: a case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02458.authors: Tao Xu, Jinhan Guo, Guangjin Tian
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02458.abstract: Urbanization is closely associated with changes in ecosystem services, but how the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand vary along urban–rural gradients remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand across urban–rural gradients and to provide evidence for landscape planning and sustainable management in rapidly urbanizing regions. We assessed the supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios of four ecosystem services—water yield, carbon sequestration, habitat quality, and soil conservation—in China’s Yangtze River Delta region (YRDR) in 2000, 2010, and 2020. Spearman’s rank correlation analysis was used to identify associations between urbanization and ecosystem service supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios across urban–rural gradients. Random forest and SHAP analyses were then used to evaluate the relative explanatory contributions of urbanization indicators and their nonlinear associations. (1) Ecosystem service supply and demand showed marked spatial mismatches across the YRDR. With increasing urbanization, habitat quality deficits deepened and soil conservation surpluses narrowed, whereas the carbon sequestration supply–demand imbalance was alleviated in old urban areas. Water-yield supply–demand patterns were sensitive to the method used to spatialize demand. All urban–rural gradients showed surpluses when sectoral water demand was allocated to the corresponding land-use types. In contrast, supply–demand pressure increased markedly in highly urbanized areas when demand was allocated by population density. (2) Urbanization indicators were generally negatively correlated with ecosystem service supply and supply–demand ratios, with stronger correlations in rural areas. Except for soil conservation, demand for the other three services was mostly positively correlated with urbanization indicators. (3) In 2020, among the seven models that met the spatial predictive-performance criterion, impervious surface proportion had the highest relative explanatory contribution in six. However, conventional urbanization indicators had limited explanatory power in old urban areas and for the supply–demand ratios of water yield and carbon sequestration across most urban–rural gradients. Ecosystem service supply–demand patterns and their associations with urbanization varied with urban–rural landscape context, service type, and the method used to spatialize demand. Landscape planning should consider the spatial configuration of land development and the continuity of ecological spaces, with particular emphasis on development control and landscape connectivity restoration in urban–rural fringes.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: Plans Without Practice: Adaptive Risk Governance and the Normative–Organizational Gap in Metropolitan Santiago
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: Renn and Klinke’s [1] adaptive risk governance framework matches complex, uncertain, and ambiguous risks to risk-informed, precautionary, and discourse-based strategies respectively. We use it to interpret Chile’s Región Metropolitana de Santiago (RM), whose three successive regional planning instruments (2011–2035) were each designed around one of the three modes. We then ask whether exposure to the San Ramón fault, as the regional strategy delimits it, is associated with formal disaster risk management (DRM) institutionalization across the RM’s 52 communes, on a normative dimension (formalized plans) and an organizational one (a dedicated DRM unit and head). The two move in opposite directions: fault-exposed communes lead the region on formal plans, yet only one of the six had a DRM unit in 2023, created that year, against 43% elsewhere. A fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis finds land-use planning capacity near-necessary for institutionalization on both dimensions but no configuration sufficient for either; a Firth-corrected logistic regression, used because the outcome is close to separation, estimates a negative but imprecise association with having a DRM unit (odds ratio 0.17, p = 0.075). Both results survive alternative calibrations; the association is significant only when the sixth commune’s record is excluded, weakens under wider delimitations of the hazard zone, and is absent for a second seismic-hazard group. We read it as a robust pattern specific to the fault classification, not a deterministic effect, and interpret it cautiously as the operational layer that regional instruments mandate but do not create.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c2.title: Impacts of combined ambitious marine and terrestrial carbon dioxide removal on major ocean stressors
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c2.authors: Hao‐Wei Wey, Yiannis Moustakis, Tobias Nützel et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c2.abstract: Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation are major stressors impacting marine ecosystems. While Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) is necessary to meet climate targets, its potential to mitigate ocean stressors under realistic future scenarios remains understudied. Here, we use two Earth System Models to simulate ambitious deployments of Afforestation/Reforestation (AR) and Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) under the high emissions scenario SSP3-7.0. Six experiments with varying CDR magnitude and combination are analyzed. Combined AR and OAE robustly mitigates acidification, deoxygenation and warming, while mitigation on primary production and nitrate declines remains undetectable. Not all mitigation responses scale linearly with carbon removal due to the complex nonlinear interactions among ocean circulation, carbonate chemistry, and biological processes. The early detectability of pH mitigation signal highlights its value for CDR monitoring. Inter-model differences in subsurface oxygen responses appear to be closely linked to differences in mean-state ocean circulation and ventilation. These findings demonstrate that ambitious CDR can measurably alleviate ocean stress, while underscoring that emissions reductions remain essential to limit climate change impacts on marine ecosystems.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c3.title: From vector to barrier: the impact of road infrastructure modernization on forest fire risk in southwestern China
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c3.authors: Qinli Xiong, Igor Bogunović, Ting Li et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c3.abstract: Climate change is widely predicted to intensify global forest fire regimes. However, how socio-economic modernization and infrastructure development alter forest fire risks under a warming climate remains inadequately understood, particularly in biodiversity hotspots. Our study investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of forest fire occurrences in Yunnan, southwestern China, from 2000 to 2019. By using the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model and Redundancy Analysis (RDA), we analyzed the shifting relationships between forest fire occurrences and 14 environmental and anthropogenic drivers over time. We observed a distinct inverted U-shaped trajectory in potential fire occurrence area, characterized by rapid expansion in the earlier period (2000–2009) followed by significant contraction in the later period (2010–2019), despite a concurrent rise in regional temperatures. The primary driver of forest fire occurrences transitioned from annual mean temperature (41.6% importance in Period I) to population density (35.9% importance in Period IV). Furthermore, road density shifted from a positive predictor to a neutral factor post-2010, indicating that modernized highway networks no longer act as localized ignition vectors. Overall, this rapid expansion followed by contraction of potential forest fire occurrence area in Yunnan can be framed within an Environmental Kuznets Curve for forest fires, demonstrating that urbanization and high-standard infrastructure modernization can effectively decouple regional fire regimes from global warming trends.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c0.title: Satellite-based assessment of combustion-related and photosynthetic influences on XCO 2 variability across South Korea
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c0.authors: Na Rae Kim, Hyung Joo Lee
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c0.abstract: Several countries are committed to achieving carbon neutrality. Reaching net-zero emissions requires the accurate identification of high-emission regions and an understanding of the balance between carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) sources and sinks. This study estimated the high-resolution column-averaged dry air mole fractions of atmospheric CO 2 (XCO 2 ) across South Korea from May 2018 to April 2025 using a mixed-effects model. Satellite-observed carbon monoxide (CO) and solar-induced fluorescence (SIF) were used as proxies for combustion-related and photosynthetic activities, respectively. The estimation model demonstrated reasonably strong predictive performance, with a cross-validation R 2 of 0.64, mean absolute error of 0.73 ppm, and root mean squared error of 1.05 ppm. The estimated XCO 2 anomalies were elevated in major metropolitan areas and coastal industrial regions. Model results indicate that a 1 standard deviation (SD) increase in CO was associated with an average increase of 0.59 ppm in XCO 2 anomalies, whereas a 1 SD increase in SIF corresponded to an average decrease of 0.03 ppm. Spatially, the CO-attributable component of the XCO 2 variability was approximately 18 times larger than that associated with SIF. These results suggest that the variability in XCO 2 anomalies was more strongly associated with combustion-related signals (CO) than with photosynthetic activity (SIF) within our daily 10-km analysis. Our findings provide insights for supporting targeted mitigation strategies and improving the effectiveness of carbon management policies.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c8.title: Methodological uncertainty in soil organic carbon estimates and carbon-footprint reporting in woody cropping systems
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c8.abstract: Olive groves, almond orchards, fruit orchards and vineyards are promoted for soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. We reviewed 129 studies and propagated the errors of four common shortcomings into 0–30 cm SOC stocks, using the 87 studies with accessible and extractable soil data. Of 107 soil-sampling studies, 37 % sampled only the inter-row, 38 % sampled less than 30 cm deep, 35 % reported no bulk density and 74 % no coarse fragments. Ignoring coarse fragments overestimated stocks by 8 %; sampling only to 20 cm overestimated them by 14 % if extrapolated to 30 cm but underestimated them by 26 % if reported as the 0–30 cm stock. A typical study’s combined error had a median of approximately +10 % and a 90 % range of roughly −15 to +73 %. Post hoc correction of published data removed the bias but narrowed this range by only around 10 %, so field standardisation appears necessary; coarse fragments taken from soil maps did not reproduce measured values. Measuring coarse fragments was the most effective single fix, followed by sampling to 30 cm. Approximately 80 % of within-study management effects (median 22 %; 48 studies) fell inside the typical methodological range. For the woody perennial systems reviewed here, most reported management effects are of similar magnitude to the methodological uncertainty, whereas within-study contrasts are largely robust. Carbon-footprint studies (n = 16) were not comparable across boundaries and functional units. We give prioritised sampling and reporting guidance.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c6.title: Atmospheric rivers associated with daily global temperature spikes and dips
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c6.authors: Andrew David King, Kimberley Reid, Jonathan D Wille, Eduardo Alastrué de Asenjo
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c6.abstract: Year-to-year global mean temperature variability and its causes have been extensively studied, but day-to-day global temperature variability remains unexplored. Here, we examine daily global mean temperature spikes and dips and find that during austral winter they are typically associated with anomalous Antarctic temperatures. Large amounts of poleward moisture transport into Antarctica generally precedes daily global temperature spikes while dips are often preceded by a marked lack of poleward moisture transport around Antarctica. We find a comparable relationship when we look at Southern Hemisphere atmospheric rivers, relatively narrow bands of high moisture transport, ahead of global temperature spikes and dips. We examine these relationships over longer timescales and find that austral winters or years with greater moisture transport towards Antarctica tend to be hotter for the globe overall, but these relationships are much weaker than with daily GSAT. This work extends understanding of how weather affects global mean temperatures across timescales.
