https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c4.title: Declining soil organic matter as a dominant control on agricultural nitrogen loss
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c4.authors: Hariom Yadav, Gregg R. Sanford, Adam C. von Haden et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c4.abstract: Nitrogen (N) losses from agricultural soils that pollute water and air and threaten biodiversity are often assumed to result from excessive fertilizer and manure applications. Yet, soil organic matter is the largest pool of N in agricultural systems and its contribution to environmental N loss remains poorly quantified. We combined comprehensive field-specific data on external N inputs and crop N removal with soil N stock measurements from a 30-y experiment including six contrasting grain and forage cropping systems typical of the US Midwest. The N removal in harvested crops approximately balanced total N inputs in most grain and forage systems, suggesting relatively efficient use of N inputs. Nevertheless, soil N stocks declined over 30 y in most systems, such that N released during organic matter decomposition contributed disproportionately to environmental N losses. Despite receiving lower fertilizer input, cropping systems including soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] in rotation with maize (Zea mays L.) had significantly higher environmental N losses than the other grain and forage systems because they lost more N from soil organic matter. Our results suggest that effective management of N fertilizer and manure is necessary but insufficient to reduce environmental N loss from intensive agricultural systems, underscoring the importance of adopting agricultural practices that maintain or enhance soil organic matter, and policies that support them.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdf.title: Bioregionalization delineates distinct regimes of winter phytoplankton blooms in the Arabian Sea
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdf.authors: Adith V B, V. P. Akhil, Keerthi M G et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aebbdf.abstract: Winter phytoplankton blooms in the northern Arabian Sea (NAS) exhibit pronounced spatial variability in timing and magnitude. A bioregionalization based on K-means clustering of satellite-derived surface chlorophyll (SChl) delineates distinct winter bloom bioregions within the NAS and provides a framework for examining regional differences in bloom dynamics. The northern bioregions (B1 and B2) are characterized by high-SChl blooms peaking during February–March, with bloom initiation following the transition of net surface heat flux from negative to positive, coincident with the relaxation of winter convective cooling and the onset of surface warming and restratification. Interannual variability in bloom onset closely follows the timing of the net heat flux transition, while intraseasonal variability manifests as episodic bloom events associated with short-term reversals and relaxations in net heat flux. More than 70% of cooling-to-warming transitions are associated with positive SChl growth, while positive and negative SChl growth preferentially occur during weakening and intensification of surface cooling, respectively. The persistence of this relationship across interannual and intraseasonal timescales supports the applicability of the convection shutdown hypothesis to the NAS, extending its relevance beyond temperate and subpolar oceans. In contrast, the southern bioregion (B3) exhibits relatively weaker blooms during December–January and shows no consistent SChl response to transitions from surface cooling to warming. Instead, peak SChl concentrations occur during sustained winter cooling, consistent with an entrainment-driven bloom regime in which continued vertical mixing maintains nutrient supply to the euphotic zone. These findings provide a basis for assessing the sensitivity of NAS winter blooms to future changes in atmospheric forcing.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c7.title: Does channel pattern matter for SWOT river discharge?
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec3c7.abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite estimates river discharge from observed water surface elevation, width and slope. Its algorithms treat each river reach as a single effective channel. About 58% of the 58,790 alluvial reaches in a global channel-pattern dataset have multiple channels, yet it is not clear whether channel pattern affects the accuracy of SWOT discharge. SWOT discharge was evaluated for meandering, anabranching, braided and straight rivers at 12,906 reaches on six continents and at 81 gauges. A larger, overlapping set of 288 gauges served as a check. In braided rivers the six discharge algorithms disagreed most, and river width varied with stage two to four times more than in the other patterns. At the 81 gauges, anabranching and meandering rivers showed no detectable discharge bias (median SWOT/gauge 1.18× and 1.13×). Straight rivers were validated only in the larger set and also showed no detectable bias (1.04×, n = 19). Braided rivers were sampled mostly on sand-bed rivers of the U.S. Great Plains and were overestimated (median 1.87×, 95% CI 1.26–3.46×, n = 7). The larger set showed this too (2.18×, n = 13). With the product’s designated variable instead of the six-algorithm consensus, braided bias was 1.57× in the larger set but not detectable at the 81 gauges. SWOT also tracked flow changes worst in braided rivers (median within-station correlation 0.43, against 0.74–0.80). In every pattern, each gauge’s median SWOT discharge stayed close to the algorithms’ prior mean discharge. The prior was close to the long-term mean flow (0.82–1.07×). On most SWOT days, braided rivers carried far less than this mean, but braided SWOT discharge stayed close to it. SWOT discharge estimates are therefore not generally worse in multichannel rivers. Braided rivers are the exception. SWOT overestimates the low flows that dominate their records.

https://doi.org/10.1080/00038628.2026.27.title: Natural ventilation in school classrooms: a systematic review of ventilation strategies, research methods, and performance indicators
https://doi.org/10.1080/00038628.2026.27.authors: Maureen Trebilcock, Nelson Arias Jiménez, Karina Neira-Zambrano, David Escorcia-Ariza
https://doi.org/10.1080/00038628.2026.27.abstract: Natural ventilation is widely used in school classrooms, yet its performance depends on design, climate, occupancy, and operation. This systematic review examines ventilation strategies, methodological approaches, and performance indicators. Following PRISMA 2020, 36 peer-reviewed articles published up to August 2025 were selected from Web of Science and Scopus. Window-based strategies, including single-sided and cross ventilation, were most frequently investigated, while special systems received less attention. Simulation studies, field measurements, field experiments, and mixed-method provided complementary evidence. Methodological quality was generally moderate to high, with limitations varying by study design. Indoor air quality dominated performance assessment, particularly through CO2 concentration, ventilation rate, and air exchange rate, while thermal comfort, energy, and acoustics received less attention. Evidence was concentrated in European and temperate-climate contexts. Overall, natural ventilation performance is context-dependent, highlighting the need for integrated assessments of air renewal, thermal conditions, pollutants, and operation, alongside broader geographical and climatic representation.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150028.title: Each building tells a story: A New York City neighborhood on the cusp of densification
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150028.authors: Mara S. Sidney, Tamara Velásquez Leiferman, Joshua McWhirter
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150028.abstract: This study seeks to understand the business of densification through analysis of public policies, property records, and “the everyday” in a rapidly changing Manhattan neighborhood. Our case study of Inwood uses a new conceptual framework for urban policy analysis to bring multiple data sources together to examine four sites that show how key elements of New York City’s rezoning strategy intersects with other housing policies. Our findings speak to the challenges of maintaining affordable housing stock amid densification and the importance of including everyday experiences in policy analysis. We find that new densification policies interact with pre-existing policies to produce complex, contradictory outcomes. For example, de-densification coexists with densification. Second, although some manifestations of densification are visible, such as high-rise buildings, others are not, including tenant displacement and apartment warehousing. Finally, we find that policy implementation works as ad hoc policy making because actors seek policy changes through alternative channels after rezoning is formally adopted.

https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150375.title: The rubble and beyond: Expanding urbicide through affective geographies and the settler-colonial longue durée
https://doi.org/10.1177/0042098026150375.abstract: Urbicide scholarship has established, in varying ways, that ‘killing a city’ reaches beyond the material. Yet the concepts used to name this ‘reach’ do not describe the same object or make the same analytical claim. The question is therefore not only whether urbicide reaches beyond the material, but what a given conceptualisation allows us to understand about what destruction reaches. This article expands urbicide scholarship by theorising affect not as an additional dimension or effect of destruction, but as a capacity enabled by material and human–nonhuman relations through which violence can be reached. The argument is developed through a situated reading of contemporary urbicidal violence in Gaza (2023–ongoing), where recurrent military operations have compounded destruction while foreclosing reconstruction between them, within a longer settler-colonial history of displacement and enclosure. Drawing on Anderson’s account of morale and affective geographies literature, the article shows how destruction reaches the material and relational conditions through which affective capacities are constituted and exercised. It further proposes storytelling and counter-mapping as situated forms of evidence for tracing the reach of this destruction: memories, attachments, spatial knowledge and relations that conventional damage assessment cannot capture. Locating these processes within the settler-colonial longue durée expands the concept of urbicide showing how its reach is shaped by historically specific conditions of enclosure, cumulative destruction and the absence of a stable aftermath.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Pooled accuracy does not transfer: validating kinetic and machine-learning models of wetland ammonium removal for design and compliance
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Reza Moghaddam, Rupert J. Craggs, Sukhjit Singh, Chris C. Tanner
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Models of nitrogen removal guide the design and consenting of treatment wetlands, and machine-learning studies often report R 2 above 0.9. These usually come from random splits of pooled records, which test interpolation, not forecasting or transfer to new systems. At one treatment plant, we compared a first-order kinetic model and a Random Forest, given identical inputs, for effluent ammonium from three partially saturated vertical-flow wetland configurations (zeolite, gravel or woodchip upper layer; triplicate units; 16 dates in 2023). As dose volume rose from 2.75 to 11 mm and in-bed temperature fell from about 22 to 10°C, gravel and woodchip effluent ammonium rose 13- to 16-fold. In pooled random splits the Random Forest explained 63% of the variance when told each record's system, 16% when not. Forecasting later dates, the kinetic model with a dose term erred least of four model variants in every system, clearly for gravel (1.14 against 3.24 mg L −1 for the Random Forest), extrapolating to an unseen dose. Carrying the last observation forward matched or beat the Random Forest everywhere, and the kinetic model for woodchip. For a system left out of training, the kinetic model erred least of the four for gravel and woodchip; no model predicted the zeolite system better than a constant. Without dose, the fitted temperature coefficient (gravel and woodchip) rose from 0.99–1.02 to 1.07–1.08, crediting cold with an effect that came with the dose increase. Validation should match the decision a model supports, and operating variables belong in wetland models.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Groundwater quality response to voluntary farmer participation in nitrogen policies: Results from an integrated modeling approach
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Kaja Jurak, Andréas Musolff, Van Tam Nguyen et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Nitrogen (N) fertilizer use increases agricultural yields and income, but excessive application can lead to elevated N surplus, threatening biodiversity, water quality, and human health. Policies aiming to reduce N surplus must balance environmental objectives with farmers’ livelihoods. However, existing policies often underrepresent how farmers’ responses to policies translate into spatially heterogeneous groundwater quality outcomes. To address this gap, we develop an integrated modeling framework linking the ecological-economic model SNAg (Sustainable Nitrogen usage in Agriculture), parameterized with simulated yields from LPJmL (Lund-Potsdam-Jena managed Land), with the process-based water-quality model mQM. This is applied to wheat cultivation in Germany and 139 subcatchments of Rhine and Elbe to assess per-hectare subsidies for voluntarily reducing mineral N-inputs. Two subsidy-schemes are compared: a moderate policy with widespread (94% participation) but limited annual N-input reductions (to 146 kgN ha − 1 ) and a tighter policy with more concentrated (56% participation) but stronger reductions (to 104 kgN ha − 1 ). Relative to a no-policy-baseline, the share of catchments exceeding a nitrate-N concentration threshold of 12 mg l − 1 in 2030 decreases by 48% and 59% under the moderate and tight policy, respectively. Across scenarios, spatial heterogeneity in groundwater quality is explained more strongly by catchment characteristics and farmers’ participation than by hydroclimatic variability. Our results show that voluntary uniform input-based policies can themselves drive heterogeneous environmental outcomes, as identical policies translate into uneven reductions in N surplus and leaching across catchments. By explicitly representing the impact from farmers’ decisions to groundwater quality, the new modeling framework provides a consistent basis for evaluating and comparing N-policy designs.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Winter de-icing salt reduces pollutant removal capacity in bioretention systems, with implications for downstream water quality
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Bhabishya Khaniya, Jennifer A. P. Drake, Tim D. Fletcher, Christopher Szota
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Bioretention systems can effectively remove pollutants like nitrogen, phosphorus, heavy metals, and total suspended solids from stormwater runoff. However, winter road salt application in cold climates can potentially decrease pollutant removal. To understand the effects of winter salt-loading on springtime pollutant removal, we simulated a six-month winter and spring saline runoff dosing regime in a glasshouse, using bioretention mesocosms. Three plant species, with different levels of salt tolerance, as well as unvegetated (bare) mesocosms, were exposed to three saline runoff treatments: no-salt (control), medium-, and high-salt, with the latter two based on realistic de-icing salt concentrations and application frequencies. Pollutant removal decreased from no-salt to high-salt treatments, reducing removal of suspended solids from 88% to 46%, total nitrogen from 60% to -65%, total dissolved nitrogen from 78% to 15%, total phosphorus from 55% to -124%, filterable reactive phosphorus from -416% to -4575%, and heavy metals from 87% to 46%. Reduced performance was mainly associated with media destabilization, which mobilized fine particles and organic matter and increased export of particulate-bound pollutants. Even in the absence of salt, planted mesocosms showed only moderate pollutant removal benefits relative to bare. Increasing salt loads reduced plant growth and root development, further reducing pollutant removal relative to bare mesocosms. Results suggest nitrogen removal was likely linked to microbial nitrogen transformations, whereas phosphorus and metal removal were governed by filtration and sorption within the media. These findings demonstrate that winter road salt loading can severely impair springtime bioretention performance, amplifying downstream freshwater pollution risks, including eutrophication.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Sewage-sludge biochar for CO2 capture: Quantitative structure–performance relationships, contaminant trade-offs, and management pathways
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Petteri Peltola
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Sewage-sludge-derived biochar (SSBC) couples waste management with CO 2 capture, but its environmental value depends on more than maximum adsorption capacity. This quantitative critical review synthesizes 19 primary studies published during 2020–2026 and 195 directly reported or explicitly converted material/test observations, evaluating preparation route, texture, feedstock composition, adsorption conditions, cycling evidence, contaminant implications, and processing intensity. Best-case study maxima had route-level medians of 32.3 mg CO 2 /g for direct-pyrolysis chars, 94.8 mg CO 2 /g for conditioner-assisted materials, and 173.0 mg CO 2 /g for co-pyrolysis/co-carbonization followed by activation; within-study medians were substantially lower, showing that maxima represent an upper bound rather than typical performance. In the strict dry, pure-CO 2 , 25 °C, approximately 1-bar equilibrium subset, uptake was associated with BET surface area based on 39 observations from six studies (Pearson r = 0.80; Spearman ρ = 0.82) and with reported micropore volume in 38 observations from five studies ( r = 0.81; ρ = 0.85). At lower CO 2 partial pressures, CO 2 -accessible ultramicropores and surface chemistry were more discriminating than total BET area. Deployment-relevant evidence remains sparse but includes humid fixed-bed working-capacity measurements, 50-cycle temperature-vacuum swing adsorption testing, and simulated and on-site real-biogas experiments. Three studies directly paired CO 2 performance measurements with contaminant or leaching measurements. Overall, SSBC is best interpreted as a carbon–mineral–contaminant design space in which pore architecture, surface chemistry, process intensity, gas environment, and contaminant fate jointly determine application potential.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: Closing the Language Gap: Evaluating Earthquake Experiences and Warning Effectiveness in the County of San Diego
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.authors: M. R. Brudzinski, D. F. Sumy, Shelley E. Olds et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: Earthquake early warning (EEW) aims to reach individuals before strong shaking to enable protective actions such as ‘Drop, Cover, and Hold On’ (DCHO). Individuals who self-identify as limited English proficient (LEP) may not respond to alerts due to language barriers. The County of San Diego (CSD), California, serves a diverse community of over 3.3 million people that speaks varied languages. Collaborating with the National Opinion Research Center, we surveyed CSD residents about their earthquake experience, alert experience, and familiarity with the CSD Office of Emergency Services SD Emergency app. We offered surveys in six languages, yet received 860 responses in English only. However, ∼30% of respondents were from LEP households (over two-thirds self-identified as LEP) that were geographically and demographically different from English-proficient (EP) households. We found statistically similar responses from LEP and EP households across nearly all topical categories, demonstrating language is a surmountable barrier for CSD alerting. Although more EP respondents felt an earthquake (91% versus 84%), more LEP respondents received an earthquake alert (38% versus 27%). Only 3-4% of both groups reported DCHO in response to shaking, which increased to 7% when receiving an alert, highlighting the importance of earthquake alerts for protective action. LEP respondents downloaded the SD Emergency app more often (65% vs. 49% for EP), but deleted the app more often (19% vs. 9%). Our findings indicate CSD has been successful in enabling similar alert experiences for LEP communities, yet opportunities remain to promote DCHO and increase how many people receive EEW.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.journal: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction (IJDRR)
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: Risk Configurations and Disaster Risk Creation: Governance, Territory and Uneven Development in Chile
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: The concept of disaster risk governance (DRG) serves to highlight the importance of collective and coordinated action in disaster prevention. Although DRG has received growing scholarly attention, dominant approaches remain largely normative, focused on the design and capacity of institutions rather than the political processes that actively produce risks. This article addresses this gap in the literature by shifting the analytical focus from disaster risk reduction (DRR) to disaster risk creation (DRC), asking how governance configurations (i.e., historically situated combinations of discourses, actor coalitions, material processes and outcomes) produce and distribute risk differently across social groups and territories. We propose the concept of disaster risk governance configuration (DRGC), and along with discussions of uneven spatial development, we argue that disaster risk is not a residual outcome of failed governance but a structural product of the way in which territories are governed. We develop our argument through a comparative qualitative analysis of two cases in Chile: the Andean foothills of Santiago and the Cachapoal valley in the O'Higgins region. The comparison reveals four patterns that are common to both cases: the depoliticisation of disaster risks, the prioritisation of economic development over DRG practices, the strategic and selective implementation of risk initiatives, and ultimately, the privatisation of risk. Together, these patterns describe a mode of governance that produces fragmented resilience and reproduces disaster risk as a structural condition of uneven development.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec314.title: Contrasting occurrence of winter compound events across different vegetation types in dryland Asia
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec314.authors: Lin Zhao, Xiyan Xu, Zhenghua Hu et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec314.abstract: Winter compound events characterized by freezing temperatures and heavy snow have profound impacts on vulnerable dryland ecosystems. However, a quantitative evaluation of winter compound events among different vegetation types in dryland Asia remains lacking. In this study, we developed a composite winter compound event index that integrates temperature, snow depth and snow density to investigate the characteristics of the events across different vegetation types over the winter months (November—March) from 2001 to 2024. We show that the year with the widest spatial extent of winter compound events was 2013, affecting approximately 31.52% of the total area of dryland Asia, while the most intense events occurred in 2021. The largest share of cumulative affected area occurs in January, while the intensity peaks in March. Temperature makes the largest relative contribution to event intensity, however, its relative contribution declines in later winter months as the relative contributions of snow depth and snow density increase. Different combinations of contribution rates of temperature, snow depth and snow density shape the divergent event characteristics among vegetation types. The steppe is the major vegetation type across dryland Asia, which experiences the largest event affected area ratio (19.52%), and the highest event frequency (64.19%). Forest cover in dryland Asia is relatively low, but demonstrates the second-highest affected area ratio after steppe and the highest mean intensity of events. These results quantified the occurrence of winter compound events among various vegetation types in dryland Asia, highlighting their different exposure patterns in the dryland ecosystems.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec312.title: Attributing Projected Evapotranspiration and Runoff Changes to CO 2 Effect Pathways under Increasing Atmospheric CO 2 across Global Large River Basins
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec312.authors: Jialing Xu, Ran Lv, Shanlei Sun et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec312.abstract: Atmospheric CO2 affects terrestrial hydrology through radiative (RAD), vegetation physiological (BGC), and nonlinear interaction (INT) pathways, yet how these pathways drive future evapotranspiration (ET) and runoff (Q) remains poorly understood. We combine idealized CO2 factorial experiments from six CMIP6 Earth System Models with a Budyko-based water-balance framework to quantify pathway contributions to projected ET and Q changes across 38 major global river basins and identify their associated hydrological controlling factors. Projected ET and Q increase in most basins but exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity. RAD dominates ET changes in 30 basins, whereas Q changes are dominated by RAD, BGC, and INT in 23, 8, and 7 basins, respectively. In RAD-dominated basins, hydrological changes are primarily associated with hydroclimatic variables, particularly precipitation, whereas the Budyko parameter n, an integrated parameter representing processes not explicitly resolved by the prescribed hydroclimatic variables, is the leading controlling factor in BGC-dominated basins and some INT-dominated basins. These results show that future basin-scale hydrological responses to rising CO2 depend on both the dominant CO2 effect pathway and its associated hydrological regulation, providing a two-level perspective on future terrestrial water-cycle changes.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec313.title: Carbon and economic implications of promoting preventive care: A case study of Japan's community gathering place
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec313.authors: Narumi Kira, Kazushige Ide, Yosuke Shigetomi
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec313.abstract: This study examines the supply-chain greenhouse gas emissions (carbon footprint) and economic impacts of preventive care policies. As a case study, we focus on community gathering places named “kayoinoba”, where older residents meet at least once a week, for group exercise and social activities as a part of the national long-term care prevention system. While preventive care is widely recognized to suppress long-term care demand, the financial and environmental impacts remain unexplored. To address this knowledge gap, this study employs an environmental input-output analysis paired with detailed operational and expenditure data obtained through interviews with 102 local organizations across nine municipalities in Japan. By quantifying the carbon footprint from preventive care activities, this study sets future scenarios based on participation rates and the subsequent reduction in the need for lower level long-term care. Findings demonstrate that net economic costs between the promotion of community gathering places and reduction in the long-term care demand are expected to decrease, and this impact will intensify over time as the population ages (339 billion Japanese yen in 2050). In addition, without rebound effects on the carbon footprint resulting from behavioral changes among older adults who have become healthier due to preventive care measures, preventive care reduces net emission within the health care system by 2.97 gCO2eq/Japanese yen. Furthermore, the study found preventive measures’ impact varies by prefecture owing to differences in of older adult numbers and certified care needs rates. Additionally, we conducted scenario analysis group with the lowest cost or carbon footprint intensity. These results suggest that each municipality can reduce the carbon footprint intensity of the health system by emulating these groups’ activities. Incorporating environmental considerations into municipal preventive care offers a pathway to achieving sustainable health systems and climate change mitigation, that is, global planetary health priorities.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec311.title: Historical population exposure to temperature extremes in Peru: evidence for health adaptation in a changing climate
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec311.authors: Yasna K. Palmeiro-Silva, William Checkley, Kyle Steenland, Stella M. Hartinger
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec311.abstract: Temperature extremes are becoming more common and pose growing risks to population health. However, spatially resolved, population-weighted evaluations are scarce for Latin American countries. We sought to estimate population-weighted exposures across the geographically diverse regions of Peru. Eight health-relevant temperature extreme indices were computed at 0.1° × 0.1° resolution from daily ERA5-Land data for 2000-2025, using the 1961-1990 baseline for percentile thresholds. Grid-level values were combined with Global Human Settlement Layer population grids to estimate population-weighted averages, person-days of exposure, and the proportion of the national and region-specific population exposed to threshold exceedances. Temporal trends were assessed using Sen’s slope and the Mann-Kendall test, and hotspots were identified by combining hazard intensity and population density. All eight indices showed statistically significant warming trends at the national level. Population-weighted warming reached 0.42-0.56 °C per decade, with nighttime extremes increasing fastest. Between 2000-2009 and 2016-2025, warm days and warm nights more than doubled, whilst cold days and cold nights declined by approximately one third. The central highlands (Junín, Cusco, Apurímac) emerged as the fastest-warming region across indices, and coastal urban centres (Lima, Callao, Piura) accumulated the largest person-day burden of heat exposure. Peru is undergoing a rapid population-weighted intensification of temperature extremes, with regional heterogeneity but nationally coherent warming. These findings provide a spatially explicit baseline to inform health adaptation planning, early warning system development, and equity-focused prioritisation across departments.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec310.title: Post-wildfire soil respiration in tundra is driven by plant community composition and soil moisture in the late growing season
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec310.authors: Fernanda Santos, Amy L. Breen, Dedi Yang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec310.abstract: Arctic wildfires are expected to increase carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from soils underlain by permafrost. However, we lack in situ measurements of post-fire soil respiration and its drivers in the Arctic tundra. We measured soil properties and late-growing season CO2 fluxes in patches of unique plant functional types (PFT) across two years using a chronosequence approach in tundra recovering from repeated wildfires over the past five decades on the Seward Peninsula of Alaska. Soil respiration varied with fire age and number of times burned and was greatest in areas dominated by forbs, declining in areas dominated by shrubs and graminoids. After accounting for PFT, soil respiration also declined as soil moisture increased in already wet systems. Early-thaw season analyses suggested that increased permafrost thaw in burned areas was associated with a denser organic layer. Changes in water availability and plant species composition along post-fire successional trajectories may influence net soil CO2 emissions from Arctic tundra.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys..title: From street-level imagery to actionable mobility metrics: A deep learning framework for computing wheelchair accessibility from pedestrian sidewalk infrastructure features
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys..authors: Maciej Adamiak, Gefei Kong, Danielle Gatland et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys..abstract: Urban space is not equally accessible to all city inhabitants. For individuals with mobility disabilities, physically open spaces can remain functionally inaccessible, as inadequate sidewalk surfaces, excessive slopes, or insufficient clearance can turn a seemingly traversable area into an impassable one. Although the need to quantify these disparities is increasingly recognised, significant gaps persist in producing reliable, scalable, and actionable accessibility data. This study introduces a processing pipeline that leverages street-level imagery and deep learning techniques to estimate key characteristics of pedestrian sidewalk infrastructure — including sidewalk segmentation, surface type and condition detection, effective clearance estimation, and slope calculation — and synthesises them into an actionable dataset followed by a composite sidewalk wheelchair accessibility index (WHAI). The Wheelchair Accessibility Dataset (WHAD) pipeline combines monocular metric depth estimation, 3D point cloud reconstruction, and terrain model analysis to derive measurements from publicly available Mapillary street-level imagery. Results are validated against unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and aerial orthoimagery across areas of varying accessibility in Łódź, Poland, and Heidelberg, Germany. The resulting index enables the identification of localised inaccessible enclaves that conventional spatial analyses often overlook, providing an explainable and comparable foundation for evidence-based urban planning and improvements to pedestrian routing.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-026-04337.title: Analysis of the impact and ambition of the new NDCs for 2035: Paris climate goal is further out of reach
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-026-04337.authors: Michel G.J. den Elzen, Elena Hooijschuur, Ioannis Dafnomilis et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-026-04337.abstract: In 2025, almost 130 countries submitted new national climate plans, known as nationally determined contributions (NDCs), outlining mitigation targets for 2035. This study evaluates their impact on emissions for all countries and assesses their ambition levels, with a main focus on the G20 economies. Full implementation of unconditional and conditional NDCs would reduce projected median global greenhouse gas emissions in 2035 by approximately 7% and 11% respectively, compared to 2019 levels—still falling short of the reductions needed to align with below 2°C and 1.5°C pathways. Among the G20, four economies—Australia, the EU, Japan, and the United Kingdom—have set new NDC targets on a linear path to net-zero emissions. In contrast, Brazil, Canada, the Russian Federation, and South Africa have NDCs misaligned with their net-zero targets. For the remaining G20 economies that have yet to peak—China, Indonesia, Mexico, the Republic of Korea, and Türkiye—transitioning to net-zero emissions must occur within 15 to 35 years, a timeline significantly shorter than the 37 to over 60 years required by those that have already peaked, underscoring the urgency for rapid decarbonization after 2035. Lastly, the majority of G20 economies do not meet 2035 reduction targets derived from Paris-aligned equity-based effort-sharing approaches.

https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.title: Analysis of the impact and ambition of the new NDCs for 2035: Paris climate goal is further out of reach
https://link.springer.com/article/10.100.abstract: More than 130 countries have submitted new national climate plans, or nationally determined contributions (NDCs), outlining mitigation targets for 2035. This study evaluates the impact of these NDCs on global and national greenhouse gas emissions by quantifying the expected emission levels by 2035. For countries without new NDCs, targets for 2030 from previous NDCs or current policies projections were used. Additionally, the study assesses the ambition levels of the individual NDCs submitted by G20 economies against different criteria, such as comparing them to linear pathways to their net-zero targets, to cost-effective scenarios, and to pathways that include equity considerations. We find that full implementation of unconditional and conditional NDCs would reduce projected median global greenhouse gas emissions in 2035 by approximately 6% and 9% respectively, compared to 2015 levels. This is not sufficient to be in line with scenarios limiting end-of-century temperature increase to 2 °C and 1.5 °C. For G20 economies, eight of the fourteen new NDCs are in line with a linear emission pathway towards net-zero emissions, while the other six require rapid decarbonisation after 2035 to reach their net-zero target. In terms of cost-effective scenarios, eight new NDCs are within the range of below 2 °C pathways, with only the NDCs of EU and UK are with the 1.5 °C range. Lastly, most G20 economies do not meet 2035 reduction targets based on equity-based effort-sharing approaches, especially when compared to 1.5 °C pathways. This finding indicates that further ambition in climate mitigation is needed across countries, even when equity is taken into consideration.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.title: Digital resource taxonomy for integrating BIM and life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA)
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.authors: Teresa Aguilar-Planet, Alberto Picardo, Juan Francisco Fernández-Rodríguez, Estela Peralta
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2026.10.abstract: The integration of Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment (LCSA) within Building Information Modelling (BIM) environments enables automated data exchange and processing to assess environmental, economic, and social impacts throughout the construction life cycle. However, full automation remains limited by interoperability challenges, fragmented digital resources, and user intervention. This study systematically reviews the technological development of BIM–LCSA integration following PRISMA. A total of 99 publications (2014 to 2025) were analysed according to automation level, interoperability strategy, sustainability dimension, and digital resources. Results reveal a transition from manual and semi-automated procedures towards interoperability-based workflows and advanced computational approaches, including semantic technologies, artificial intelligence, data-driven methods, digital twins, and IoT monitoring. A hierarchical taxonomy is proposed to classify these resources by purpose, automation level, and sustainability dimension. It supports workflow selection and identifies technological gaps in automation and interoperability, highlighting priorities for advancing integrated environmental, social, and economic life cycle assessment within BIM environments.

https://doi.org/10.1080/00038628.2026.27.title: A latitudinal study of insolation on geometric forms
https://doi.org/10.1080/00038628.2026.27.abstract: The estimation of the solar load on a building envelope before its geometry is fixed is still a practical issue to be resolved. This paper presents a validated design formula that yields the envelope-to-horizontal irradiation ratio from only two inputs – the base-to-surface ratio B/F of the form and the site latitude: m = u(φ)·(B/F − 1) + 1, with u(φ) = 0.683 − 0.00556·φ. The Form Insolation Index m expresses the mean envelope irradiation G as a fraction of the horizontal irradiation G0. The validation at 22 additional locations on four continents showed a mean absolute relative error of 3.5%; the quadratic u(φ) fit reduces same-latitude errors to 1.2%. The underlying linear m-B/F relationship is confirmed across 92 convex form variants at nine locations from 6°N to 64°N using PVGIS v5.3 satellite-derived radiation data (R2 = 0.955–0.990). Given that any building can fit within a minimum convex hull, the formula also sets an upper limit to the solar energy entering any non-convex geometry that the hull encloses.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02490.title: Seeking coolness and shelter: behavioural responses of a large ungulate to severe weather conditions
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02490.authors: Adeline Bonaglia, Pia Anderwald, Stefanie Gubler et al.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-026-02490.abstract: Abstract Context Alpine ecosystems are highly vulnerable to climate change, with rising temperatures and altered precipitation posing increasing challenges to cold-adapted mountain ungulates. How these species adjust their behaviour to cope with short-term adverse weather conditions remains poorly understood. Objectives We investigated how summer weather shapes habitat selection and movement of Alpine ibex ( Capra ibex ), with a focus on thermoregulatory behaviour and shelter seeking. Methods We conducted integrated step selection analysis (iSSA) using high-resolution GPS data from 21 adult ibex in the Swiss National Park to link individual movements and habitat selection to meteorological (temperature, precipitation) and topographic variables. Results Alpine ibex showed clear weather-dependent behavioural responses. Diel vertical movements resulted in an overall selection for higher elevations during warm temperatures. Moreover, ibex selected for more rugged terrain, shaded areas, and less productive habitats to evade the heat. Longer step length suggested a temperature-dependent increase in movement distances. Therefore, at short-temporal scales, ibex appear to rely more on microhabitats, rather than on performing large-scale altitudinal shifts for thermoregulation. Precipitation resulted in downward movements, with ibex increasingly selecting steeper but less rugged terrain as precipitation intensity increased. Overall, our findings suggest that ibex rely on landscape heterogeneity to cope with contrasting weather conditions. Furthermore, behavioural adjustments to severe weather conditions may lead to a trade-off between thermoregulation and foraging opportunities. Conclusions Alpine ibex rely on behavioural plasticity to cope with severe short-term weather conditions. Maintaining landscape heterogeneity and altitudinal connectivity will thus be essential to ensure ibex persistence under climate change.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Why Indonesia captures limited value from cottonii - linking quality incentives, processing and environmental management
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Sudhir Yadav, Wellem Anselmus Teniwut, Cresha Gracy Nadar et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Indonesia is a major supplier of cottonii, used here for cultivated Kappaphycus alvarezii, yet much is exported as raw dried seaweed. This narrative review integrates evidence on market structure, quality incentives, regulatory requirements, processing economics and environmental burdens to identify conditions for greater domestic value capture. Trade data indicate concentrated market exposure, with China receiving 85.9% of Indonesia's seaweed and other algae export volume during 2022-2024. Procurement studies show that better handling does not consistently attract higher prices, while payment terms, credit and transport services shape suppliers' net returns. Processing viability depends on reliable feedstock, buyer-accepted output and achievable utilisation, with extraction gains sometimes accompanied by lower functional quality. Water, chemical and energy requirements make environmental management integral to investment appraisal, but incomplete plant balances and inconsistent boundaries limit comparisons among upgrading routes. Laboratory studies demonstrate ethanol production from selected carrageenan residues without establishing commercial viability or environmental benefits for industrial filter cake. We propose a staged roadmap linking quality measurement and transparent payment rules with product qualification, working capital, testing and wastewater management. Residue conversion warrants investment only where characterised streams, measured recovery and credible demand support an advantage over current handling and alternative uses. Evaluation should distinguish supplier returns, processing profitability and environmental outcomes, while tracking how costs and benefits are distributed. Linking transaction records with plant-level material and energy balances would make these conditions testable and strengthen investment and policy decisions.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Coastal protection and restoration with stabilised large driftwood: What we do (and do not) understand
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Alice J. Twomey, Oliver Lojek, Enda Murphy, Nils Goseberg
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Stabilised large driftwood (woody debris fixed in place with anchors, ballast or burial) is increasingly promoted as a nature-based alternative to hard coastal defences, offering erosion protection alongside co-benefits including sediment trapping, dune rebuilding and habitat provision. Yet this promotion has outpaced the evidence, raising the question of what design and implementation principles can guide effective use of stabilised driftwood as a nature-based solution (NbS) for coastal protection and restoration. We systematically review the global evidence base, synthesising experimental, field and observational studies to evaluate its design, implementation and performance. We identify 45 documented installations worldwide, predominantly North America, with single examples in South America and Australia, underpinned by two flume experiments and two field investigations. Cross-shore placement relative to the still water level is a key control on performance; wave attenuation, though widely assumed, has not been directly measured; and scour from buoyancy-driven log movement is a recurring, mechanistically explainable failure mode. Outcomes are sensitive to beach-sediment characteristics and wave-energy regime, so no single design generalises across sites. While the evidence base remains too sparse and narrow for validated design criteria, findings suggest genuine potential for stabilised driftwood as a coastal protection tool, pending research targeting these process-level uncertainties. Notably, because driftwood naturally stabilises in the backshore rather than the foreshore where deployed, burial may outperform anchoring by bypassing the mobilisation problem and inserting the log further along the wave-sediment-wood feedback loop. These findings provide a foundation for guidance to improve stabilised driftwood's reliability and uptake as a coastal NbS.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Impacts of traditional and industrial approaches to oil palm cultivation on bird biodiversity and conservation in a West African rainforest landscape
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Joris H. Wiethase, Andrew N. Gweh, Cicely A. M. Marshall et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Agricultural expansion threatens tropical ecosystems worldwide. Oil palm is cultivated primarily in Southeast Asia, but production in West Africa (its native range) is increasing rapidly. Here, oil palm is cultivated under traditional and industrial management, and the impacts on native West African ecosystems are poorly understood. Working within the framework of the Sustainable Oil Palm in West Africa (SOPWA) Project in Sinoe County, Liberia, we derived bird occurrence data using point count surveys across 54 plots in January-February 2023, spanning rainforest ('forest'), traditionally managed oil palm ('country palm'), and industrial oil palm systems, to investigate differences in bird species richness, community composition and community-level trait associations. Forest and country palm had comparable species richness, which was significantly higher than industrial oil palm. Taxonomic community composition differed across systems, with assemblages in country palm representing a mix of those in forest and industrial oil palm. Further, communities in forest and country palm were more associated with foraging in high strata, ant-associated behaviour, and an invertebrate diet. We detected four species of conservation concern in all systems, showing no consistent collective response to any specific system. Our findings show that country palm offers a promising option to preserve relatively high biodiversity as well as traditional cultivation practices in Liberia's managed landscape, although country palm is likely less productive than industrial oil palm. Oil palm systems are no replacement for rainforest ecosystems, and protection and designation of reserves and remnant forest patches are critical for wider bird conservation across West Africa.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Sulfate reduction controlled by microbial community structure and solid substrate at low temperatures in woodchip-based bioreactors
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Laura Nina Bettoni, Maria Hellman, Ekaterina Sokolova et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Microbial sulfate reduction is a promising approach for treating sulfate-rich mining water; however, low temperatures in subarctic regions remain a challenge. This study evaluated sulfate removal in laboratory-scale column bioreactors packed with woodchips, woodchips with biochar, and woodchips with potato peels, at 5 °C and 15 °C and supplemented with lactate and macronutrients. Average sulfate removal rates ranged from −4 to 61 mg SO 4 2- –S/L/d, depending on temperature, solid substrate, and supplemented electron donor supply. Lactate and nutrient additions enhanced sulfate reduction, although elevated total organic carbon (TOC) concentrations were detected in the effluent. Elevated TOC concentrations in the potato peel columns indicated ongoing hydrolysis and fermentation, particularly at higher temperatures. The highest sulfate removal efficiencies were observed in biochar reactors at 15 °C (up to ∼100 %) and in potato peel reactors at 5 °C (up to 53 %). Characterization of the microbial community by 16S rRNA gene-based sequencing revealed changes in community composition across experimental stages. Sulfate removal aligned with the enrichment of sulfate-reducing bacteria, with Desulfovibrionia being the dominant class. The results show that temperature-dependent performance can be mitigated through substrate selection and supplementation. At low temperatures, readily degradable substrates such as potato peels are advantageous, whereas biochar-amended systems perform best under heated conditions. Shifts in community composition further indicate that process performance is not limited by slow microbial turnover but can respond dynamically to operational changes. Finally, the calculated sulfate removal rates provide a basis for sizing full-scale bioreactors for sulfate removal at low temperatures.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Exploring Canadian beef farmers’ perceptions of participation in climate change mitigation: Insights from Prince Edward Island
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Maggie McCormick, Ataharul Chowdhury, Nasir Abbas Khan
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Beef farmers can play a significant role in reducing and sequestering greenhouse gas emissions through specific farm management practices. Understanding how farmers perceive this role is essential for effective knowledge exchange and communication strategies that promote climate change mitigation. This study investigates how beef farmers in Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada, perceive their involvement in farm-level mitigation efforts. Using identity theory as a framework, the study conducted a framing analysis to examine how participating farmers communicated their actions through four identity lenses: productivist, conservationist, hero, and scientist. Through purposive sampling, nine in-depth interviews were conducted with PEI beef farmers actively engaged in mitigative practices. Findings reveal that farmers often drew on multiple identities, with the productivist frame emerging most prominently. To foster broader engagement in climate mitigation, communication strategies should reflect the range of identities farmers associate with. Future research should explore perceptions among those not currently participating in mitigative practices.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Is the river clean? Comparison between public perceptions and water quality monitoring reveals divergences in the understanding of pollution sources in Arequipa, Peru
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Rémi Germain, Gary Vanzin, Aaron Malone et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Public perceptions of water quality are crucial in shaping water-related behaviors and management decisions that influence water conditions. Yet these perceptions, formed through social, cultural, and environmental experiences, do not always align with scientific assessments of water quality. This study combines a face-to-face survey of 692 adult residents of Arequipa, Peru, conducted in 2022, with an analysis of river water quality data from the prior decade to examine the congruence between perceived and measured water quality in the city's largest water body, the Chili River. Results indicate that residents correctly perceived the river as polluted but misidentified the main source of pollution, with the majority focusing on mining and litter. Analysis of longitudinal and temporal water quality profiles indicates degradation during urban and peri-urban transit, with signatures consistent with untreated sewage discharges and urban/agricultural runoff, but limited mining influence. Supporting this interpretation, the 2016 commissioning of the La Enlozada wastewater treatment plant, which intercepts municipal wastewater before it reaches the river, was associated with improved water quality downstream of the interceptors, while upstream conditions deteriorated. Despite these improvements, thermotolerant coliform levels generally remained above regulatory standards throughout the urban area and downstream. The pollution sources emphasized by the public, whether visible or assumed, explain only part of the contamination measured in this watershed. This discrepancy could hinder environmental progress and highlights the need to address gaps between public perceptions and measured conditions by improving environmental communication, ensuring data quality and transparency, and encouraging community involvement in watershed management.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Integrating the marine domain into the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem nexus: A data-driven framework for Mediterranean environmental management
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Jerome El Jeitany, Alexandra E. Spyropoulou, Enrica Caporali
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is a vital socio-ecological system where the “Blue Economy” is increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures and climate-driven variability. While the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem (WEFE) nexus has emerged as a key framework for sustainable resource management, the marine environment remains a significant “blind spot” in integrated assessments. This study introduces a quantitative “WEFEM” (Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem-Marine) framework that explicitly incorporates the marine domain as an active driver of the nexus. Using multi-decadal Earth Observation data from the Copernicus Marine Service covering the period [2000-2024] at a 1 km grid resolution, a lead-lag correlation and Vector Autoregressive modeling is employed to unravel the complex, time-lagged interactions between physical, biological, and biogeochemical indicators. Findings reveal that Mediterranean environmental interlinkages are governed by dynamic cascades rather than static associations, with pairwise correlations ranging between absolute values of 0.21 and 0.38. A critical “Thermal-Biogeochemical-Biological” cascade is observed: while sea surface warming immediately impacts carbon regulation through acidification and increased pressurized CO 2 (r = 0.37), there is a 3-to-4-month delay before thermal stratification suppresses biological productivity by starving the surface of nutrients(r = −0.32). Furthermore, we provide evidence of bidirectional coupling, where phytoplankton blooms can actively modulate the physical environment by influencing surface temperature and mixing depths. These results demonstrate that the marine domain is not merely a geographic backdrop but a primary engine of the nexus. By quantifying these spatiotemporal responses, this study provides a predictive window for resource managers and supports the integration of nexus-based indicators into regional policy frameworks such as the Marine Strategy Framework Directive and Maritime Spatial Planning.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Beyond single-stage classification: A hybrid AI–expert validation framework for environmental monitoring of European food waste prevention
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Wilmer Garzón, Manuel Amador Cervera, Haizea Cruz Elejalde, Ainhoa Alonso‐Vicario
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: European food loss and waste prevention records are reported through heterogeneous sources and formats, limiting their comparability and reuse for environmental monitoring. We developed a hybrid Zero-Shot Learning and Human-in-the-Loop framework to transform these records into a traceable, multidimensional corpus while retaining expert oversight. The workflow integrated 1164 Action Tracker records with 161 expert-curated records. 1324 records were retained after one semantically insufficient entry was excluded. A confidence-based routing step sent 331 Action Tracker records to full expert review, while a separate blind audit examined 125 of 832 higher-confidence records. Expert review showed that classification confidence and eligibility as a discrete prevention action are distinct quality dimensions. On 75 qualifying audit records, model-expert agreement remained limited, supporting automated inference as a first-pass routing tool rather than a substitute for expert assessment. The resulting taxonomy also showed that 512 of 1163 classified Action Tracker records (44.0%) were assigned to two or more food supply chain stages. These are model-assigned labels rather than verified proportions of qualifying interventions, but they retain cross-stage information that a strictly single-stage representation would omit. The framework does not estimate environmental impacts directly. Instead, it structures heterogeneous prevention evidence so that intervention characteristics, data gaps, and cross-stage coverage are explicit before subsequent linkage to activity data, life-cycle inventories, and policy assessment.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Partitioning and retention of PFAS in a Salix-planted constructed wetland treating foam-fractionated leachate and groundwater
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Oscar Liljeström, Dahn Rosenquist, Dan Berggren Kleja et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent and mobile contaminants frequently detected in landfill leachate and leachate-impacted groundwater, posing risks to environmental and human health. In this study, a pilot-scale (147 m 2 ) subsurface flow constructed wetland (CW), planted with Salix sp. in a peat–biochar substrate, was evaluated as a post-foam fractionation treatment step. Over 176 days, 72.9 m 3 of PFAS-contaminated water was treated. The CW reduced the water volume by 48% via evapotranspiration (2.11 L m −2 d −1 ), but PFAS concentrations did not decrease significantly between influent and effluent. In contrast, a mass balance indicated that 51% (50.7 mg) of the influent PFAS mass was retained within the system. The PFAS retention was primarily associated with the evapotranspiration-driven volume reduction and sorption to the filter substrate, particularly for long-chain PFAS. Short-chain PFAS were retained to a lower extent by the substrate but preferentially accumulated in Salix biomass. Plant uptake accounted for 6.9% of total retained PFAS, with 82–84% of accumulated PFAS located in leaves. No evidence of retranslocation during senescence was observed, indicating potential remobilization via leaf litter unless biomass is managed. The estimated phytoextraction potential of the system for PFAS ranged from 77 to 230 mg ha −1 yr −1 , dominated by short-chain compounds. Overall, this CW configuration reduced PFAS mass load rather than aqueous concentrations, suggesting limited suitability as a polishing step. The CW technology could instead be useful as a pre-treatment step prior to advanced treatment, in order to reduce both water volume and contaminant load.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.title: Thermophilic intensification governs abiotic fragmentation and microbiome restructuring during anaerobic co-digestion of bioplastics with OFMSW and waste activated sludge
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.authors: Altea Pedullà, Jelena Pavlović, Mariastella Ferreri et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvman.2026.1.abstract: Anaerobic co-digestion (Co-AD) of the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW) and waste-activated sludge (WAS) is a promising strategy for waste valorisation and renewable energy recovery; however, the increasing presence of compostable bioplastics in organic waste streams raises concerns regarding their degradation behaviour and impact on anaerobic digestion (AD) performance. In this study, semi-continuous mesophilic-to-thermophilic Co-AD of OFMSW and WAS containing Mater-Bi, crystallised polylactic acid (CPLA), and polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) was investigated under progressively intensified operating conditions, with and without graphite supplementation. Reactor performance was monitored through methane production, volatile fatty acids (VFAs), pH, and FOS/TAC ratio, while complementary abiotic assays and ATR-FTIR analyses were used to assess physicochemical polymer transformation in the absence and presence of microbial activity. Long-read metagenomics was further applied to evaluate microbial community restructuring during thermophilic operation. Thermophilic intensification strongly affected polymer transformation pathways and microbial composition. Among the tested materials, CPLA showed the highest abiotic solubilisation at 55 °C, reaching 1280 mg COD L −1 and exhibiting clear fragmentation under thermophilic conditions. In contrast, P(3HB-co-4HB) showed limited solubilisation and structural transformation. Graphite supplementation produced limited and condition-dependent effects on reactor performance. Metagenomic analysis revealed a marked transition from mesophilic Bacillota-dominated communities toward thermophilic enrichment of Patescibacteria, Thermotogota, and syntrophy-associated Pseudomonadota taxa. Overall, thermophilic intensification was associated with material-specific physicochemical transformation and marked microbial community restructuring, highlighting parallel responses of bioplastics and the anaerobic microbiome to changing operating conditions.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: From Accessibility Gaps to Shelter Allocation: A Huff-Enhanced 2SFCA and Equity-Informed Framework for Indoor Emergency Shelters in Coastal Cities
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.authors: Qiuyan Lü, Lin Wang, Kangjie Yang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: Indoor emergency shelters are critical for urban disaster risk reduction, yet their spatial distribution and service capacity may not match population demand in high-density coastal cities. This study develops an integrated evaluation–optimization framework using Shenzhen and Zhuhai as comparative cases. Based on ASPECT population data, official shelter inventories, and Amap API-estimated walking-time origin–destination data, hexagonal grids were used as analytical units. Huff-E2SFCA was applied as the primary accessibility model, with G2SFCA used for comparison. Service pressure, Gini and Theil indices, and bivariate Moran’s I were used to assess supply–demand pressure, equity, and population–supply association, while LP/MILP models were used for population allocation and candidate-shelter augmentation. Shenzhen has better walking-time coverage but widespread service pressure and persistent aggregate-capacity shortages, whereas Zhuhai has sufficient nominal capacity but weaker effective spatial connections between shelter supply and population demand and more localized mismatches. Evacuation-time inequality is greater in Zhuhai, while accessibility inequality is greater in Shenzhen. Optimization shows that Zhuhai gains most accommodation improvement early and then approaches a plateau, whereas Shenzhen remains constrained after extensive additions. These contrasting patterns suggest that indoor shelter systems may be limited by different combinations of aggregate capacity and spatial reachability, and the observed differences may also be associated with differences in urbanization level, population concentration, and urban spatial structure. The proposed framework provides a transferable basis for identifying dominant shelter-system bottlenecks and supporting differentiated indoor emergency shelter planning in coastal cities.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.title: Chronic Disease Management Following Hurricane Helene in East Tennessee
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.authors: Kimberly Michelle Kelly, Michelle Y. Martin, Charleen McNeill et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106.abstract: Disaster planning is a key factor for healthcare provision. Hurricane Helene in October 2024 was a devastating disaster, exacerbated by infrastructure challenges and the geography of eastern Tennessee in the US. The purpose of our study was to understand the roles of healthcare providers (advanced practice nurses (APNs), community pharmacists (CPs), and primary care physicians (PCPs) during a disaster in management of chronic disease. Further, we sought to understand differences as a function of metro status/rurality. This retrospective, cross-sectional study used a mixed methods design to collect survey data from 169 APNs, CPs, and PCPs. Providers were more likely to report having a disaster plan in place after Hurricane Helene. Those serving both metro and non-metro counties perceived the highest negative impact on patient health and chronic disease management, compared to those in only metro or only non-metro counties. Factor analysis identified two roles sub-scales: Operations and Management and Evaluation and Treatment. MANOVAs indicated that Operations and Management roles were higher for CPs, while Evaluation and Treatment were lower for CPs. Patients had challenges with basic needs, such as access to clean water, transportation, and communication. Patients also experienced health care access issues, including prescription drug shortages and cancelled appointments. Resources included local volunteers, technology (drones, satellite internet, telehealth), and external organizations. Our project helped to elucidate how APNs, CPs, and PCPs navigated the extensive flooding and infrastructure damage of Hurricane Helene, including the barriers encountered and resources identified.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ad2d3c.title: Vertical characteristics of HCHO and NO 2 in suburban Shanghai: understanding of ozone formation sensitivity via secondary HCHO
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ad2d3c.authors: Aimon Tanvir, Zeeshan Javed, Shanshan Wang et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ad2d3c.abstract: Since ozone (O 3 ) pollution in China is on the rise, vertical distribution of nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) and formaldehyde (HCHO) and their role towards O 3 formation are critical towards designing O 3 control strategies. Seasonal characteristics of aerosols, HCHO and NO 2 were investigated over suburban Shanghai using multi-axis differential optical absorption spectroscopy from June 2020 to May 2021. For HCHO, the highest average vertical mixing ratios (VMRs) were observed for summer (0.775 ppb), followed by autumn (0.719 ppb), spring (0.718 ppb) and winter (0.672 ppb) at ground level. Seasonal trends in NO 2 VMRs were observed to be opposite to that of HCHO with peak values occurring during winter (2.212 ppb) at the ground level followed by autumn (1.881 ppb), spring (1.415 ppb) and summer (1.124 ppb). In vertical, aerosols depicted a Gaussian shape with a higher values between 0.2–0.5 km. An exponential decay in NO 2 VMRs is observed from 0.0 km to 3.0 km while the integral component of HCHO was found to be concentrated up to 2.0 km particularly during summer months. The vertical distribution of NO 2 in different seasons mainly appeared below 0.5 km, while that of HCHO appeared within the range of 0.2–1.0 km. Both aerosols and NO 2 tend to be higher during haze days compared to non-haze days while HCHO was found to be higher during non-haze days owing to high photochemical activity on a clear day. Based on the ratio of HCHO to NO 2 (RFN), this study attempted to quantify the vertical characteristics of O 3 sensitivity for different seasons. The results indicated that the O 3 sensitivity was VOC-limited both at lower (generally, 0.0–0.6 km) and higher heights (1.8–3.0 km) while some transition limited scenarios were found at middle height (0.7–1.7 km) particularly during daytime. The results depicted that secondary HCHO is a crucial factor controlling on O 3 sensitivity over Shanghai where enhanced ratio of VOC limited regime was observed with secondary HCHO for all the seasons.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec282.title: Within-fire estimates of biomass loss across national forests of the US West Coast: inventory-informed inference with uncertainty
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec282.authors: Elliot S. Shannon, Andrew O. Finley, Paul B. May et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec282.abstract: Wildfire is reshaping forests in the western United States (US), yet estimates of wildfire impacts often rely on burned-area summaries or satellite-derived severity metrics that do not directly quantify changes in forest biomass or their uncertainty. We combine US Forest Inventory and Analysis plot measurements with annual 30 m tree canopy cover data in a Bayesian spatio-temporal modeling framework to estimate within-fire changes in live aboveground biomass (AGB) and forest mortality area across National Forest System lands in Washington, Oregon, and California. The model represents both live forest presence or absence and AGB conditional on live forest, allowing posterior predictive estimates of pre- and post-fire conditions at the pixel scale. Applied to 6,308 fire analysis areas from 2000 to 2022, the analysis estimates 117.8 million Mg of wildfire-associated AGB loss and 2.98 million ha of forest mortality area, with the largest aggregate impacts occurring in 2020. Pixel-level estimates reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity within fire perimeters, including large differences between total burned area, forest mortality area, and associated biomass loss. This inventory-informed, uncertainty-aware approach provides a scalable framework for quantifying forest carbon impacts of disturbance across broad regions while retaining within-fire spatial detail.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec281.title: Enhanced coupling between the North Atlantic oscillation and Pacific-North American patterns in a warmer climate
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec281.authors: Qi Tian, Hyacinth C. Nnamchi, Jianping Li et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec281.abstract: The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) and Pacific-North American (PNA) patterns are the most prominent atmospheric teleconnections over the Northern Hemisphere, which are traditionally considered independent of each other. Here we use reanalysis and state-of-the-art climate models to show the emergence of unprecedented coupling between the NAO and PNA in recent decades. This enhanced coupling primarily arises from non-uniform global warming associated with Arctic amplification, which weakens the meridional temperature gradient between the tropics and Arctic. The consequent poleward shift of the midlatitude westerlies displaces PNA’s downstream centers eastward into the North Atlantic region associated with the NAO. Future projections indicate that the NAO-PNA coupling will further strengthen under elevated anthropogenic forcing. These findings reveal a critical impact of climate change on atmospheric teleconnections, reshaping our understanding of the NAO-PNA relationship and its influence on Northern Hemisphere weather extremes.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec27f.title: Strategic cropland retirement can achieve groundwater sustainability and biodiversity co-benefits while minimizing economic impacts under climate change
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec27f.authors: Maxwell Pepperdine, Stella Wing, Harry Scott Butterfield et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec27f.abstract: Groundwater overdraft and climate change are driving large-scale agricultural land retirement across the world’s water-stressed farming regions, but the hydrologic, ecological, and economic outcomes of retirement depend heavily on where it occurs. Using the San Joaquin Valley, California, as a case study, we identify least-cost spatial configurations of cropland retirement that simultaneously meet groundwater and species habitat goals. We constructed species distribution models, estimated field-level applied water and foregone agricultural revenue, and used mixed-integer linear programming (prioritizr) to solve water-only, habitat-only, and combined (water + habitat) retirement optimizations for present and future scenarios, solving the water-only framework at both regional and individual groundwater basin scales. Our results show that meeting regional overdraft reduction targets required retiring roughly 326,000 ha of cropland at approximately $1.44B in foregone revenue under baseline conditions, rising to about 367,000 ha ($1.60B) under a high-emissions scenario. Regional planning met targets at approximately 4.6% less area and 18.5% lower cost than basin-by-basin planning, revealing a trade-off between regional efficiency and local feasibility in achieving long-term groundwater sustainability. The land needed to meet overdraft reduction goals contained far more suitable habitat than the conservation targets required (170–1298% of each target), indicating significant potential for habitat co-benefits when water-driven retirement was spatially coordinated. Our results do not suggest the retirement configurations as a prescriptive design, but rather as a demonstration of a generalizable spatial planning framework for identifying portfolios that balance irrigation reductions with conservation co-benefits and economic efficiency under climate uncertainty.

https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec280.title: Antecedent drought exposure weakens vegetation decline without promoting recovery
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec280.authors: Shijun Zheng, Le Yu, Zhenrong Du et al.
https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aec280.abstract: Repeated drought can alter vegetation responses to subsequent water stress, but whether reduced canopy decline is accompanied by improved recovery remains unresolved. We analysed global leaf area index and meteorological drought records for 1982–2020 using an event-based framework that separately quantified detectable declines in canopy leaf area, standardized leaf-area losses and recovery to pre-drought conditions. Antecedent drought frequency and cumulative severity were evaluated over five historical windows spanning 12–60 months, alongside the interval since the previous drought. After adjustment for current-drought characteristics and environmental conditions, greater antecedent frequency and severity were associated with lower odds of a clear negative LAI response and smaller losses across all five windows. In contrast, associations with recovery were weak and inconsistent across exposure windows. For the 60-month frequency measure, adjusted predictions from zero to six prior events indicated decreases of 3.7 percentage points in response probability and 0.15 standard deviations in leaf-area loss, while modelled recovery probability within 24 months decreased by only 0.8 percentage points. Associations differed among vegetation groups and forest types, with smaller losses accompanying either faster or slower recovery. Baseline adjustment and recovery sensitivity analyses broadly supported this separation between decline and recovery. These modest observational associations do not establish adaptation or a specific ecological memory mechanism. They show that muted canopy decline alone is insufficient evidence of improved drought resilience and support evaluating impact and recovery separately when assessing vegetation responses to recurrent drought.
